rows.source: Adarí Ìgbìmọ Ìjọba ti Masidóníà Zoran Zaev, aya rẹ̀ Zorica àti ọmọdékùnrin rẹ̀ Dushko fi ìwé àmútẹ̀kasí láti dìbò wọn sílẹ̀ fún ìbò oníbẹ́ẹ̀ni-bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ní Masidónía lori yíyí orúkọ orilẹ-ede náà pada eyiti yóò sí ọ̀nà fún un láti darapọ mọ àjọ NATO àti Ẹgbẹ́ Àwọn Orilẹ'ede Yuroopu ní ìlú Strumica, lorilẹ-ede Masidóníà ni ọgbọ̀nọ́jọ́ oṣù Owewe ĺọ̀dún 2018.
rows.output: The President of the Republic of Macedonia Zoran Zaev, his wife Zorica, and his son Dushko submitted their resignations to participate in the early parliamentary elections in Macedonia, which will lead to the country's name change that will allow it to join NATO and the European Union in the city of Strumica, in the Republic of Macedonia on 30 September 2018.
rows.reference: Macedonia's PM Zoran Zaev, his wife Zorica and his son Dushko cast their ballot for the referendum in Macedonia on changing the country's name that would open the way for it to join NATO and the European Union in Strumica, Macedonia September 30, 2018.

rows.source: Níwájú ilé ìgbìmọ̀ àwọn aṣoju-ṣòfin ní ìlú Skopje, Vlamirir Kavardarkov, ẹni ọdún mẹ́rìnléláàádọ́ta, ńgba ìtàgé kékeré kan láradì tí ó sì fa àwọn àga tówà niwaju àwọn àgọ́ tí àwọn ti yóò dẹ́yẹ sí ìbò oníbẹ́ẹ̀ni-bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ náà ṣàtòpọ̀ wọn sókè.
rows.output: In the front of the parliament building in Skopje, Vlamir Kavardarov, a 45-year-old man, is holding a small sign and shouting at the crowd of supporters of the opposition party.
rows.reference: In front of parliament in Skopje, Vladimir Kavardarkov, 54, was preparing a small stage and pulling up chairs in front of tents set up by those who will boycott the referendum.

rows.source: ''Àwa wà fún àjọ NATO àti EU, ṣugbọn a fẹ́ darapọ̀ pẹ̀lú orí wa lókè, kìí ṣe nípaṣẹ̀ iṣe ẹnu ọ̀nạ̀́'' Kadarkov ni o so bẹẹ̣́ ̣.
rows.output: "We are for NATO and the EU, but we want to join with our heads up, not tail between our legs," said Kadarkov.
rows.reference: "We are for NATO and EU, but we want to join with our heads up, not through the service door" Kavadarkov said.

rows.source: “Àwá jẹ́ orilẹ-ede tí ò kúùṣẹ́, ṣ̵ùgbọ́n a ní ọ̀wọ̀ ara-ẹni.
rows.output: We are a proud but humble people.
rows.reference: "We are a poor country, but we do have dignity.

rows.source: Bí wọn kòbá fẹ́ gbà wá gẹ́gẹ́bí Masidóníà, a leè kọjú sí àwọn ẹlòmíràn bíi orilẹ-ede Ṣáínà àti Rọ́síà kí á sì dí ara ti àjọṣepọ̀ Euro-Asia.
rows.output: If they do not want to accept us as Macedonians, we can turn to others like China and Russia and strengthen the Euro-Asia alliance.
rows.reference: If they don't want to take us as Macedonia, we can turn to others like China and Russia and become part of Euro-Asia integration."

rows.source: Adarí Ìgbìmọ̀ Zaev sọpé ìjọ́mọ-ẹgbẹ́ NATO yóò mú ìdókòòwò tíwọ́n nílò púpọ̀ wọ orilẹ-ede Masidóníà, eyiti tí ó ní òdiwọn àìríṣẹ́ṣe tí o ju ìdá ogún ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún lọ.
rows.output: The Zaev-led coalition said that NATO membership would bring a lot of foreign investment to Macedonia, which has a high unemployment rate of over 20 percent.
rows.reference: Prime Minister Zaev says NATO membership will bring much needed investment to Macedonia, which has an unemployment rate of more than 20 percent.

rows.source: ''Mo gbàgbọ́ wípé àwọn eniyan pupọ̀ yóò fi ojú rere hàn síi nitori àwọn ọmọ ìlú wa tóju ìdá ọgọ́rin ninu ọgọ́ọ̀rún lọ ńfi ojú rere hàn sí ti àjọ EU àti NATO,'' Zaev ni o sọ báyií lẹ́yìn tí o ju ìwé amútẹ̀kàsí rẹ̀ sínu àpótí.
rows.output: "I believe that many people will see the face of the city of Skopje in a more positive light because 80 percent of the population is supporting the EU and NATO," Zaev said in a statement after submitting his resignation.
rows.reference: "I believe the huge majority will be in favor because more than 80 percent of our citizens are in favor of EU and NATO," Zaev said after casting his ballot.

rows.source: Ó sọpé ìbò ''bẹ́ẹ̀ni'' yóò jẹ ''ìjẹ́ríìsí ọjọ́ iwájú wa.”
rows.output: He said that a "yes" vote would be "our future's guarantee."
rows.reference: He said that a "yes" result would be "confirmation of our future."

rows.source: Ìdìbò èrò ara ìlú kan tíwọ́n ṣàgbéjáde rẹ̀ lọ́jọ́ Ajé láti ọwọ́ Àjọ fún Ìwáàdí nípa Ìlàna Ìṣèjọba sọpé láàrin ìdá ọgbọ̀n àti ìdá mẹ́tàlélógójì ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn olùdìbò ni yóò kópa ninu ìbò oníbẹ́ẹ̀ni-bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ náà - tí o ́lọ sílẹ̀ ju iye ìjáde-dìbò tíwọ́n nílò lọ.
rows.output: A public opinion poll conducted by the Agency for Public Opinion Research on Monday said that between 30 and 43 percent of eligible voters would participate in the referendum - more than the number of votes needed for a valid referendum.

rows.source: Ìdìbò èrò ara ìlú miran, tí ilé iṣẹ́ Amóhùnmáwòrán Telma ṣe, ríi pé ìdá mẹ́tàdínlọ́gọ́ta ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn olùdáhùn ni wọ́n ńgbèrò láti di ìbò náà lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta.
rows.output: Another public opinion poll, conducted by the Telma Television Station, found that 75 percent of those surveyed intend to vote on Monday.

rows.source: Nínú wọ̀n, ìdá àádọ́rin nínú ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún sọpé àwọn yóò dìbò fún bẹ́ẹ̀ni.
rows.output: In that case, 70 percent said they would vote yes.

rows.source: Fún ki ìbò oníbẹ́ẹ̀ni-bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ náà láti jẹ́ àṣeyọrí ìjáde-dìbò nílò láti jẹ́ ìbò ìdá àádọ́ta ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àti ẹyọ kan.

rows.source: Ìkùnà ninu ìbò oníbẹ́ẹ̀ni-bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ náà yóò duro fún àbùkù gbòógì àkọ́kọ́ tí yóò kan ìlànà ìṣèjọba ti ìjọba tó ńṣeti awọn orilẹ-ede Yuroopu ati ilẹ Amẹ́ríkà látígbà tóti gba ìjọba lóṣù Ẹ̀bibi lọ́dún tó kọjá.
rows.output: The postponement of the referendum will be a major blow to the first comprehensive test of the system of government of the European Union and the United States since the election of the European Parliament in June last year.

rows.output: The Rockies won a thrilling game that was not expected with a victory over the Nationals on Thursday, but they are now looking to secure their first division title in the early season.
rows.reference: The Rockies clinched at least a wild-card spot with a 5-2 win over the Nationals on Friday night, but are still looking to lock up their first division title.

rows.source: ''Àní botilẹjepe à ńdíje fún òfo, ó kéré tán á sáà leè fi ọmọ-ìka ẹsẹ̀ taari rọ́bà náà pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ wípé àyíká Denver níbí pẹ̀lú àwọn èrò àti ikọ̀ miran yóò maá gba bọ́ọ̀lù ní ipele tóṣeé ṣe kójẹ́ eyiti ó ga jùlọ ti emi yóò kojú lọ́dún yìí.
rows.output: "Even though I'm competing for a hole, at least I can still throw the ball with the knowledge that the environment of Denver with its altitude and other factors will still allow me to throw the ball at a level that I will face this year.

rows.output: Trump continued, "Have you seen the worst, worst group, the Democrats, you see it happening now.
rows.reference: Trump continued, "You see this horrible, horrible radical group of Democrats, you see it happening right now.

rows.source: Wọ́n sì ̈ti pinnu láti gba agbára padà nípa lílo ọ̀nà èyíkéyìí tó pọn dandan, sé ẹ rí ìwà aìláàánu, àiṣ̵̵eésúnmọ náà.
rows.output: They also decided to take back power by any means necessary, to end the injustice and the oppression.
rows.reference: And they're determined to take back power by using any means necessary, you see the meanness, the nastiness.

rows.source: Wọn kò bìkítà nípa ẹnití wọ́n pa lára, ẹnití wọ́n nilati kọjá lórí rẹ̀ láti lee gba agbára àti ìṣàkóso, ìyẹn nípe ohun tíwọ́n fẹ́ ni agbára àti ìṣàkóso, a kò ní fi i fún wọn.
rows.output: They didn't care about the person they killed, the one they had to walk over to get power and control, that was what they wanted, power and control, we wouldn't give it to them.
rows.reference: They don't care who they hurt, who they have to run over in order to get power and control, that's what they want is power and control, we're not going to give it to them."

rows.source: Àwọn Democrats, ni ó sọpé, wọn wà ninu ìlépa láti ''dínilọ́wọ àti dínamọ́ni.''
rows.output: The Democrats, he said, were in the pursuit of "destruction and chaos."
rows.reference: Democrats, he said, are on a mission to "resist and obstruct."

rows.source: ''Bẹ́ẹ̀ ẹ rí ìyẹn láàrin ọjọ́ mẹ́rin ṣẹ́yìn,''ni o sọ, tó sì ńpe Awọn Democrats ní ''bínubínú àti aláìláàánú àti aláìṣeésúnmọ àti aláiṣòtítọ́.
rows.output: "That's what you're seeing in the last four days," he said, calling the Democrats "cowardly and unprincipled and untrustworthy and untruthful."
rows.reference: "And you see that over the last four days," he said, calling the Democrats "angry and mean and nasty and untruthful."

rows.source: Ó tọ́kasí ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ Democrats Àsojú-ṣòfin Àgbà Dianne Feinstein ti Ìgbìmọ̀ Ètò Ìdájọ́ ti Ilé Ìgbìmọ̀ Aṣojú-ṣòfin Àgbà nípa orúkọ, eyiti o gba ariwo oní-ìbínú láti ọdọ́ àwọn olùtẹ́tígbọ náà.
rows.output: He pointed out that the Democratic Senator Dianne Feinstein's Senate Judiciary Committee had taken the name of the nominee, which caused a wave of angry protests from the nominee's supporters.
rows.reference: He referenced Senate Judiciary Committee ranking Democratic Sen. Dianne Feinstein by name, which received loud boos from the audience.

rows.source: ''Ránti ìdáhùn rẹ̀?
rows.output: "Are you sure of your answer?"
rows.reference: "Remember her answer?

rows.source: Ǹjẹ ìwọ tú àṣ̵írí ìwé àpilẹ̀kọ náà?
rows.output: Have you read the article?
rows.reference: Did you leak the document?

rows.source: Uh, uh, kínni.
rows.output: Uh, uh, what.
rows.reference: Uh, uh, what.

rows.source: Bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́, uh bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́, Mo dúró ọ̀kan - ìyẹn jẹ́ èdè ìfarasọ̀rọ̀ tí kò dára - èdè ìfarasọ̀rọ̀ náà tó burú jùlọ tí Mo tí ì rírí.''
rows.output: However, I'm just one - that's a very bad spoken language - the spoken language is the worst I've ever seen.''
rows.reference: No, uh no, I wait one - that was really bad body language - the worst body language I've ever seen."

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ òṣèlú Labour ko dàbíi ilé ìjọsín tó gbòòrò kan mọ.
rows.output: The Labour Party is not like a large church.
rows.reference: Labour is no longer a broad church.

rows.source: Kòní ìpamọ́ra fún àwọn ti wọ́n ńsọ èrò ọkàn wọn
rows.output: They are not afraid of those who speak their minds.
rows.reference: It is intolerant of those who speak their minds

rows.source: Nigbati àwọn aṣatúnṣe ti Momentum ni ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlu agbègbè mi dìbò láti bámi wí, kò fi gbogbo ara jẹ́ ìyàlẹ̵́nu.
rows.output: When the local political party's Momentum faction voted to censure me, I was not surprised.
rows.reference: When Momentum's activists in my local party voted to censure me, it was hardly a surprise.

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn gbogbo rẹ̀, Èmi ni ẹni tó tuntun jùlọ lórí ìlà àwọn MP ti ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour tíwọn yóò sọ fún pé àwọn kòfẹ́ rí - gbogbo rẹ̀ fún sísọ àwọn èrò ọkàn wa.
rows.output: In the end, I was the youngest on the Labour Party's list of MPs who were told they were not wanted - all because of speaking our minds.
rows.reference: After all, I'm the latest in a line of Labour MPs to be told we are not welcome - all for speaking our minds.

rows.source: Akẹgbẹ́ mi ní ilé ìgbìmọ aṣojú-ṣòfin Joan Ryan gba irú ìfọwọ́múni kan náà nitoripe o fi ọkàn tó pinnu díde dúró sí ìgbógun ti àwọn Júù.
rows.output: My colleague in the House of Commons Joan Ryan received a similar endorsement because she stood up to the bullying of the Jews.
rows.reference: My parliamentary colleague Joan Ryan received similar treatment because she resolutely stood up to antisemitism.

rows.source: Nítèmi, àbá láti bámi wi bú ẹnu àtẹ́ lù mi nitoripe N ko fohùnṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú Jeremy Corbyn.
rows.output: In fact, I was being sarcastic because I didn't agree with Jeremy Corbyn.
rows.reference: In my case, the censure motion criticised me for disagreeing with Jeremy Corbyn.

rows.source: Lórí ìṣepàtàkì ti ìlànà ètò ọ̀rọ̀ ajé kan, lórí ààbò orilẹ-ede, lórí Yuroopu, lọ́nà tó panilẹ́ẹ̀rín àwọm ọ̀rọ̀ tó farajọ ohun tí Jeremy kòfi fohùnṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú àwọn adarí tó saáju.
rows.output: On the importance of a well-designed economic plan, on national security, on Europe, on the very serious issues that Jeremy has not engaged with, the leaders who have been in office for far too long.
rows.reference: On the importance of a responsible economic policy, on national security, on Europe, ironically similar issues on which Jeremy disagreed with previous leaders.

rows.source: ̀Ìfitónilétí fún ìpàdé ẹ̵gbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour ti Ìlà-oòrùn Nottingham lọ́jọ́ Ẹtì sọpé ''a fẹ́ kí ìpàdé náà jẹ́ eyiti ó fààyè gba gbogbo eniyan tí ó sì lérè.''
rows.output: The police were called to the Labour Party meeting in East Nottingham on Thursday after it was said to be "out of control."
rows.reference: The notice for the Nottingham East Labour meeting on Friday stated that "we want the meetings to be inclusive and productive."

rows.source: Fún púpọ̀ ninu ọdún mẹ́jọ mi gẹ́gẹ́bí MP ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour agbègbè, àwọn ìpàdé GC àlẹ́ ọjọ́ Ẹtì náà ti rí bẹ́ẹ̀ gẹ́lẹ́.
rows.output: For most of the eight years of my time as a Labour Party MP, the GC meetings on the 9th of July have been like this.
rows.reference: For most of my eight years as the local Labour MP, the Friday night GC meetings have been exactly that.

rows.source: Ó banilọ́kàn pé lóòní, kìí ṣe ohùn ti ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ìpàdé àtipe ìlérí ti òṣèlú ''tó láàánú, tó ńṣe jẹ́jẹ́ díẹ̀ síi'' ni a ti gbàgbé tipẹ́ bí ó bájẹ̀pé, lóòtítọ́, ó tiẹ̀ bẹ̀rẹ̀ rí rárá.
rows.output: He believes that today, it is not the voice of the many meetings and promises of "compassionate, progressive" politics that have been heard for so long, but rather that, in fact, it has already begun to be heard.
rows.reference: Sadly today, it is not the tone of many meetings and the promise of "kinder, gentler" politics has long been forgotten if, indeed, it ever began.

rows.source: Ó ti wá ńhàn gbangba síwájú síi wipe wọn kò fààyè àwọn ojú ìwòye tó yàtọ̀ ninu ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour àtipé gbogbo èrò ọkàn ni wọn ńṣédájọ́ wọn lórí bóyá ó jẹ́ ìtẹ́wọ́gbá sí àwọn adarí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú náà.
rows.output: It has become increasingly clear that they are not giving space to different views within the Labour Party and that all opinions are being dismissed as whether they are acceptable to the party leaders.
rows.reference: It has become increasingly apparent that differing views are not tolerated in the Labour party and every opinion is judged on whether it is acceptable to the party leadership.

rows.source: Èyí bẹ̀rẹ̀ láìpẹ́ lẹ́yìn tí Jeremy di olórí, bí àwọn akẹgbẹ́ tí Mo ti rò tẹ́lẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ wípé a jọ ńṣàjọpín ojú-ìwòye òṣèlú kan tójọrawọn bẹ̀rèsí rétí wipe kí ńyà bàrà láti gba àwọn ipò tí N kòní fẹ́ ṣe ohun miran láti fohùnṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú rẹ̀ láilái - bóyá lórí ààbò orilẹ-ede tàbí lórí ọjà kan ṣoṣo ti àjọ EU.
rows.output: This began shortly after Jeremy took over, as some of my former colleagues had been sharing a political perspective for years, and they began to retweet more of my tweets, and they began to retweet more of my tweets.
rows.reference: This started shortly after Jeremy became leader, as colleagues with whom I had previously thought I shared a similar political outlook began expecting me to do a U-turn and take positions I would never have otherwise agreed with - whether on national security or the EU single market.

rows.source: Nígbàkúùgbà tí Mo bá sọ̀rọ̀ ni gbangba - tí kòsì ní fiṣe irú ohun ti Mo sọ - níbẹ̀ ni àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ èèbú alásọfitakoni kan yóò ti tẹ̀lé e lórí àwọn ojú-òpó ìbáṣepọ̀ ti ayelujara tíwọn ńpè fún ìyọkúrò, títako òṣèlú ti ààrin náà, tó sì ńsọ fún mi wipe kòyẹ ki N wà ninu ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour.
rows.output: Whenever I speak out publicly - without being censored for the kind of things I say - there are a few tech company executives who will follow me on social media and denounce me as a left-wing radical, telling me that I should not be in the Labour Party.
rows.reference: Whenever I speak publicly - and it doesn't really matter what I say - there follows a tirade of abuse on social media calling for deselection, denouncing the politics of the centre, telling me I should not be in the Labour party.

rows.source: Àtipé ìyẹn kìí ṣe ìrírí tèmi nìkan.
rows.output: That is not my experience alone.
rows.reference: And that is not just my experience.

rows.source: Ní tòótọ́, Mo mọ̀ wipe Mo jẹ́ olóríire ju àwọn kan ninu àwọn akẹgbẹ́ mi lọ bí ó ṣe jẹ́pé àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí a darí sọ́dọ̀ mi tí máa ńjẹ́ ti òṣèlú.
rows.output: In fact, I know that I am luckier than some of my colleagues because the words directed to me are often of a political nature.
rows.reference: Indeed, I know I am more fortunate than some of my colleagues as the comments directed at me tend to be political.

rows.source: Ẹnu máa ńyà mi nípa ti ìwà akọ́ṣẹ́mọṣẹ́ àti ìṣọkàngírí ti àwọn akẹgbẹ́ wọ̀nyen tí wọ́n ńdojúkọ òjò èèbù ti àwọn tí kòka obìnrin sí nǹkan àti àwọn ẹlẹ́yàmẹ̀yà lójoojúmọ́ ṣùgbọ́n tíwọn kò sálọ nígbà kankan.
rows.output: I am disgusted by the hypocrisy and arrogance of these colleagues who are exposed to the rain of the oppressed women and the marginalized every day but never get wet.
rows.reference: I am in awe of the professionalism and determination of those colleagues who face a torrent of sexist or racist abuse every day but never shy away.

rows.source: Ọ̀kan ninu àwọn nǹkan tó ńjánikulẹ̀ jùlọ ninu òṣèlú ti òde-ìwòyí ni bí àwọn ipele èèbù bíbú ti wá di àṣà tó bójúmu.
rows.output: One of the most disturbing things in the current political climate is the way in which the level of polarization has become a socially accepted norm.
rows.reference: One of the most disappointing aspects of this era of politics is how levels of abuse have become normalised.

rows.source: Jeremy Corbyn  sọ lọ́sẹ̀ tókọjá wipe ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlu Labour níláti jẹ́kí ìdàgbàsókè bá àṣà ìpamọ́ra.
rows.output: Jeremy Corbyn said last week that the Labour Party should be committed to growth that is sustainable and environmentally friendly.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn claimed last week that the Labour party should foster a culture of tolerance.

rows.source: Òtítọ náà nipé a kìí ṣe sọọsi tó gbòòrò yẹn mọ́ àtipé pẹ̀lu gbogbo àbá ''kòsí-ìgbẹkẹ̀lé'' tabi àwọn ìlàna ìyípadà ti ìyannisipò ẹgbẹ òṣèlu náà ńdi eyiti ó ńtín-ín-rín púpọ síi.
rows.output: The truth is that we are not talking about a large-scale surrender, but rather about the gradual erosion of the "non-alternative" or the transformation of the position of the left, which is becoming more and more marginalized.
rows.reference: The reality is we are no longer that broad church and with every "no-confidence" motion or change of selection rules the party becomes narrower.

rows.source: Mo ti ní ọpọ ìmọràn láàrin ọdún méjì tókọjá tó ńpàrọwà fún mi láti jẹ́kí orí mi wà nísàlẹ̀, kí ńmá fí bẹ́ẹ̀ sọ̀rọ̀ mọ́ àtipé lẹ́yìn náà N ó ''wà dáadáa.''
rows.output: I've had a lot of thoughts in the past two years that have been nagging me to get my head down, to just shut up and get on with it.
rows.reference: I have had lots of advice over the past two years urging me to keep my head down, not to be so vocal and then I would "be all right."

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n ìyẹn kìí ṣe ohun tí Mo wá sínú òṣèlú láti ṣe.
rows.output: But that's not what I came into politics to do.
rows.reference: But that is not what I came into politics to do.

rows.source: Láti ìgbà tí Mo ti darapọ̀ mọ́ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour bí ọmọ ilé ìwé kan, lẹ́yìn inú tó bí mi nípa àìbìkítà ìjọba Thatcher eyiti ó fi kíláàsì ilé-ìwé onígbogbo-ẹ̀kọ́ mi sílẹ̀ nípò tóti fẹ́rẹ̀ wólulẹ̀ tán, Mo ti ṣe àwárí láti máa jà fún ìmúdára síi àwọn iṣẹ́ ìlú fún àwọn tí wọ́n nílò wọn jùlọ - bóyá gẹ́gẹ́bí káńsílọ̀ agbègbè kan tàbí aláàkóso ìjọba.
rows.output: Since joining the Labour Party as a student, after being born of the neglect of Thatcher's government which left my comprehensive school on the brink of collapse, I have sought to fight for better public services for those who need them most - whether as a local councillor or a government minister.
rows.reference: Ever since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a school pupil, provoked by the Thatcher government's neglect that had left my comprehensive school classroom literally falling down, I've sought to champion better public services for those who need them most - whether as a local councillor or government minister.

rows.source: Èmi kòfi ìgbà kankan fi òṣèlú mi pamọ́, àti ninu ìdìbò tókọjá náà.
rows.output: I have never hidden my politics, and in the last election.
rows.reference: I have never hidden my politics, including at the last election.

rows.source: Kòsí ẹnikan ninu Ìla-oòrùn Nottingham tí ó leè ní ìpòrúùru ọkàn lọ́nàkọnà nípa àwọn ipò ìlànà mi àti àwọn ipele àìleèfohùnṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú àwọn adàri tówànípò lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: No one in the Eastern part of Nottinghamshire can have a more disturbed mind than I do about my legal position and the lack of transparency with the current crop of charlatans.
rows.reference: No one in Nottingham East could have been in any way confused about my policy positions and areas of disagreement with the current leadership.

rows.source: Fún àwọn tíwọn jẹ́kí ìtẹ̀síwájú bá àbá náà lọ́jọ́ Ẹtì, gbogbo ohun ti N ó sọ nipé nigbati orilẹ-ede náà ńroko sọ́nà ọ̀dọ̀ Brexit kan eyiti yóò pa àwọn ara-ilé, àwọn oko-òwò, àti àwọn iṣé ìlú lára, Èmi kòní òye ìfẹ́ náà láti máa fi àkókò àti agbára mi ṣofo lórí jíjẹ́ olóòtítọ́ si adarí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour.
rows.output: For those who are making progress towards the goal of the referendum on June 23, all I can say is that when the country votes for a Brexit that will tear apart families, businesses, and communities, I will not have the time or energy to be a loyal member of the Labour Party.
rows.reference: To those who promoted the motion on Friday, all I would say is that when the country is ploughing towards a Brexit that will hurt households, businesses and our public services, I do not understand the desire to waste time and energy on my loyalty to the Labour party leader.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọn lóòtítọ iṣẹ ìránṣẹ́ kan tí Mo ní kìí ṣe sí Nothingham Momentum, o wá fún àwọn to dìbò fún mí, bóyá wọ́n jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour tàbí bẹ́ẹ̀kọ́: Mo ń yangàn láti sìn yín tí Mo sì ṣe ìlérì wipe kòsí iye àwọn ìdúnkookò ìyọnikúrò tàbi ti òṣèlú   kòṣẹlẹ̀-kíákíá tí yóò dámi lọ́wọ́ kọ́ láti máṣe kópa mọ́ ninu ohun tí Mo gbàgbó wipe wọ́n jẹ́ àwọn ohun dára jùlọ fún gbogbo yín.
rows.output: However, a genuine offer of work that I have not taken up with Nothingham Momentum, came for those who voted for me, whether they were Labour Party members or not: I am willing to serve you and I have promised that no amount of left-wing or right-wing politics will deter me from participating in what I believe are the best interests for all of you.
rows.reference: But really the one message I have is not to Nottingham Momentum, it is to my constituents, whether Labour members or not: I am proud to serve you and I promise that no amount of deselection threats or political expediency will deter me from acting in what I believe are the best interests of you all.

rows.source: Chris Leslie  ni MP fún Ìla-oòrùn Nottingham
rows.output: Chris Leslie is the MP for Nottingham East
rows.reference: Chris Leslie is MP for Nottingham East

rows.source: Ayr 38 - 17 Melrose: Ayr tíwọn kòlù rí lọ sóke
rows.output: Ayr 38 - 17 Melrose: Ayr won by 21 points
rows.reference: Ayr 38 - 17 Melrose: Unbeaten Ayr go top

rows.source: Awọn ìgbìyànjú ìgbẹ̀yìn méjì leè ti sún èsì ìpari náà bákan-bákan, ṣùgbọ́n kòsí àni-àní wipe Ayr yẹ láti borí ninu ìdíje ọjọ́ náà yìí tójẹ́ apanilẹ́ẹ̀rín tótún yanilẹ́nu ninu Ìṣọ̀rí Aláàkọ́kọ́ ti Tennent.
rows.output: The two previous attempts may have fallen short of a perfect ending, but there is no doubt that Ayr should have won the day's match, which was a thrilling replay of the First Division decider between Tennent's.
rows.reference: Two late tries may have skewed the final result somewhat, but there is no doubt Ayr deserved to triumph in this wonderfully-entertaining Tennent's Premiership match of the day.

rows.source: Báyìí àwọn ni ó wà lóòkè tábìlì náà, ikọ̀ kan ṣoṣo ninu mẹ́wàá tíwọn kò tíì lù rí.
rows.output: Now they are on top of the table, only one of the ten has not yet been knocked down.
rows.reference: They now top the table, the only unbeaten side of the ten.

rows.source: Ní òpin rẹ̀, ààbò wọn tógbópọn ni, pẹ̀lú pé wọ́n ńṣàmúlò àwọn àǹfààní lọ́ná tódára jù, eyiti ó gbé ikọ̀ ti ilé náà tí olùkọ́ni wọn sì ní gbogbo ẹ̀tọ́ láti máa dunnú.
rows.output: In the end, their security was strong, with the use of the advantages of the house, which was a fortress, and the master of the house had every right to be happy.
rows.reference: In the end, it was their superior defence, as much as their better chance-taking, which carried the home side and coach Peter Murchie had every right to be pleased.

rows.source: ''A ti dán wa wò nínú àwọn ayò wa tìtí dé ibí yìí, àtipé síbẹ̀ kòsí ẹnití ó tíì lù wá, nitorinaa Mo nílatí máa dunnú,'' ni ó sọ.
rows.output: "We have been tested in our ways until now, and yet no one has ever defeated us, so I must be proud."
rows.reference: "We've been tested over our games this far, and we're still unbeaten, so I have to be happy," he said.

rows.source: Robyn Christie ti Melrose sọpé: ''Òṣùba lọ sọ́dọ̀ Ayr, wọ́n ṣàmúlò àwọn àǹfààní wọn lọ́nà tódára ju bí àwa tiṣe lọ.''
rows.output: Robyn Christie of Melrose said: "The osbornes went to Ayr, they took advantage of their opportunities in a more effective way than we did."
rows.reference: Robyn Christie of Melrose said: "Credit to Ayr, they took their chances better than we did."

rows.source: Ìgbìyànjú ìṣẹ́jú ìkẹrìnlá ti Grant Anderson, ti a yípada nípaṣẹ̀ Frazier Climo, fi Ayr síwájú, ṣùgbọ́n káàdì aláwọ̀ òfééèfé kan fún onífìla ilẹ̀ Scotland Rory Hughes, tí Warriors fi sílẹ̀ fún ìdíje náà, gba Melrose láyè láti jẹ́kí àwọn nọmba sọ̀rọ̀ tí Jason Baggot sì sáré di ìgbìyànjú kan tí a kò yípadà mu.
rows.output: The 14th-minute attempt by Grant Anderson, converted by Frazier Climo, put Ayr ahead, but a late equaliser for Scotland international Rory Hughes, who was brought on for the match, allowed Melrose to take the lead with Jason Baggot scoring an unconverted try.
rows.reference: Grant Anderson's 14th minute try, converted by Frazier Climo, put Ayr in front, but, a yellow card for Scotland cap Rory Hughes, released for the game by Warriors, allowed Melrose to make numbers tell and Jason Baggot grabbed an unconverted try.

rows.source: Climo fẹ ìléwájú Ayr lójú pẹ̀lú ìjìyà pẹnariti kan, saájú, ní ìdajì àkókò gan-an, ó gbá ayò wọlé lẹ́yìn náà ó yí ìgbìyànjú aláàdáṣe kan padà láti sọ ọ́ di 17-5 fún Ayr ní àkókò ìsinmi náà.
rows.output: Climo was punished with a five-penalty for Ayr, before, in the first half, he scored a goal and then turned a penalty into a 17-5 advantage for Ayr during the break.
rows.reference: Climo stretched the Ayr lead with a penalty, before, right on half-time, he scored then converted a solo try to make it 17-5 to Ayr at the break.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n Melrose bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìdajì ìdíje ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì náà lọ́nà tódára tí ìgbìyànjú Patrick Anderson, tí Baggot yípadà sì dín ìyàtọ̀ náà kù sí àwọn kókó máàrún.
rows.output: But Melrose began the second half of the game in a more positive manner than the attempt by Patrick Anderson, who was replaced by Baggot, and reduced the difference to five points.
rows.reference: But Melrose began the second half well and Patrick Anderson's try, converted by Baggot, reduced the leeway to five points.

rows.source: Ìdádúró gígùn kan wà lẹ́yìn náà fún ìfarapa púpọ̀ tí Ruaridh Knott ní, ẹnití wọ́n gbé jáde kúrò, àtipé láti àtúnbẹ̀rẹ̀ náà, Ayr tún yọrí síwájú nípaṣẹ̀ ìgbìyànjú Stafford McDowall kan, eyití wọ́n yípadà láti ọwọ́ Climo.
rows.output: A long stop followed for a lot of punishment inflicted on Ruaridh Knott, who was taken off, and then Ayr advanced further through a Stafford McDowall attempt, which was changed from Climo's hand.
rows.reference: There was then a lengthy hold-up for a serious injury to Ruaridh Knott, who was stretchered off, and from the restart, Ayr surged further ahead through a Stafford McDowall try, converted by Climo.

rows.source: Adele balógun ti Ayr Blair Macpherson niwọ́n fún ní káàdì aláwọ̀ òfééèfé lẹ́yìn náà, àtipé lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, Melrose jẹ́kì ọkùnrin àfikún náà sanwó pẹ̀lú ìgbìyànjú Bruce Colvine kan tíwọn kò yípadà, ní òpin èèdi oní-ìdààmu tó gbóná gidigidi kan.
rows.output: Deputy chief constable of Ayrshire Blair Macpherson was awarded a certificate of commendation for his efforts, and again, Melrose was the man who paid the price with a Bruce Colvine attempt that was not changed, at the end of a very hot summer.
rows.reference: Ayr acting captain Blair Macpherson was then yellow-carded, and again, Melrose made the extra man pay with an unconverted Bruce Colvine try, at the end of a spell of fierce pressure.

rows.source: Ikọ̀ onílé náà padà wá, lábẹ̀ botiwukori, àtipé nigbati wọ́n fún Struan Hutchinson ni káàdì aláwọ̀ òfééèfé fún títako Climo láìsí bọ́ọ̀lù, láti ibi ìlà ìjìyà pẹnariti, MacPherson fẹṣẹ̀ kan ilẹ̀ lẹ́yìn òòlù àwọn Ayr tó ńtẹ̀síwájú.
rows.output: The owner of the house came back, under the eaves, and when they gave Struan Hutchinson a green card for Climo's kick without a ball, from the penalty spot, MacPherson kicked the ground behind the Ayr goal.
rows.reference: The home side came back, however, and when Struan Hutchinson was yellow-carded for tackling Climo without the ball, from the penalty line-out, MacPherson touched down at the back of the advancing Ayr maul.

rows.source: Climo yí padà, bí ó tunṣe ṣe n’ibẹ̀rẹ̀, lẹ́yìn tí Kyle Rowe gba bọ́ọ̀lù ti David Armstrong gbá lati inú apoti tí ó sì fi onípò-igun ránṣẹ́ síta fún ìgbìyànjú ẹlẹẹ̀kaàrún fun àwọn ikọ̀ onílé náà.
rows.output: Climo turned, as he always did, after Kyle Rowe took a throw-in from David Armstrong and sent a long ball for a tenth-minute attempt for the home team.
rows.reference: Climo converted, as he did again almost from the restart, after Kyle Rowe gathered David Armstrong's box kick and sent flanker Gregor Henry away for the home side's fifth try.

rows.source: Ìràwọ Still Game dábì ẹniti óti ṣetán fún iṣẹ́-ìṣe tuntun ní ilé iṣẹ́ ẹka ti olóúnjẹ.
rows.output: Still Game's star is ready for a new role in the food industry's division.
rows.reference: Still Game star looks set for new career in restaurant industry

rows.source: Ìràwọ Still Game Ford Kieran dábì ẹnitó ṣetán láti lọ sínú ilé iṣẹ́ ti ẹka olóúnjẹ lẹ́yìn tíwọ́n ṣàwárí wipe wọ́n ti dárúkọ rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí olùdarí ile iṣẹ́ tóní àwọn ile ìsoúnjẹta oníìwé-àṣẹ kan.
rows.output: Kieran Ford, the star of Still Game, is ready to join the team of the food sector after they discovered that he was named as the director of a company that owns a chain of restaurants.
rows.reference: Still Game star Ford Kieran looks set to move into the hospitality industry after it was discovered he's been named as the director of a licensed restaurants company.

rows.source: Ẹni ọdún mẹ́rìndínlọ́gọ́ta náà ló ńkópa bíi Jack Jarvis lórí ètò BBC tó gbajúmọ̀ náà, níbití ó ti ńkọ̀wé tó sì ńdìjọ ṣeré pẹ̀lú akẹgbẹ́ aláàwàdà ọlọ́jọ́-pípẹ́ Greg Hemphill.
rows.output: A 46-year-old man is playing the role of Jack Jarvis on the popular BBC radio show, in which he writes and performs with long-time comedy partner Greg Hemphill.
rows.reference: The 56-year-old plays Jack Jarvis on the popular BBC show, which he writes and co-stars with long-time comedy partner Greg Hemphill.

rows.source: Àwọn méjèèjì ti kédé wipe oníṣíṣẹ̀-n-tẹ̀lé ìkẹẹ̀sán tó ńbọ náà yóò jẹ́ ìkẹyìn ninu eré ti ètò náà, tí o sì dàbí wípé Kiernan ńṣètò fún ìgbésí-ayé lẹ́yìn Craiglang.
rows.output: Both of them have acknowledged that the next episode will be the last of the series, and it seems like Kiernan is preparing for life after Craiglang.
rows.reference: The duo have announced that the upcoming ninth series will be the final one in the show's run, and it appears Kiernan is planning for life after Craiglang.

rows.source: Gẹ́gẹ́bí àwọn àtòkọ àkọsìlẹ́ ilé iṣẹ́, òun ni olùdarí Adriftmorn Limited.
rows.output: As the corporate records indicate, he is the director of Adriftmorn Limited.
rows.reference: According to official record listings, he is the director of Adriftmorn Limited.

rows.source: Òṣèré náà kọ láti sọ̀rọ̀ ìtàn náà, botilẹjẹpe orísun ìwé ìròyìn Scottish Sun yọ́ ọ sọpé Kiernan tí ńfojú wá ọ̀nà láti dásí ''oko-òwò ilé iṣẹ́ olóúnjẹ tó ńgbèrú'' ti Glasgow.
rows.output: The actor refused to speak the story, although the Scottish Sun newspaper reported that Kiernan was looking for a way to "disrupt the business of the catering industry" of Glasgow.
rows.reference: The actor declined to comment on the story, though a Scottish Sun source hinted that Kiernan was looking to get involved in Glasgow's "thriving restaurant trade."

rows.source: 'Òkun náà jẹ́ tiwa': Orilẹ-ede Bolifia tí ilẹ̀ gbígbẹ yípo pátápátá ńretí wipe ilé ẹjọ́ yóò tún sí ọ̀nà sínú òkun Pàsífíìkì
rows.output: "The sea is ours": The Bolivian Amazon, a land of rivers, expects the court to return to the Pacific Ocean
rows.reference: 'The sea is ours': landlocked Bolivia hopes court will reopen path to Pacific

rows.source: Àwọn ọmọ ogun orí-omi ńlọ káàkiri yíka àwọn olú ilé iṣẹ àwọn ọmọ ogun orí-omi tíwọn wọ̀ lásọ ní ìlú La Paz.
rows.output: The naval troops are moving around the perimeter of the naval base, which they have surrounded in the city of La Paz.
rows.reference: Sailors patrol a rigging-clad naval headquarters in La Paz.

rows.source: Awọn ilé ìjọba ńgbé àsìá aláwọ omi òkun sókê.
rows.output: The government buildings hoist the blue flag.
rows.reference: Public buildings fly an ocean-blue flag.

rows.source: Àwọn ibùdó àwọn ọmọ ogun orí-omi láti adágún Titicaca sí Amazon náà ni wọ́n lẹ àkọmọ̀nà náà mọ́pé: ''Òkun náà jẹ́ tiwa nípa ẹ̀tọ́.
rows.output: The camps of the river soldiers from Lake Titicaca to the Amazon were marked by the motto: "The river is ours by right."
rows.reference: Naval bases from Lake Titicaca to the Amazon are daubed with the motto: "The sea is ours by right.

rows.source: Láti gbà á padà jẹ́ ojúṣe kan.''
rows.output: To restore it is a responsibility.''
rows.reference: To recover it is a duty."

rows.source: Jákè-jádò orilẹ-ede Bolifia tí ilẹ̀ gbígbẹ yí káàkiri, ìrántí ti bèbè òkun tíwọ́n pàdánù sọ́wọ́ orilẹ-ede Ṣílè nínú aáwọ̀ ohun àmúṣọrọ̀ ti ọgọ́ọ̀rún ọdún ìkọkàndínlógún ninu eyiti ẹ̀jẹ̀ ti sàn sì hàn kedere - gẹ́gẹ́bí ìpòǹgbẹ láti tún tukọ̀ lórí òkun Pasífíìkì lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi.
rows.output: The Bolivian Amazon, a vast and verdant region, is a reminder of the oceanic barrier that once separated the land from the island of Chile, a barrier that was overcome through the blood and sweat of generations who sought to sail the Pacific Ocean once more.
rows.reference: Throughout landlocked Bolivia, the memory of a coastline lost to Chile in a bloody 19th-century resource conflict is still vivid - as is the yearning to sail the Pacific Ocean once more.

rows.source: Àwọn ìrètí wọ̀nyẹn ní wọ́n wà ní bóyá nípò tóga jùlọ ninu àwọn ọdún, bí orilẹ-ede Bolifia ti ńdúró dé ìdájọ́ ilé ẹjọ́ àgbáyé lọ́jọ́ ìkínní oṣù Ọ̀wàrà lẹ́yìn àwọn ìfikùnlukùn ọdún máàrún.
rows.output: Those hopes were perhaps in the most precarious position in the years, as the Bolifia nation waited for a judgment from the World Court on the fifth anniversary of the coup.
rows.reference: Those hopes are perhaps at their highest in decades, as Bolivia awaits a ruling by the international court of justice on 1 October after five years of deliberations.

rows.source: ''Bolifia ni ipá náà tó ńti, ẹ̀mí ìṣọ̀kan àti ìbàlẹ̀-ọkàn, tí ó sì ńretí àbájáde náà pẹ̀lú ojú-ìwòye rere,'' gẹgẹ bíi Roberto Calzadilla, aṣojú orilẹ-ede Bolifia kan ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "Power is in the people, unity and strength, and they are expecting the results with a positive vision," as Roberto Calzadilla, a Bolivian representative, said.
rows.reference: "Bolivia has the momentum, a spirit of unity and serenity, and is of course expecting with a positive view the outcome," said Roberto Calzadilla, a Bolivian diplomat.

rows.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ọmọ orilẹ-ede Bolifia yóô ìdájọ́ ICJ náà lórí àwọn ojú-ìwòran ńlá jáke-jádò orilẹ-ede náà, pẹ̀lú ìrètí wipe ìgbìmọ ìdájọ́ náà ní The Hague yóò fi ojú rere wo àwíjàre Bolifia wipe - lẹ́yìn àwọn ọdún ti àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí kò yọrísí rere - orilẹ-ede Ṣílè wà lábẹ́ ojúṣe tójẹ́ danfan eyiti ó ńfún Bolifia ní ẹ̀tọ́ sí ọ̀nà láti jade sí òkun náà.
rows.output: Many Bolivians are looking to the ICJ ruling on the sea dispute, hoping that the court in The Hague will give Bolivia a favorable view of its claim that - after years of fruitless negotiations - Chile is obligated to grant Bolivia access to the sea.
rows.reference: Many Bolivians will watch the ICJ ruling on big screens across the country, hopeful that the tribunal in The Hague will find in favour of Bolivia's claim that - after decades of fitful talks - Chile is obliged to negotiate granting Bolivia a sovereign outlet to the sea.

rows.source: Evo Morales, ààrẹ orilẹ-ede Bolifia tójẹ́ ojúlówó ọmọ ìlú táyé ńfẹ́ - ẹniti on ja ìjà aláàríyànjiyàn atún dìbò yàn lọ́dún tó ńbọ̀ - tí ó sì̀ ní igùn púpọ̀ láti ṣe bákannáa lórí ìdájọ́ ti ọjọ́ Aje ́.
rows.output: Former Bolivian President Evo Morales, who is a candidate for re-election in the upcoming elections, has a lot to say about the judgment of the day.
rows.reference: Evo Morales, Bolivia's charismatic indigenous president - who faces a controversial battle for re-election next year - also has plenty riding on Monday's ruling.

rows.source: ó ṣèlérí ní òpin oṣù Ògún pe ''A ti súnmọ pípadà sí Òkun Pàsif́ìkì gidi gáàn''.
rows.output: He promised at the end of August that "We are getting close to the real Pacific Ocean again."
rows.reference: "We are very close to returning to the Pacific Ocean," he vowed in late August.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n àwọn ọ̀mọràn kan gbàgbọ́ wipe kòṣeé ṣe kí ilé ẹjọ́ pinnu lọ́nà ti yóò ṣe orilẹ-ede Bolifia ní rere - àtipé nǹkan kékeré ni yóò yípadà bí ó bá ṣée.
rows.output: But some people believe that the judiciary cannot decide in a way that would benefit the country of Bolivia - and that a small change would make a big difference if it were to happen.
rows.reference: But some analysts believe that the court is unlikely to decide in Bolivia's favour - and that little would change if it did.

rows.source: Àjọ UN náà tófìdí kalẹ̀ sí orilẹ-ede Nẹdáláǹdi kòní agbára láti fi ilẹ̀ Ṣílì dánilọ́lá, àtipé ó ti sọ wipe òun kòni pinnu àbájáde àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ṣeé ṣe.
rows.output: The UN Security Council has not been able to impose a ceasefire in Syria, and it has said that it has no intention of making a decision on the possible consequences of its actions.
rows.reference: The Netherlands-based UN body has no power to award Chilean territory, and has stipulated that it will not determine the outcome of possible talks.

rows.source: Wipe ìdájọ́ ICJ náà ńwáyé ní oṣù mẹ́fà péré lẹ́yìn tíwọ́n gbọ́ àwọn àwíjàre ìgbẹ̀yìn tọ́kasíi pé ẹjọ́ náà ''kò ta kókó’,-  gẹgẹ bíi Paz Zárate, ọmọ orilẹ-ede Ṣílè kan tójẹ́ akọ́ṣẹ́mọṣẹ́ ninu òfin àgbáyé ṣe sọ.
rows.output: The ICJ's ruling took six months to come after the last oral hearings, which were held in March, as stated by Paz Zárate, a Chilean lawyer specializing in international law.
rows.reference: That the ICJ's ruling comes only six months after the final arguments were heard indicates the case "wasn't complicated," said Paz Zárate, a Chilean expert in international law.

rows.source: Àtipé ní jíjìnnà sí mímú ìtẹ̵̀síwájú bá ìlépa orilẹ-ede Bolifia, àwọn ọdún mẹ́rin náà tókọjá leè ti fà á sẹ́yìn.
rows.output: The country is still far from achieving the goal of the Bolivian National Plan, which was set for four years ago.
rows.reference: And far from furthering Bolivia's cause, the past four years may have set it back.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ nípa àtirọ́nàde òkun náà ni ìṣàkóso orilẹ-ede Bolifia tówà lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ náà ti já gbà,'' gẹgẹ bíi Zárate ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "The news about the sea is in the hands of the current Bolivian government," as stated by Zárate.
rows.reference: "The issue of access to the sea has been hijacked by the current Bolivian administration," said Zárate.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ oníjà dúndùn ti Morales ti fa ìfẹ́ inú rere tóṣékù ti orilẹ-ede Bolifia mu tán, ni ó dá láàbá.
rows.output: The harsh words of Morales have stirred up a deep sense of national pride in Bolivia.
rows.reference: Morales's belligerent rhetoric has sapped any residual Chilean goodwill, she suggested.

rows.source: Orilẹ-ede Bolifia àti Ṣílì̀ yóò tẹ̀síwajú láti máa sọ̀rọ̀ ni àwọn ibi kan, ṣùgbọ́n yóò ṣòro gidigidi láti ní àwọn ìjíròrò lẹ́yìn èyí.
rows.output: The Bolivian and Chilean governments will continue to talk in certain places, but it will be very difficult to have further discussions after this.
rows.reference: Bolivia and Chile will at some point continue to talk, but it will be extremely difficult to hold discussions after this.

rows.source: Àwọn orilẹ-ede méjì náà kò tíì ṣe pàsípààrọ̀ àwọn aṣoju láti ọdún 1962.
rows.output: The two countries have not yet exchanged ambassadors since 1962.
rows.reference: The two countries have not exchanged ambassadors since 1962.

rows.source: Ààrẹ tẹ́lẹ̀rí Eduardo Rodriguez Veltzé, aṣojú orilẹ-ede Bolifia ní The Hague, kọ èròǹgbà náà wipe ìpinnu-ṣíṣe ti ilé-ẹjọ́ náà tiyá kíakía ju bótiyẹ lọ.
rows.output: Former President Eduardo Rodriguez Veltzé, Bolivia's representative in The Hague, wrote that the court's decision was rushed.
rows.reference: Former president Eduardo Rodríguez Veltzé, Bolivia's representative at The Hague, rejected the idea that the court's decision-making was unusually speedy.

rows.source: O sowipe Ọjọ́ Ajé yóò mu orilẹ-ede Bolifia wọnú ''ànfààní tóṣe àrà-ọ̀tọ̀ kan láti sí ìgbà ọ̀tun ti àwọn ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú orilẹ-ede Ṣílì̀'' àti ààyè kan láti ''fi òpin sí àwọn ọdún mọ́kàndínlógóje ti àwọn èdé-àìyedè pẹ̀lú àwọn àǹfààní aláàjùmọ̀je”̣̣.
rows.output: He said that the day of the election would bring Bolivia into "a unique opportunity to move into a new era of relations with Chile" and to "put an end to 150 years of conflict with the advantages of a more just society."
rows.reference: Monday will bring Bolivia "an extraordinary opportunity to open a new era of relations with Chile" and a chance to "put an end to 139 years of disagreements with mutual benefits," he said.

rows.source: Bákannáà Calzadilla tún ṣẹ́ wipe Morales - tó sí jẹ ọ̀kan ninu àwọn ààrẹ̀ ilẹ Latinni Amẹ́ríkà tó gbajúmọ̀ jùlọ - ńlo ọ̀rọ̀ ìgbòke-gbodò lórí omi òkun bí ọ̀pákùtẹ̀lẹ̀ òṣèlú kan.
rows.output: Calzadilla also said that Morales - who is one of the most popular presidents in Latin America - is using the term "green economy" as a political slogan.
rows.reference: Calzadilla also denied that Morales - still one of Latin America's most popular presidents - was using the maritime issue as a political crutch.

rows.source: ó tun fi kún un pe Bolifia kòní fi ẹ̀tọ́ rẹ̀ sí Òkun Pàsífíìkì náà sílẹ̀ láíláí’.
rows.output: He also emphasized that Bolivia has never renounced its rights to the Pacific Ocean.
rows.reference: "Bolivia will never give up its right to have access to the Pacific Ocean," he added.

rows.source: ''Ìdájọ́ náà jẹ àǹfààní láti rí i pé a nì láti borí ohun àtijọ́ náà
rows.output: The judgment is a chance to see that we are able to overcome the old thing.
rows.reference: "The ruling is an opportunity to see that we need to overcome the past."

rows.source: Orilẹ-ede Àrìwá Kòríà sọpé kíkó àwọn àdó olóro dánù kòní ṣẹlẹ́ àyàfi tí òun bá leè gba orilẹ-ede US gbọ́
rows.output: North Korea claims that it will not denuclearize unless the U.S. accepts it as a nuclear state.
rows.reference: North Korea says nuclear disarmament won't come unless it can trust US

rows.source: Aláàkóso Ọ̀rọ̀ Ilẹ̀ Òkèèrè ti orilẹ-ede Àrìwá Kòríà Ri Yong sọpé orilẹ-ede òun kòni kó àwọn ohun ìjà àdó olóro rẹ̀ dánù láilái bí kòbá leè gba orilẹ-ede Washingtọn gbọ́.
rows.output: The Director of the North Korean Central News Agency, Ri Yong, said that his country would never give up its nuclear weapons unless the United States accepts North Korea as a nuclear state.
rows.reference: North Korean Foreign Minister Ri Yong Ho says his nation will never disarm its nuclear weapons first if it can't trust Washington.

rows.source: Ri ńsọ̀rọ̀ lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta níbi Ìpéjọpọ̀ Gbogbogbòò ti Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé náà.
rows.output: Speaking on Wednesday at the General Assembly of the United Nations.
rows.reference: Ri was speaking Saturday at the United Nations General Assembly.

rows.source: Ó pe orilẹ-ede Àmẹ́ríkà láti tẹ̀lé àwọn ìlérí tí ó ṣe nígbà ìpàdé kan ní orilẹ-ede Singapore láàrin àwọn adarí tí ńbá ara wọn ṣe orogún náà.
rows.output: He called on the United States to follow through on commitments made during a meeting in Singapore between leaders of the two countries.
rows.reference: He called on the United States to follow through on promises made during a summit in Singapore between the rivals' leaders.

rows.source: Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀ wá bí US. Akọwe ti Ilẹ̀ Òkèèrè Mike Pompeo ti ńṣe bí ẹnití ó wà ní bèbe àtítúnbẹ̀rẹ̀ ìjíròrò lórí ọ̀rọ̀ àdó olóró tóti dúró sójú kan ju oṣù mẹ́ta lẹ́yìn ti Singapore náà pẹ̀lú Kim Jong Un ti Àríwá Kòríà.
rows.output: His words came like a US. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo was acting like a man on the brink of a deal on denuclearization after three months since the Singapore summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
rows.reference: His comments come as US. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo seems to be on the verge of restarting deadlocked nuclear diplomacy more than three months after the Singapore with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.

rows.source: Ri sọpé ó jẹ́ ''àlá tí kò leè ṣẹ'' kan wipe àwọn ìjẹniníyà tó ńtẹ̀síwájú àti àtakò ti U.S. sí ìkéde kan tó ńparí Ogun Kòríà yóò mú Àríwá náà wá sórí àwọn orúnkún rẹ̀.
rows.output: It was said to be a "pipe dream" that the continued sanctions and hostility of the U.S. to the idea of a Korean Peninsula settlement would bring North Korea back to its knees.
rows.reference: Ri says it's a "pipe dream" that continued sanctions and U.S. objection to a declaration ending the Korean War will ever bring the North to its knees.

rows.source: Washington ńsọ́raṣè láti faramọ́ ìkéde náà láijẹ́ wipe Pyongyang kọ́kọ́ gbé àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ pàtàkì láti kó àwọn nǹkan ogun dánù.
rows.output: Washington is cautious about endorsing the agreement, even though Pyongyang first took significant steps to dismantle its weapons.
rows.reference: Washington is wary of agreeing to the declaration without Pyongyang first making significant disarmament moves.

rows.source: Kim àti U.S. Ààrẹ Donald Trump fẹ́ ìpàdé ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì.
rows.output: Kim and U.S. President Donald Trump are set to meet for a second summit.
rows.reference: Both Kim and U.S. President Donald Trump want a second summit.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n ìsiyèméjì tótàn káàkiri wà wipe Pyongyang  kòfi ọ̀rọ̀ ṣeré nípa kíkọ àwọn nǹkan ogun tí orilẹ-ede náà rí bí ọ̀nà kan ṣoṣo láti jẹ́kí ààbò rẹ̀ dájú sílẹ̀.
rows.output: But the real question is whether Pyongyang is serious about giving up its nuclear weapons as the only way to ensure its security.
rows.reference: But there is widespread skepticism that Pyongyang is serious about renouncing an arsenal that the country likely sees as the only way to guarantee its safety.

rows.source: Pompeo ńṣètò láti ṣàbẹ̀wò sí Pyongyang lóṣù tó ńbọ láti gbaradì fún ìpàdé ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì Kim-Trump kan.
rows.output: Pompeo is planning to visit Pyongyang next month to prepare for a second meeting between Kim and Trump.
rows.reference: Pompeo is planning to visit Pyongyang next month to prepare for a second Kim-Trump summit.

rows.source: Àfihàn aṣọ wíwọ̀ ti ìlú Paris fi ìlà àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀jáde tuntun ninu nǹkan àwọ̀sóri tópọlọ́kan lójú ọ̀nà rẹ̀ sí Òpópónà High nítòsí rẹ.
rows.output: The fashion show of the city of Paris presented a new trend in the world of fashion, which is a long, flowing dress that is perfect for the streets near the High Street.
rows.reference: Paris fashion shows reveal latest line in massive headwear on it's way to a High Street near you

rows.source: Bí o báfẹ́ mú ìgbéga bá àkójọpọ̀ ate-orí rẹ tàbí kí o dínàmọ́ òòrùn náà pátápátá máṣe wá a lọ síwájú mọ́.
rows.output: If you want to add a touch of elegance to your outfit or simply brighten up your day, don't hesitate to come along.
rows.reference: If you want to upsize your hat collection or completely block out the sun then look no further.

rows.source: Àwọn aránsọ Valentino àti Thom Browne sị́́ óju àkójọpọ àwọn asọ wíwọ̀ orí wọn eyiti o bùyààri fún àkójọpọ̀ SS19 wọn lójú ọ̀nà-eré náà eyiti o ta àkojọpọ̀ irúfẹ́ wọn yọ níbi Ọ̀sẹ̀ Àfihàn Asọ ní Ìlú Paris.
rows.output: Valentino and Thom Browne's runway collections for SS19 were inspired by the sportswear trend, which was showcased at the Paris Fashion Week.
rows.reference: Designers Valentino and Thom Browne unveiled an array of wacky oversized head gear for their SS19 collection on the runway which dazzled the style set at Paris Fashion Week.

rows.source: Àwọn ate-ori tí kòṣeé lò lọ́nà tóga ti gba Instagram pátá nígbà ooru yìí ti àwọn aránsọ wọ̀nyí sì ti fi àwọn ìṣẹ̀dá wọn tó ńṣẹ́jú síni ránṣẹ́ sí ìsàlẹ̀ àwọn ọ̀nà tóóró náa.
rows.output: The trend of using long, flowing hairstyles has taken Instagram by storm this summer, and these young women have sent their creations down the catwalk.
rows.reference: Highly impractical hats have swept Instagram this summer and these designers have sent their eye-popping creations down the catwalk.

rows.source: Iṣẹ́ ara-ọ̀tọ̀ kan tótayọ láti ọwọ́ Valentino ni ate aláwọ̀ búráùn tó-ń-fòlókè eyiti wọ́n fi àṣomọ́ tódàbí ìyẹ́ sí etí-òkè rẹ̀ tókún gbogbo orí àwọn àwòṣe náà.
rows.output: A perfect example of Valentino's work is the red velvet cake that is topped with a crown of buttercream or ice cream.
rows.reference: The stand out piece by Valentino was an over-the-top beige hat adorned with a feather-like wide brim that swamped the models heads.

rows.source: Àwọn àṣomọ tí ìwọ̀n wọn pọ̀ lápọ̀jù ní àwọn ẹ̀gúsí-olómi tíwọ́n ṣe lọ́ọ̀ṣọ́, ate-orí oṣó kan àti ọ̀pọ̀n-òyìnbó kan - ṣùgbọ́n wọn kò rán wọn láti jẹ́kí ori rẹ móooru.
rows.output: The most prominent of these are the two bronze statues, a priest's head and a female head - but they were not made to be mobile.
rows.reference: Other over-sized accessories included bejeweled watermelons, a wizard hat and even a pineapple - but they are not designed to keep your head warm.

rows.source: Thom Browne tún ṣàfihàn àṣàyan ti àwọn ìbòjú tókọyìnsáyé - tíwọn sí dé láàkókò tóyẹ fún àjọdún Halloween.
rows.output: Thom Browne also presented a collection of oversized, exaggeratedly shaped sunglasses - perfect for the Halloween party.
rows.reference: Thom Browne also revealed a selection of bizarre masks- and just in time for Halloween.

rows.source: Púpọ̀ ninu àwọn ìbòjú náà niwọ́n rán àwọn ètè wọn pa ti wọ́n sì jọ Olóri-ogun Hannibal Lecter ju àwọn asọ tó ńgbayì lóde ìwòyí lọ.
rows.output: Most of the masks were so realistic that they were even more terrifying than the real-life cannibalistic serial killer, Hannibal Lecter.
rows.reference: Many of the colourful masks had sewn up lips and resembled more like Hannibal Lecter than haute couture.

rows.source: Ìṣẹdá kan jọ àwọn asọ ẹ̀rọ ìbẹ́lumi tí ó pé pẹ̀lu ẹ̀rọ amúnimílábẹ-omi àti àwọn awò ojú, nigbati òmíràn wò bíi òkòtó ohun mímu aládùn dídì bíi yìnyín tóti yo.
rows.output: A creation that combines a beverage cooler with a smart display and a camera, while others look like a sleek, modern, and transparent glass of wine.
rows.reference: One creation resembled scuba diving gear complete with snorkel and goggles, while another looked like a melted ice cream cone.

rows.source: Àtipé bí ó bá tẹ̀síwájú pẹ̀lú gbólóhùn asọ ìgbàlódé tó gbòòrò náà- ó ṣe oríire.
rows.output: If he continues with the long, modern sentence - he is lucky.
rows.reference: And if you continue the huge fashion statement- you are in luck.

rows.source: Àwọn olùwòran àrà sọtẹ́lẹ̀ wipe àwọn ate-ori títóbi tíwọn ńsomó àgbọ̀n náà leè máa wá ọ̀nà wọn dé àwọn òpópónà ńlá nítòsí rẹ̀.
rows.output: The astronomers predict that the large asteroid will come close to Earth.
rows.reference: Style watchers predict that the enormous bonnets could be making their way to high streets near you.

rows.source: Àwọn ate-ori oníwọn-ńlá náà dé ní yàjóyàjó lẹ́yìn gìgìrísẹ̀ ti 'La Bomba', ate-ori tíwọn fi ìko hun pẹ̀lú etí oníwọn ẹsẹ̀ bàtà méjì ní fífẹ̀ eyiti wọ́n ńrí lórí gbogbo eniyan láti orí Rihanna dé Emily Ratajkowski.
rows.output: The oversized hats arrived in a flurry of excitement after the performance of 'La Bomba', a hat made of feathers and two-inch heels that were worn by everyone from Rihanna to Emily Ratajkowski.
rows.reference: The out-sized hats come hot on the heels of 'La Bomba', the straw hat with a two-foot wide brim that's been seen on everyone from Rihanna to Emily Ratajkowski.

rows.source: Àlẹ̀mọ́ ẹ̀ṣìn náà tówà lẹ́yìn ate-ori tóṣòro láti lò  tíwọ́n fọ́n káàkiri ojú-òpò ìbáṣepọ̀ ayelujara fi ìṣẹ̀dá ńlá miran rańṣẹ́ sísàlẹ̀ ojú ìrìn náá - àpò etíkun tíwọ́n fi ìko hun tí ó fẹ́rẹ̀ tóbi tó asọ ìwẹ̀lódò àwòṣe náà tí ó kó o jọ papọ̀.
rows.output: The religious leader followed a difficult path to master the art of using the internet to spread a new creation - a large, knotted bag that was almost as big as a traditional weaving loom.
rows.reference: The cult label behind the highly impractical hat that was splashed across social media sent another big creation down the catwalk - a straw beach bag almost as big as the swimsuit-clad model toting it.

rows.source: Àpọ raffia aláwọ̀ omi-ọsàn tóti jóna náà, tíwọn fi raffia gbá létí tíwọ́n sì fi awọ funfun kan ṣe ìfàlọ́wọ́ rẹ̀, ni ó dádúró yàtọ̀ níbi àkójọpọ̀ ti Jacquemus' La Riviera SS19 ní Ọ̀sẹ̀ Àfihàn Asọ ní Ìlu Paris.
rows.output: The raffia bag in a soft, ocean blue hue, which was attached to the wrist with raffia and finished with a white tassel, stood out against the backdrop of Jacquemus' La Riviera SS19 collection at the Paris Fashion Week Show.
rows.reference: The burnt orange raffia bag, trimmed with raffia fringing and topped with a white leather handle, was the stand out piece in Jacquemus' La Riviera SS19 collection at Paris Fashion Week.

rows.source: Ìlúmọ̀ọ́ká gbajúmọ̀ afasọdárà Luke Armitage sọ fún FEMAIL: ''Mo ńretí láti rí àwọn ate-ori ńlá àti awọn àpò ìfàlọ́wọ́ etíkun ní òpópónà ńlá fún ìgba ooru tókàn - bí aránsọ náà ti ṣèdá irú ipa títóbi yóò ṣòro láti fóju fo àwọn ìbéèrè fún àwọn àṣomọ́ oníwọ̀n-tópọ̀lápọ̀jù náà.
rows.output: The famous sand dune of Luke Armitage told FEMAIL: "I'm looking forward to seeing the giant sand dunes and beach buckets in the big streets for the next summer - as the impact of the drought will be hard to ignore the demands of the high-end tourists."
rows.reference: Celebrity stylist Luke Armitage told FEMAIL: 'I'm expecting to see large hats and beach bags arrive on the high street for next summer - as the designer has made such a huge impact it would be hard to ignore the demand for the oversized accessories.'

rows.source: John Edward: Àwọn ìmọ̀ èdè jẹ kòṣeémáàní fún àwọn ọmọ ìlú àgbáyé
rows.output: John Edward: Language skills are essential for global citizens
rows.reference: John Edward: Languages skills essential for global citizens

rows.source: Àwọn ilé ìwé olómìnira ti ilẹ̀ Sikọtiland ńsì ríipé àkọsílẹ̀ eyiti o lààmì-laaka wọn ninu ẹ̀kọ́ tótayọ sì wà síbẹ̀, tí èyí sì ńtẹ̀síwájú lọ́dún 2018 pẹ̀lú àkójọpọ̀ àwọn èsì ìdánwò miran, eyiti wọ́n fún lágbára nípa àṣeyọrí ẹnìkọ̀òkan àti alápapọ̀ ninu eré ìdárayá, iṣẹ́-ọwọ́, orin àti àwọn ìdáwọlé àwùjọ.
rows.output: The independent schools of Scitland are also reporting a record number of students enrolled in top-level courses, which continued in 2018 with a collection of other exam results, which were praised for the success of individual and collective students in sports, crafts, music and social activities.
rows.reference: Scotland's independent schools maintain a track record of academic excellence, and this has continued in 2018 with another set of outstanding exam results, which is only strengthened by individual and collective success in sports, art, music and other community endeavours.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lu àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ tíwọ́n tó ẹgbẹ̀rún lọ́nà ọgbọ̀n jákè-jádò Sikọtiland, àwọn ilé ìwé wọ̀nyí, ti igbìmọ̀ ti àwọn Ilé ìwé olómìnira Ilẹ Sikotiland ńṣojú fún. ńgbìyaǹjú láti máa pèsè iṣẹ́ onípele tódára jùlọ fún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àti àwọn òbí wọn.
rows.output: With over 30,000 students from all over Sikotiland, these schools, represented by the Council of Public Schools of Sikotiland, are striving to provide the best possible education for students and their parents.
rows.reference: With upwards of 30,000 pupils across Scotland, these schools, represented by The Scottish Council of Independent Schools (SCIS), strive to deliver the best level of service to their pupils and parents.

rows.source: Àwọn ilé ìwé olómìnira ńlépa láti gba àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ wọn lárádi fún ẹ̀kọ́ tójinlẹ̀ tí o síga síi, iṣẹ́-ìṣe tíwọ́n yàn láàyò àti ipò wọn gẹ̵́gẹ́bí ọmọ ìlú àgbáyé.
rows.output: Libraries are working to provide their students with a more comprehensive education, including the skills they choose and their position as global citizens.
rows.reference: Independent schools aim to prepare their pupils for further and higher education, their chosen career and their place as global citizens.

rows.source: Bí ẹ̀ka ètò ẹ̀kọ́ kan eyiti ó leè ṣàgbékalẹ̀ ètò tí ó sì leè ṣàmúlò ètò ìkẹkọ̀ọ́ ti ilé ìwé àṣetẹ́ra-ẹnilọ́rùn kan, a ńrí àwọn èdè ọ̀làjù tó ńtẹ̀síwájú bí iṣẹ́ kan tógbajúmọ̀ táyé-ńfẹ́ láàrin àwọn ilé ìwé.
rows.output: As a department of education that can develop and implement a curriculum for a special school, we are seeing the growth of indigenous languages as a significant activity among schools.
rows.reference: As an education sector that can design and implement a bespoke school curriculum, we are seeing modern languages continue as a popular and desired subject of choice within schools.

rows.source: Nelson Mandela sọpé: ''Bí o bá sọ̀rọ̀ sí ọkùnrin kan ní èdè tí ó yé e, ìyẹn yóò wọ inú orí rẹ lọ.
rows.output: Nelson Mandela said: "If you talk to a man in a language he understands, it goes right into his heart.
rows.reference: Nelson Mandela said: "If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head.

rows.source: Bí o bá sọ̀rọ̀ sí i ní èdè tiẹ gan-aṇ̀ ìyẹn yóò wọ inú ọkàn rẹ lọ.''
rows.output: If you speak to her in a language that is not her own, she will not understand you."
rows.reference: If you talk to him in his own language that goes to his heart."

rows.source: Èyí jẹ́ ìránnilétí tólágbára kan wipe a kò kàn leè gbáralé èdé Gẹ́ẹ̀si nigbati a báfẹ ṣàgbéró àwọn ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn eniyan latí àwọn orilẹ-ede miran.
rows.output: This is a powerful reminder that we cannot simply rely on English when we want to communicate with people from other countries.
rows.reference: This is a powerful reminder that we can't just rely on English when wanting to build relationships and trust with people from other countries.

rows.source: Láti àwọn èsì ìdánwò àìpẹ́ ti ọdún yìí, a leè ríi pé àwọn èdè ló ńwà lókè àwọn tábìlì líìgí náà  pẹ̀lú àwọn òdiwọn ìṣọwọ́yege láàrin àwọn ilé ìwé olómìnira.
rows.output: From the latest test results, we can see that languages are on top of the charts with high correlation coefficients between the liberal arts and humanities.
rows.reference: From this year's recent exam results, we can see that languages are topping the league tables with the highest pass rates within independent schools.

rows.source: Àpapọ ìdá méjìdínláàdọrin ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ tí wọ́n kọ́ èdè ilẹ̀ òkèèrè lógba giredi Giga A.
rows.output: 68% of students who study foreign languages are very interested in Giga A.
rows.reference: A total of 68 per cent of pupils who studied foreign languages achieved a Higher grade A.

rows.source: Àkọsilẹ̀ dátà náà, tíwọ́n gbà láti ọwọ́ àwọn ilé ìwé mẹ́rìnléláàádọ́rin tójẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ SCIS fihàn pé ìdá méjìléláàádọ́rin ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ gba giredi A Giga ninu èdè Mandarin, nigbati ìdá méjìléláàádọ́rin ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún ti àwọn tó ńkọ́ èdè Jamani, ìdá mọ́kàndínláàádọ́rin ninu ọgọ́ọ̀rún ti àwọn tó ńkọ́ èdè Faranṣe, àti ìdá mẹ́tàdínláàádọ́rin ninu ọgọ́ọ̀rún ti àwọn tó ńkọ́ èdè Sipeeni bákannáà gba giredi A.
rows.output: The data note, drawn from 74 libraries that are members of SCIS, shows that 73% of students studying Mandarin Chinese, 73% of students studying German, 75% of students studying French, and 74% of students studying Spanish all received an A grade.
rows.reference: The data, collected from SCIS's 74 member schools, showed that 72 per cent of students achieved a Higher grade A in Mandarin, while 72 per cent of those studying German, 69 per cent of those studying French and 63 per cent studying Spanish also achieved an A.

rows.source: Èyì ńfihàn wipe àwọn ilé ìwé olómìnira ní ilẹ Sikọtilandi ńṣàtílẹ́yìn fún àwọn èdè ilẹ̀ òkèèrè gẹ́gẹ́bí àwọn ìmọ̀ tóṣe pàtàkì èyìtí àwọn ọmọdé àti àwọn ọ̀dọ́ yóò nílò láisì àní-àní lọ́jọ́ iwájú.
rows.output: This shows that the independent schools in Scotland are supporting foreign languages as essential knowledge that children and young people will need in the future.
rows.reference: This demonstrates that independent schools in Scotland are supporting foreign languages as vital skills that children and young people will undoubtedly require in the future.

rows.source: Àwọn èdè nísinsìnyí, bí i̇ṣẹ́ yíyàn, niwọ́n ńmú pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ àpọ́nlẹ́ kaǹ gẹ́gẹ́bí àwọn iṣẹ́ STEM (sáyẹ́ńsì, tẹkinọlọji, ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ àti ẹ̀kọ́ ìsiró tójinlẹ̀) ninu àwọn ìlànà ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ti àwọn ilé ìwé olómìnira àti níbiimíràn.
rows.output: Now, the arts, as a STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) subject, are being integrated into the curriculum of both public and private schools.
rows.reference: Languages now, as a subject choice, are being held in the same regard as STEM subjects (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) in independent school curriculums and elsewhere.

rows.source: Ìwáàdí nípa èrò-ọkàn àwọn ènìyàn láti ọwọ Ìgbìmọ̀ Amúṣẹ́ṣe fún Ìgbaniṣíṣẹ́ àti Àwọn Ìmọ̀ lọ́dún 2014 ṣàwárí pé ninu àwọn ìdí tí àwọn agbaniṣ̵íṣẹ́ sọ fún lílàkàkà wọn láti di àwọn ààyè òṣìṣẹ́ tó ṣófo, ìdá mẹ́tàdínlógún ninu ọgọ́ọ̀rún wọn ni wọ́n sọpé ó jẹ́ nitori àìni ìmọ̀ ède miraǹ.
rows.output: The 2014 report by the Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination found that, among the reasons given by workers for their displacement from their jobs, 17 percent cited a lack of proficiency in the dominant language.
rows.reference: A survey by the UK Commission for Employment and Skills in 2014 found that of reasons employers gave for struggling to fill vacancies, 17 per cent were attributed to a languages skills shortage.

rows.source: Nítorínáà púpọ̀̀ àwọn ìmọ̀ èdè níwọ́n ńdi ohun tó ńfẹ̀ àmójútó láti leè gba àwọn ọ̀dọ́ láradì fún àwọn iṣẹ́-ìṣe ọjọ́ iwájú wọn.
rows.output: Therefore, many language learning resources are now focused on preparing students for their future careers.
rows.reference: Therefore more and more, language skills are becoming imperative in order to prepare young people for their future careers.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn àǹfààni iṣẹ̵́ tówà lọ́jọ́ iwájú eyiti wọ́n nílò àwọn èdè, àwọn ìmọ̀ wọ̀nyí jẹ́ kòṣeémáàní ninu ayé tí ìkáwọ́ rẹ̀ ti dọ̀kan yìí.
rows.output: With many future job opportunities that require languages, these skills are essential in this increasingly globalized world.
rows.reference: With more prospective job opportunities requiring languages, these skills are essential in a globalised world.

rows.source: Láìnífiṣe irú iṣẹ́-ìṣe ti ẹnìkan yàn, bí wọ́n báti kọ́ èdè keji, wọn yóò ní àǹfààní gidi kan ní ọjọ́ iwájú náà pẹ̀lú níní ìmọ̀́ irú èyí.
rows.output: Without the type of work that one is assigned, if they are able to learn a second language, they will have a real advantage in the future with having knowledge of this type.
rows.reference: Regardless of the career someone chooses, if they've learned a second language, they'll have a real advantage in the future having a life-long skill such as this.
