rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlọ́gọ́ta nínú àwọn tí ó lè dìbò ló sọ pé kí amòfin náà má díje gẹ́gẹ́ bí Suffolk University Political Research Ceenter àti Boston Globe poll ṣe fi hàn.

rows.output: The referendum showed that the local people supported the former Governor Deval Patrick when two-thirds of the vote favored his candidacy, and two-thirds opposed him.
rows.reference: The poll showed more support for a run by former Governor Deval Patrick, with 38 percent supporting a potential run and 48 percent against it.

rows.source: Níbi ìwọ́de fún Donald Trump ní ìlú Tulsa, Oklahoma ni Sarah Palin rí sọ fún àwọn èrò pé “Mo mọ̀ pé ohun tí ọmọ mi ń là kọjá jẹ́ ohun kan náà tí àwọn ìdílé mìíràn là kọjá látàrí ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí àwọn ọmọ wa lójú ogun“
rows.output: At the rally for Donald Trump in Tulsa, Oklahoma, Sarah Palin told the audience, "I know that what my son is going through is the same thing that other families are going through because of what happened to our children in the war."
rows.reference: "What my own son is going through, what he is going through coming back, I can relate to other families who feel ramifications of PTSD and some of the woundedness that our soldiers do return with," she told the audience at a rally for Donald Trump in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

rows.source: Palin ṣàlàyé pé ohun ìtìjú ni mímú tí àwọn agbófinró mú ọmọ òun àti àwọn ọmọ ogun mìíràn. Ó tẹ̀síwájú pé àwọn ọmọ ogun máa ń padà wálé ní àrà ọ̀tọ̀ pẹ̀lú ojúúwòye mìíràn, ìbéèrè tó sì ń sọ sí gbogbo wọn lọ́kàn ni pé ṣe èrè tí ó tọ́ sí àwọn ọmọ ogun tí wọ́n ti farajìn fún orílẹ̀èdè wọn nìyí."
rows.output: Palin explained that it was a shock to be arrested by police and military personnel. He continued that soldiers would often return home in a state of shock with a different perspective, and the question that was on everyone's mind was whether the reward was worth it for the soldiers who had risked their lives for their country.
rows.reference: Palin called his arrest "the elephant in the room" and said of her son and other war veterans, "they come back a bit different, they come back hardened, they come back wondering if there is that respect for what it is that their fellow soldiers and airmen, and every other member of the military, has given to the country."

rows.source: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí Dan Bennett, agbẹnusọ fún àjọ ọlọ́pàá mí Wasilla ṣe sọ, Ọjọ ẹtì ni àwọn agbófinró mú Track ní ìlú Wasilla, Alaska, wọ́n sì fẹ̀sùn kàn án pé ò na obìnrin, ó tún wà pẹ̀lú ohun èlò ìjà ní ipò ẹni ti ó ti mú ọtí yó.

rows.output: Twenty states, including DC, signed a letter to oppose the new law on immigration to the US.

rows.output: Twenty-six states and the District of Columbia are leading the way in enforcing the new U.S. immigration law, after rejecting sanctuary for groups that are being persecuted or discriminated against inside the country.
rows.reference: Eighteen states and the District of Columbia are supporting a legal challenge to a new U.S. policy that denies asylum to victims fleeing gang or domestic violence.

rows.output: The full name of the case is Grace v. The ACLU's amicus brief, filed in court in August, has not yet been made public.
rows.reference: The full name of the plaintiff in the Grace v. Sessions suit that the American Civil Liberties Union filed in August against the federal policy has not been revealed.

rows.source: Grace sọ pé olólùfẹ́ rẹ pẹ̀lú àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ oníjàgídíjàgan rẹ̀ ṣe ìpalára fún òun ṣùgbọ́n àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ orílẹ̀èdè US tako sísálọ òun lọ orílẹ̀èdè náà.
rows.output: Grace said that her lover and his militant group harmed her but the US government opposed her leaving the country.

rows.output: The government lawyers representing Grace said that El Salvador, Honduras, and Guatemala, which are countries facing a high level of violence and internal conflict due to a large number of people fleeing for safety in the US, are involved in the case.
rows.reference: The states' attorneys supporting Grace described El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala, which produce a large number of applicants for U.S. asylum, as nations facing pervasive problems with gangs and domestic violence.

rows.source: Òfin titun tí US ní lórí àwọn tó ń wá ààbò ṣe jẹ́ àtúnṣe sí ipinnu ọdún 2014 tí ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn aṣíkiri tí ó gba àwọn aṣíkiri tí kò ní ìwé láyè láti bèèrè fún ààbò ní orílẹ̀èdè US.
rows.output: The new US law on asylum seekers is an update to the 2014 ruling by the Board of Immigration Appeals that allowed asylum seekers who lack documentation to request asylum in the US.

rows.source: Agbẹjọ́rò àgbà fún District of Columbia ṣàlàyé lọ́jọ Ẹtì pé ètò àmúlò titun yìí yẹ̀ba kúrò lára ofin tí àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ àti orílẹ̀èdè ti ń ṣàmúlò fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọdún sẹ́yìn."
rows.output: The chief prosecutor for the District of Columbia explained on Thursday that this new method of execution is exempt from the laws that states and countries have been using for decades.

rows.source: "Ọ̀rẹ́ ilé ẹjọ́ kan sọ pé òfin ìjọba gbogbogbò là á kalẹ̀ pé kí a dájọ́ àwọn tó ń wá ààbò lórí òótọ́ àti àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó rọ̀gbà yí irúfẹ́ ẹjọ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ká.
rows.output: A friend of the court stated that the government's law stipulated that those seeking asylum should be judged on the truth and the circumstances of their case.
rows.reference: "Federal law requires that all asylum claims be adjudicated on the particular facts and circumstances of the claim, and such a bar violates that principle," the friend-of-the court brief said.

rows.source: Àwọn agbẹjọ́rò túbọ̀ wòye pé ètò àmúlò titun yìí ń mú ìpalára bá ètò ọrọ̀ ajé orílẹ̀èdè US nítorí àwọn tó ń wá ààbò yìí sábà máa ń di oníṣòwò àti òṣìṣẹ́ tí ìlú nílò."
rows.output: Some lawyers argue that this new system is detrimental to the US economy because those seeking this protection often become entrepreneurs and employees that the city needs.
rows.reference: Attorneys further argued in the brief that the policy denying immigrants entry hurts the U.S. economy, saying they are more likely to become entrepreneurs and "supply necessary labor."

rows.source: Amòfin àgbà fún ìjọba Jeff Sessions ní oṣù kẹfà pàṣẹ kí àwọn adájọ́ tó ń rí ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn aṣíkiri má ṣe fún àwọn aṣíkiri náà ni àyè láti fi orílẹ̀èdè US ṣe ibùgbé.
rows.output: Attorney General Jeff Sessions ordered immigration judges in June to stop granting asylum to immigrants who cross the border.
rows.reference: Attorney General Jeff Sessions ordered immigration judges to no longer grant asylum to victims fleeing domestic abuse and gang violence in June.

rows.source: “Àyè wà fún àwọn tó fi ìlú wọn sílẹ̀ nítorí ìyà àìtọ́ bóyá lórí ẹ̀yà, ẹ̀sìn, orílẹ̀èdè tí ènìyàn ti wá, ẹgbẹ́ tí ènìyàn ń ṣe tàbí ojúùwoye ènìyàn nípa ìṣèlú” Sessions sọ èyí nínú ìkéde ètò àmúlò ní ọjọ́ kọọkànlá, oṣù kẹfà.
rows.output: "There is a place for those who have left their country due to political persecution, whether on the basis of race, religion, the country of origin, the group one belongs to, or one's political views," Sessions said in a statement of purpose on June 11.
rows.reference: "Asylum is available for those who leave their home country because of persecution or fear on account of race, religion, nationality, or membership in a particular social group or political opinion," Sessions said in his June 11 announcement of the policy.

rows.source: Sísá kiri fún ààbò kò lè tán gbogbo ìṣòro -- kódà gbogbo ìṣòro tí ó kẹnú -- tí àwọn ènìyàn ń là kọjá lójoojúmọ́ kaakiri agbàayé.
rows.output: Surfing for safety cannot solve all problems - even all problems that are insurmountable - that people pass through every day all over the world.

rows.output: The water is crystal clear."

rows.output: We saw the residents returning to their damaged homes to gather whatever they could find in their debris.

rows.source: Ọ̀gọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn ló farapa nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ilẹ̀ mímì tí agbára rẹ̀ tó 7.5
rows.output: At least 7.5 million people were injured in the earthquake.

rows.output: Some of the victims in this incident, which Dwi Harris, who is still active, shot in the back, are resting in front of Palu's Army Hospital, where patients are receiving treatment.

rows.output: With tears, Dwi recounted the earthquake that shook her, her daughter, and her husband, leaving them homeless in a hotel.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba US ní orílẹ̀èdè China fẹ̀sùn kan orílẹ̀èdè náà pé ó ń ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn pẹ̀lú pípolówó ẹ̀tàn.
rows.output: The US representative in China accused the country of undermining other countries with fraudulent currency.
rows.reference: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan tí ìwé ìròyìn fún ìjọba China gbé ìròyìn olójúùwé mẹ́rin kan jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn kan ní US. Ìròyìn náà ṣe àtòólẹ̀ àǹfààní tó wà láàrin òwò láàrin China àti US, èyí tí aṣojú ìjọba náà na ìka àbùkù kan China pé ó ń fi àwọn ìwé ìròyìn orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà tan àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: After a week of media coverage in China, a report by the US-based newspaper revealed the advantages of trade between China and the US, which the Chinese government criticized as a smear campaign by the American media.
rows.reference: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.

rows.source: U.S. Ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè U.S. Donald Trump ní Ọjọ́rú tó kọjá tọ́ka sí ìròyìn tí China gbé jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register- ilé-iṣẹ́ ìwé ìròyìn tí ń tà jùlọ ní ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa fẹ̀sùn kan China pé ó ń gbìyànjú láti dásí ètò ìdìbò ilé fún ilé amòfin tí yóò wáyé ní ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá. Orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ pé àwọn kò mọwọ́-mẹsẹ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà.
rows.output: On December 3, U.S. President Donald Trump pointed to a report from China's state-run newspaper, the Des Moines Register, which is the largest newspaper in Iowa, accusing China of attempting to influence the upcoming midterm elections. China has denied the allegations.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ibu ẹnu atẹlu Trump ti Beijing n gbiyanju lati dasi ninu idibo U.S saami si ohun ti awọn osisẹ U.S sọ fun Reuters jẹ ipele tuntun ninu irusoke ipolongo ibo lọdọ Washington lati funmọ China.
rows.output: Trump's trade war with Beijing is trying to interfere in the U.S. election, which is seen as a new level of escalation in the trade war between Washington and Beijing, according to Reuters.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ kìí ṣe ohun àràmọ̀ndà kí àwọn ìjọba òkèèrè ṣe ìpolówó fún ìlọsíwájú ọrọ̀ ajé, rògbòdìyàn nípa ọrọ̀ ajé wà láàrin Beijing ati Washington, èyí tí ó sì fà á kí àwọn méjèèjì gbé owó lórí àwọn ọjà tí ó ń wọlé láti orílẹ̀èdè kejì.
rows.output: While it is not a trade war per se that foreign governments have promoted, there is a trade dispute between Beijing and Washington, which has led both sides to impose tariffs on imports from the other country.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ lórílèedè U.S. wòye pé China ṣe àfikún owó lè ọjà tó ń wọlé sí U.S. láti orílẹ̀èdè China pàápàá jùlọ ní àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bíi Iowa tí ó gbárùkù Trump àti ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú rẹ̀.
rows.output: U.S. officials believe that China is adding to its trade surplus with the U.S. particularly in states like Iowa that are crucial to Trump and his party.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba U.S. ni China àti Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ rí fún ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa, ẹni tí ó ń ta ohun ògbìn sí China jù, Terry Branstad sọ pé China ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, okoòwò àti àgbẹ̀ nílẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: The U.S. Ambassador to China and former Governor of Iowa, who has sold the most corn to China, Terry Branstad, said that China has harmed American workers, businesses and farmers.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: Branstad wòye nínú ìwé tí ó kọ sínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register ní ọjọ́ Àìkú pé China ti sa gbogbo ipa wọn láti ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn nínú àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn ní Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: Branstad wrote in an op-ed in the Des Moines Register on Monday that China has completely lost its influence to promote propaganda in American media.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: "Ìjọba China ń ṣe àmúlò ètò ìròyìn tí kò ní ìpalára láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba tí ó wà ní Amẹ́ríkà láti sanwó ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn àti irọ́ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register,” ni ohun tí Branstad kọ.
rows.output: "The Chinese government is implementing a non-toxic information system from the American government to pay for propaganda and lies in the Des Moines Register newspaper," wrote Branstad.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: "Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé “Lódì kejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí àwọn alátakò tàbí ààfihàn èrò àwọn ará China lórí irúfẹ́ ọwọ́ ti ìjọba fi mú ètò ọrọ̀ ajé. Èyí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí abẹ́ ìṣàkóso ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Chinese Communist Party ni àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn wà.
rows.output: It also continued to say that "The second wave of the epidemic, did not allow for any criticism or expression of the Chinese people's views on the government's handling of the economy. This was because the Chinese Communist Party's control extended to the media outlets.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ó tún fikún un pé ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ògbóntarìgì ilé ìwé ìròyìn ní orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ láti tẹ iṣẹ́ òun sínú ìwé ìròyìn wọn bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé Branstad kò dárúkọ ìwé ìròyìn náà ní pàtó.
rows.output: He also added that one of the state-run news media outlets in China published an article detailing his work, even though Branstad did not mention the news outlet specifically.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì ń ya àwọn obìnrin kúrò pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ Kavanaugh, Àwọn Onímọ̀ kìlọ̀
rows.output: The Republican Party is splitting women from the issue of Kavanaugh, the experts warn
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbà ọ̀jẹ̀ olóṣèlú ẹgbẹ́ republican ṣe ń gbárùkù ẹni tí wọ́n yàn ní ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀, àwọn onímọ̀ tí ń kìlọ̀ pé ọ̀rọ̀ yìí yóò lẹ́yìn pàápàá jùlọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn obìnrin nínú ètò ìdìbò áàrin táàmù.
rows.output: With so many Republican elders endorsing the Supreme Court nominee with a long list of allegations of sexual misconduct, experts warn that this issue will especially hurt women in the midterms.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti fa ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀pọ̀ rúkèrúdò, àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sì ń takú àwọn yóò tún dìbò fún àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn.
rows.output: The issue has caused a lot of controversy, and Republican lawmakers are pressuring their members to vote for their candidates.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú ní Maxwell School tí ó wà ní Yunifásítì Syracuse Grant Reheer ṣọ fún àwọn ìwé ìròyìn The Hill lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta pé ọ̀rọ̀ náà yóò lẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Professor of political science at the Maxwell School at Syracuse University Grant Reeher spoke to the media on Thursday that the story would follow.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reheer sọ pé òun kò rò bóyá ìgbésẹ̀ tí Amòfin Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) nípa pípè àjọ FBI láti wá ṣe ìwádìí àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanaugh yóò tó láti pẹ̀tù sọ́kàn àwọn olùdìbò tí inú ń bí lọ́wọ́ lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: Reheer said he didn't know whether the action of Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) in calling the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh would be enough to satisfy the voters who were so deeply concerned about the issue.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: "“Àwọn obìnrin ò ní gbàgbé ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àná, wọn kò ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ lónìí, wọn kò sì ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ nínú ètò ìdìbò tí yóò wáyé ní oṣù kọọkànlá” ni ohun tí Karine Jean-Pierre, olùbádámọ̀ràn àgbà àti agbẹnusọ gbogbo fún ẹgbẹ́ MoveOn sọ lọ́jọ Ẹtì, èyí tí ó sì jẹyọ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened today, they will not forget it today, and they will not forget it in the election that will take place in November" said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, in a statement on Thursday, which was published in the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: Oṣù kọọkànlá ń bọ̀! Ní ohun tí àwọn afẹ̀hónúhàn ń ké bí wọ́n ṣe fi ìtaara wọn hàn ní ilé Aṣòfin pẹ̀lú bí àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì tí ó wà ní ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń ṣàkóso ọ̀rọ̀ ilé ẹjọ́ ṣe ń tẹ̀síwájú láti yan Kavanaugh sípò. The Mic jẹ́ kí ó yé wa pé èyí wáyé lẹ́yìn ẹ̀rí dọ́kítà Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic ní ó ń jọ́bọ̀ ìròyìn.
rows.output: November is coming! The irony of the Democrats' witness testimony in the Senate with the Republican-controlled Judiciary Committee's continued push to confirm Kavanaugh is striking. The Mic highlights this irony after the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reports, is a survivor of sexual assault.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: Onímọ̀ ìṣèlú Stu Rothenberg sọ “Ìmọ̀sílára kò ní í sí lára àwọn ènìyàn, èyí yóò sì mú wọn dìbò”
rows.output: Political scientist Stu Rothenberg said "The public is not paying attention, and that will cost them"
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: Àwọn ènìyàn tilẹ̀ ti ń sọ pé àwọn kò lè dúró kí ọjọ́ ìdìbò dé.
rows.output: People have been saying that they can't wait until the election day.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Ó ṣeéṣe kí ìmọ̀sílára pọ̀ sí pàápàá jùlọ láàrin àwọn obìnrin tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko àti àwọn ọmọbìnrin láàrin ọmọ ọdún méjìdínlógún sí óòkandínlọ́gbọ̀n tí wọ́n ò nífẹ̀ẹ́ ààrẹ, síbẹ̀ tí wọ́n kìí dìbò.”
rows.output: It is possible that the sense of alienation will increase particularly among women in the countryside and among girls between the ages of 15 and 29 who do not like the president, even though they do not vote.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Kí Ford tó jẹ́rìí ní gbangba nípa ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀ tí ó fi kan Kavanaugh ni àwọn onímọ̀ ti ń kìlọ̀ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí yíyan Kavanaugh sípò bu ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: Before Ford's allegations of sexual assault against Kavanaugh were confirmed, some experts warned that his appointment to the Supreme Court could be a boon to the Republican Party.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti dá yánpọyánrin kalẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ wa” ni ohun tí Michael Steele tí ó fìgbà kan jẹ́ alága fún ìgbìmọ̀ gbogbogbò ní ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sọ ní ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "This phrase has been used to whip up a frenzy in our ranks" is what Michael Steele, the former chairman of the Republican National Committee, said last week as NBC News reported.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí kìí ṣe nípa bóyá àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì yan Kavanaugh sípò nìkan, ó tún nííṣe pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì fi mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà àti ọwọ́ tí wọ́n fi mú Ford” Olùdarí ẹgbẹ́ tó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Dẹ́mókírààtì Priorities USA, Guy Cecil ló sọ èyí fún ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn náà.
rows.output: "This is not just about whether Republican voters chose Kavanaugh, but also about the hands that the Republican Party put on the issue and the hands that they put on Ford," said Guy Cecil, the manager of the Democratic Priorities USA, in an interview with the news organization.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀, èrò àwọn ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà pín sí méjì lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú bí wọn kò mọ ẹni tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbàgbọ́ nínú Kavanaugh àti Ford.
rows.output: However, American public opinion is divided on the issue, with people unsure of who to believe in Kavanaugh and Ford.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Ìdìbò afèròhàn tí YouGov gbé kalẹ̀ fi hàn pé ìdá mọ́kànlelógoji nínú àwọn tó kópa nínú ètò ìdìbò náà sọ pé àwọn gba Ford gbọ́ nígbà tí ìdá márùndínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn gba Kavanaugh gbọ́.
rows.output: The YouGov poll found that 49% of respondents said they trust Ford, while 45% said they trust Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Kavanaugh ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ nígbà tí ìdá ọgbọ̀n ló gbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Ford ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí tirẹ̀ bákan náà.
rows.output: 48 percent said they believed Kavanaugh was lying in his testimony, while 30 percent said they believed Ford was lying in her testimony.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: The Guardian ròyìn pé lẹ́yìn tí amòfin Flake ké sí àjọ FBI, ìwádìí ti ń lọ lọ́wọ́ lórí ẹ̀sùn tí Ford and afẹ̀sùkan mìíràn Deborah Ramírez fi kan Kavanaugh.
rows.output: The Guardian reported that after Flake's request to the FBI, the investigation was continuing into the allegations against Ford and another accuser, Deborah Ramirez.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford jẹ́rìí níwájú ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ilé ẹjọ́ nílé Aṣòfin pé Kavanaugh mú ọtí yó, ó sì fipá bá òun lòpọ̀ nígbà tí òun pé ọmọ ọdún mẹ́tàdínlógún.
rows.output: Ford testified before the Senate committee that Kavanaugh had sexually assaulted her when she was 15 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez ṣàlàyé pé Kavanaugh ṣí nǹkan ọmọkùnrin rẹ̀ fún òun láti rí nígbà tí wọ́n ń dìjọ kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní Yale. Èyí ṣẹlẹ̀ ni patí kan tí wọ́n lọ láàrin ọdún 1980 síwájú sí i.
rows.output: Ramirez explained that Kavanaugh opened a package of his son's to look at while they were studying at Yale. This happened in a year between 1980.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Olùdásílẹ Ìtàkùǹ Àyélujára ń gbèrò láti Bẹ̀rẹ̀ Íntánẹ̀ẹ̀tì Tuntun kan láti lé Mú Google àti Facebook
rows.output: The founder of the Internet Archive is planning to launch a new Internet to replace Google and Facebook.
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, olùdásílẹ̀ Ìtàkùn ayélujára, ń ṣe ifilọ́lẹ̀ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ kan tí ó máa jẹ́ orogún pẹ̀lú Facebook, Amazon àti Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a new initiative that will be a competitor to Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Iṣẹ́ àkànṣe Ògbóǹtarìgì onímọ̀ ẹ̀rọ, Inrupt, jẹ́ ilé iṣẹ́ tí ó dúró lórí i orísun ìpìlẹ̀ iṣẹ́ Berners-Lee.
rows.output: The World Wide Web project, Inrupt, is a company based on the original source code of the World Wide Web by Tim Berners-Lee.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid fààyè gba àwọn aṣàmúlò láti yan ibi tí dátà wọn yóò di fífipamọ́ sí àti àwọn ènìyàn wo ní wọ́n le ráyè sí àti irú ìwífún tí wọ́n le ráyè sí.
rows.output: Solid fààdé gba àwọn aṣàmùlò láti yan ibi tí dátà wọn yóò di fífipamọ́ sí àti àwọn ènìyàn wo ní wọ́n le ráyè sí àti irú ìwífún tí wọ́n le ráyè sí.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: Nínú ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹ́nuwò pẹ́lú ilé iṣẹ́ Fast, Berners-Lee ṣàwàdà pé èròńgbà lẹ́yìn Inrupt ni láti le “jẹ gàba lórí ayé.”
rows.output: In an interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee described the vision behind Inrupt as being to "bring the web back to the people."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe báyìí," ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ náà.
rows.output: "We must do this now," he said, regarding the start.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: "Ó jẹ́ àkókò onítàn."
rows.output: "It is a time of stories."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ìṣàfilọ́̀lẹ̀ náà ń lo ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ Solid láti fààyègba àwọn ènìyàn láti ṣẹ̀dá “ilé ìtàjà dátà adáni lórí ayélujára” tàbí POD.
rows.output: The project uses Solid's technology to empower people to create their own "personal data stores on the web" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ó le ní àwọn àtòkọ olùbásọ̀rọ̀, ohun-àti-ṣe, kàlẹ́ńdà, ibi ìpamọ́ orin àti àwọn irinṣẹ́ àdáni àti àfyṣiṣẹ́ mìràn.
rows.output: It may have contact lists, to-do lists, calendars, music storage, and other custom and third-party tools.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ó dábí Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack àti Spotify tí gbogbo wọ́n wà nílẹ̀ lórí aṣawákiri ní àṣìkò kannáà.
rows.output: He opened Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify, all of which were available on the browser at the time.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dá yàtọ̀ nípa ilé ìtàjà dátà àdáni ayelujára pé aṣàmúlò ló kù sí lọ́wọ́ láti mọ ẹni tí ó le ráyèsí àti irú ìwífún tó le ráyèsí.
rows.output: The unique thing about the online data center is that the software is responsible for determining who can access and what type of information can be accessed.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ pè ní “Ìrónilágbára àdáni nípaṣẹ̀ dátà.”
rows.output: The company is called "Personal Data Power."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Èròńgbà fún Inrupt, gẹ́gẹ́bí Olùdásílẹ̀ ilé iṣẹ́ náà John Bruce ṣe sọ, ni pé ó wá fún ilé iṣẹ̀ láti mú àwọn ohun àmúlò, ìlànà àti àwọn ọgbọ́n àtinúdá láti ṣèrànwọ́ láti mú kí Solid wà nílẹ̀ fún gbogbo ènìyàn.
rows.output: The vision for Inrupt, as stated by the company's founder John Bruce, was to bring a suite of tools, processes, and methodologies to bear to help make Solid a reality for everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ náà ní Berners-Lee, Bruce, ètò ìpèsè ààbò tí IBM rà, àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ fúngbàdíẹ̀ tí wọ́n gbà láti ṣiṣẹ́ lórí iṣẹ́ àkànṣe náà, àti àwùjọ àwọn akọkóòdù tí wọ́n jẹ́ olùfarajìn.
rows.output: The project was funded by IBM, and included Tim Berners-Lee, a contract programmer, and a few other employees who were taken on to work on the project, and a community of volunteers who were enthusiastic about the project.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí inú rẹ̀ ṣe dùn lórí i bí àwọn elére ìdárayá rẹ̀ ṣe fakọyọ sí lórí pápá gọ́ọ̀fù, Bjorn ṣàláyè sí wípé: "Èmi kò ní síwájú ara mi lórí eléyìí.
rows.output: With how much he was enjoying himself as his fellow golfers gathered around the green, Bjorn said: "I'm not going to top that one."
rows.reference: Delighted how his players have performed on a tough golf course, Bjorn added: "I would never get ahead of myself in this.

rows.source: Ohun to yàtọ̀ pátápátá ni ọ̀lá jẹ́.
rows.output: The most important thing is respect.
rows.reference: Tomorrow's a different beast.

rows.source: Ọ̀lá jẹ́ ìṣesí ẹ̀nì kọ̀ọ̀kan to ń farahàn, àtipé èyí jẹ́ ohun ti ó yàtọ̀ gedégbé láti ṣe.
rows.output: Respect is a personal attitude, and this is something that can be learned.
rows.reference: Tomorrow is the individual performances that come forward, and that is a different thing to do.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dára ni láti wà pẹ̀lú enìkan nígbàtí àwọn n[kan bá ńlọ dáradára, ṣùgbọ́n, nígbàtí o ẹ̀nìkọ̀ọ̀kan bá dá wà, nigbànáa ní ìdánwò àdánán máa ṣẹ̀lẹ̀ sí ọ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí eléré ìdárayá gọ́ọ̀fù.
rows.output: It's better to be with someone when they're going well, but when you're both down, then a test of patience often occurs as a golfer.
rows.reference: It's great to be out there with a partner when things are going good, but when you're out there individually, then you're tested to the full of your capacity as a golfer.

rows.source: Ìyẹn ní ìfiránṣẹ́ tí o níláti fi ránṣẹ́ sí àwọn elérée ìdárayá, èyí ní láti mú ohun tó dára jùlọ jáde lára rẹ ní ọ̀la.
rows.output: That is a message that you have to send to the athletes, in order to make the best of you in the future.
rows.reference: That's the message that you need to get across to players, is get the best out of yourself tomorrow.

rows.source: Nísìnyí, o fi ẹnìkejì rẹ sẹ́hìn ó sì níláti lọ mọ́ bí ó sẹ máa mu ohun tó dára jù jáde lát ara rẹ̀, bákan náà."
rows.output: Now, you're putting the other person first and you have to figure out how to get the best out of yourself, too."
rows.reference: Now, you leave your partner behind and he has to go and get the best out of himself, as well."

rows.source: Ní ìdàyàtọ̀ sí Bjorn, opposite number Jim Furyk tí ó jẹ́ nọ́ńbà ìdàkejì máa ma wá àwọn eléré ìdárayá rẹ̀ láti le ní ìṣesí tó dára ní ẹlẹ́nìkọ̀ọ̀kan ju bí wọ́n ṣe ṣe lọ ní aláṣepọ̀, àwọn tó dáyàtọ̀ Jordan Spieth àti Justin Thomas, tí wọ́n ní máàkì mẹ́ta nínú mẹ́rin
rows.output: In contrast to Bjorn, his opposite number Jim Furyk, who is always ranked second, will bring his players to have a better feeling in the individual than in the team, the two who are always together, Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas, who have three of the four majors.
rows.reference: In contrast to Bjorn, opposite number Jim Furyk will be looking for his players to perform better individually than they did as partners, the exceptions being Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas, who picked up three points out of four.

rows.source: Furyk funra ara rẹ ti wà ní apá méjèèjì ibi ti àwọn ọjọ́ tó kẹ́hìn ńlá ti ṣàdédé yípadà, lẹ́yìn tí ó ti jẹ́ ara àwọn alájọṣepọ̀tó tò borí ní kí ó tó parí rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí aláìláṣeyọrí ní Yúrópù mú kí “Ìyànu ńlá ní Mẹ̀dínà” ti ara rẹ̀ jáde.
rows.output: Furyk himself was on both sides of the great change of the last few days, after having been a partner in the most successful European tour before finishing as a loser in "The Great Miracle in Medinah" brought his own "Furyk's Miracle" out.
rows.reference: Furyk himself has been on both ends of those big last-day turnarounds, having been part of the winning team at Brookline before ending up a loser as Europe pulled off the "Miracle at Medinah."

rows.source: “Mo ránti gbogbo gbolohun kọ̀ọ̀kan tó jẹ jáde nínú rẹ̀,” ó sọ̀rọ̀ ní ìfèsì sí ìbéèrè bí Ben Crenshaw, olórí ilé ní 1999, ṣe ṣàtòjọ̀ àwọn eléré ìdárayá rẹ̀ lásìkò ìgbà ìkẹ̀hìn náà.
rows.output: "I remember every word of it," he said in response to a question about how Ben Crenshaw, the 1999 champion, listed his players during the final round.
rows.reference: "I remember every damn word of it," he said in reply to being asked how Ben Crenshaw, the captain in 1999, had rallied his players heading into the last day.

rows.source: "A ní ìfigagbága 12 tó ṣe pàtàkì lóla, ṣùgbọ́n o máa fẹ́ láti tètè dé ibi ìyára bẹ̀rẹ̀ bí i ọ ṣe rí i ní Brookline, bí o ṣe rí i ní Medinah.
rows.output: "We have 12 major tests, but you want to get to the finals as soon as you see them in Brookline, as you see them in Medinah."
rows.reference: "We have 12 important matches tomorrow, but you'd like to get off to that fast start like you saw at Brookline, like you saw at Medinah.

rows.source: Nígbà abala kan bá ń lọ dáadáa, ó máa rán àwon ìfigagbaga ààrín lọ́wọ̀.
rows.output: When a person is in a good mood, they will often be more generous.
rows.reference: When that momentum gets going one way, it puts a lot of pressure on those middle matches.

rows.source: A ṣètò ìtọ̀ gbọorọ̀ wa lórí ìlà lọ́wọ̀ọ̀wọ́ tí a sí mú kí àwọn ẹni tiwa jẹ́ jádení ọ̀nà àrà ọ̀tọ̀ tí ó wù wá, o mọ̀, a ń gbìyànjú láti pidán lọla."
rows.output: We have set our sights on the straight line that we have chosen for ourselves, you know, we are trying to move forward with our lives.
rows.reference: We set up our line-up accordingly and put the guys out in the fashion that we felt like, you know, we're trying to make some magic tomorrow."

rows.source: Thomas ní ó gba iṣẹ́ pàtàkì lórí dídarí ìjagbara àti kíkojú Rory Mcllroy nínú ìfigagbaga to le jù, Pẹ̀lú Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahim, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulte tThomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter tí wọ́n jẹ́ ara Yúrópù núnú ìdámejì ìtòléra láti òkè.
rows.output: Thomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter, who are the European pair, in the second match from the top.
rows.reference: Thomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter the other Europeans in the top half of the order.

rows.source: "Mo ti wà pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀wọ̀ àwọn ẹni wọ̀nyìí nínú ìtòléra yìí nítorípé mo rò pé ó kó àkóyáwọ́,” Bjorn ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa àwọn àkopa ẹlẹ́nìkọ̀ọ̀an rẹ̀.
rows.output: "I've been with these people in this tolerance because I think it's a very important thing," Bjorn said about his teammates.
rows.reference: "I went with this group of guys in this order because I think it covers all the way through," said Bjorn of his singles selections.

rows.source: Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tuntun ti Germany ti di sísún síwájú lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi
rows.output: The new German warship has been launched for the second time
rows.reference: Germany's new warship postponed yet again

rows.source: Àkọ̀tun Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi ti Jámáànù ní ó yẹ kí ó ti di fífi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ọdún 2014 láti pààrọ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi Sáà-ogún Dúkùú, ṣùgbọ́n kò ní rí bẹ́ẹ̀ títí di, ó kéré jù, ọdún í ó ń bọ̀ nítorí àwọn èròjà tó ti bàjẹ̀ àti àwọn ìnáwò tó ti ṣarajọ, ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn abẹ́léni ó jábọ̀ rẹ̀.
rows.output: The German Navy's submarine rescue ship, the "Bergen", was supposed to be decommissioned in 2014 to make way for the new "Baden-Württemberg" class submarines, but it will not be until, at the earliest, next year due to technical problems and high costs, the defense ministry announced.
rows.reference: German Navy's newest frigate should have been commissioned in 2014 to replace ageing Cold War-era warships, but it won't be there until at least the next year due to faulty systems and snowballing cost, local media reported.

rows.source: Síṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ "Rheinland-Pfalz," olórí ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tí ìsọ̀rí fírígéètì Baden-Wuerttemberg tuntun nini, ni ó ti di sísún ṣíwájú títi di ìdájì àkọ́kọ́ ọdún 2019, gẹ́gẹ́bi ìwé ìròyìn Die Zeit ṣe sọ tí ọgá ológun kan sọ.
rows.output: The "Rheinland-Pfalz" ship, which is the first ship of the new Baden-Wuerttemberg class of submarines, has been ahead of schedule until the first half of 2019, according to a report in the newspaper Die Zeit.
rows.reference: Commissioning of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the brand new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates, has now been postponed until the first half of 2019, according to Die Zeit newspaper citing a military spokesman.

rows.source: Ó yẹ kí ọkọ̀ ojú omi nlá náà darapọ̀ ní 2014, ṣùgbọ̀n àwọn wàhálà ìṣòro lẹ́yìn ìfakalẹ̀ rẹ̀ ní ó mú kí ìgbẹ́kẹ́lé nínú itẹ̀síwájú àkànṣe iṣẹ́ náà já sófo.
rows.output: The shipyard was supposed to join the project in 2014, but the problems following its bankruptcy led to a loss of confidence in the continuation of the project.
rows.reference: The vessel should have joined the Navy in 2014, but the troubling post-delivery issues plagued the fate of the ambitious project.

rows.source: Àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá mẹ́rin ti ìsọ̀rí Baden-Wuerttemberg tí Àwọn ọmọ ogún ojú omi sànwó fún ;áti 2007 máa wá gẹ́gẹ́bí arọ́pò sí ìṣọ̀rí àwọn fírígéétì Bremen.
rows.output: Four large patrol ships of the Baden-Wuerttemberg class, which were built for the German Navy, will arrive in 2007 as replacements for the Bremen class frigates.
rows.reference: The four Baden-Wuerttemberg-class vessels the Navy ordered back in 2007 will come as replacement to the ageing Bremen-class frigates.

rows.source: Ó yé wá pé wọ́n máa ṣàfihàn Kanọ́ọ̀nù tó lágbara,ọ̀wọ́ àwọn mísáìlì aṣòdì-sí-bàálù àti aṣòdì-sí-ọkọ̀ orí omi àti àwọn ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ nǹka ìjagun mìíràn, bíi rédà, ínfúrárẹ́ẹ̀dì àti àwọn ìfọ́wọ́sí abáfẹfẹ́ṣiṣẹ́.
rows.output: We also know that they will be able to withstand the impact of a nuclear warhead and other types of conventional weapons, such as rockets, torpedoes, and other underwater weapons.
rows.reference: It is understood they will feature a powerful cannon, an array of anti-aircraft and anti-ship missiles as well as some stealth technologies, such as reduced radar, infrared and acoustic signatures.

rows.source: Àwọn ohun pàtàkì mìràn gẹ́gẹ́bí ìgbà ìṣàbójútó lóòrèkóòrè - p yẹ kó ṣeéṣe láti ṣàfillẹ̀ awọn fírígéètì fún bí ọdún méjì jìnnà sí ìbúdó \kọ ojú omi.
rows.output: Other important factors such as the frequency of the inspections - it should be possible to defrost the refrigerators for at least two years from the port of entry.
rows.reference: Other important features include longer maintenance periods - it should be possible to deploy the newest frigates for up to two years away from home ports.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, ìdádúró gbogbo ìgbà túmọ̀ sí wípé àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ìṣaajú - tí wọn sọ pé ó jẹ́ kí ilẹ̀ jámánì ní agbara ní òkè òkun - ti máa di èyí tí kò bá ìgbà mu mọ́ ní àkókò tí wọ́n bá wọ iṣẹ́. Die Zelt ló pe àkíyèsí yìí.
rows.output: However, the continued presence of the naval blockade - which is said to give Germany control of the seas - would be a constant reminder of the war when they enter the workforce. The Zelt refers to this observation.
rows.reference: However, continuous delays mean that the cutting-edge warships - said to allow Germany to project power overseas - will already become outdated by the time they enter service, Die Zeit notes.

rows.source: Fírígèètì F125 tí ó kùnà náà gba gogbo ìròyìn kan ní ọdún tó kọjá, nígbàtí Àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi kọ̀ jàlẹ̀ láti ṣafilọlẹ̀ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá náà tí wọ́n sì dá a padà sí ìlé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi Blohm & Voss ní Hamburb.
rows.output: The F125-class submarine that failed its trials last year has been the subject of much media coverage, while the Navy has been trying to get the submarine back to the Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.
rows.reference: The ill-fated F125 frigate made headlines last year, when the German Navy officially refused to commission the vessel and returned it to Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.

rows.source: Èyí jẹ ìgbà àkọ́kọ́ tí Àwọn ọ́mọ ogun ojú omi máa dá ọkọ̀ ojú omi padà fún ilé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ṣiṣe lẹ́yìn tí wọn ti fà á kalẹ̀.
rows.output: This is the first time that the Navy SEALs will return a ship to the Navy's shipbuilding program since they were decommissioned.
rows.reference: This was the first time the Navy has returned a ship to a shipbuilder after delivery.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ ní a mọ̀ nípa ìdí tí ọkọ̀ ojú omi náà fi di dídá padà, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn oníwè ìròyìn jámànù sọ díẹ nípa “àṣìṣe sọ́fútìwíà àti hádìwíà” tí ó mú kí ọkọ̀ ìfijagun ojú omi náà má wúlò tí ó bá di lílò ní ojú ogun.
rows.output: Some details are known about the reason for the ship's return, but German newspapers reported on "software and hardware errors" that made the amphibious assault ship useless if it were to be used in war.
rows.reference: Little was known about the reasons behind the return, but German media cited a number of crucial "software and hardware defects" that made the warship useless if deployed on a combat mission.

rows.source: Àìpé sọ́fùtiwìà jẹ́ ohún tí ó ṣe pàtàkì gan nítorí awọn 120 awakọ̀ ojú omi ni wọ́n máa wa ìsọ̀rí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá Baden-Wuerttemberg-class náà - èyí tí ó jẹ́ ìdájí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ nínú àwọn fírígéètì ìsọ̀rí Bremen àtijọ́.
rows.output: The software is important because 120 seafarers will be trained to operate the large Baden-Wuerttemberg-class ferry - which is equivalent to the employment of 2,000 workers in the Bremen shipyard.
rows.reference: Software deficiencies were particularly important as the Baden-Wuerttemberg-class vessels will be operated by a crew of some 120 sailors - just half of the manpower on older Bremen class frigates.

rows.source: Bákan náà, ó ṣelẹ̀ pé ọkọ̀ ojú omi náà ti wúwo ju bí ó ṣe yẹ lọ èyí tí ó ṣàdínkù ìṣesí rẹ̀ tí ó sì mú ìdópín bá ìpa Àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi láti ṣàlékún àmúdágbà ọjọ́ iwájú.
rows.output: At the same time, the ship was too heavy for its size, which reduced its maneuverability and made it difficult for the Navy to intercept enemy ships.
rows.reference: Also, it emerged that the ship is dramatically overweight which reduces its performance and limits the Navy's ability to add future upgrades.

rows.source: "Rheinland-Pfalz" tó ní ìwọ̀n 7,000-ton ní ìwọ́n rẹ̀ jẹ́ ìlọ́po méjì ní ìwúwo sí ọkọ̀ ojú omi tí ó jẹ́ ìsọ̀rí kannáà tí àwọn Jámànù lò ní Ogun Àgbáyé Kejì..
rows.output: The Rheinland-Pfalz, with a displacement of 7,000 tons, is twice the weight of the aircraft carrier that the Germans used in World War II.
rows.reference: The 7,000-ton "Rheinland-Pfalz" is believed to be twice as heavy as similar-class ships used by the Germans in the Second World War.

rows.source: Yàtọ̀ sí àṣìṣe hádìwià, ìgbówólórí àkànṣe iṣẹ́ náà - pẹ̀lú ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àwọn ọ̀wọ́ òṣìṣẹ - ́ jẹ́ àwọn ohun ìṣòrò.
rows.output: Aside from the technical error, the project's success rate - including the training of workers - is debatable.
rows.reference: Aside from faulty hardware, the price tag of the entire project - including the training of the crew - is also becoming an issue.

rows.source: Wọ́n jẹ́ ká mọ̀ pé ó ti dé €3.1billion ($3.6bn) - sókè láti €2.2 billion ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀.
rows.output: They are now estimated to have reached €3.1 billion ($3.6 billion) - up from €2.2 billion at the start.
rows.reference: It is said to have reached staggering €3.1billion ($3.6bn) - up from initial €2.2 billion.

rows.source: Àwọn ìṣòro tó wà nípa níní àwọn àkọ̀tun fírígèètì ti di ohun tí ó ṣè pàtàkì pàápàá nípaṣẹ̀ àwọn ìkìlọ̀ pé àgbára àwọn ọmọ ogún ojú omi Jámánì tí dín kù.
rows.output: The problems associated with having a fleet of submarines have become particularly important due to warnings about the reduced strength of the German Navy.
rows.reference: Problems gripping the newest frigates become especially of importance in light of recent warnings that Germany's naval power is shrinking.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ọdún yìí, Hans-Peter Bartels, olórí ìgbìmọ̀ ilé aṣòfin ti Jámànù, gbà pé Ilé iṣẹ́ àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi “kò ní àwon ọkọ ìfijagún ojú omi tó tó mọ́.”
rows.output: At the beginning of this year, Hans-Peter Bartels, the leader of the German Bundestag, stated that the Navy "does not have enough patrol ships."
rows.reference: Earlier this year, Hans-Peter Bartels, chief of the German parliament's defense committee, acknowledged the Navy is actually "running out of deployment-capable ships."

rows.source: Òṣìṣẹ́ ìjọba náà sọ wípé ìṣòro náà ti ṣarajọ láti ọ́jọ́ tó ti pẹ́, nítorípé àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi àtijọ́ kò sí fún lílò mọ́ ṣùgbọ́n tí kò sì sí ọ̀kankan àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi tí a le fi rọ́pò wọn.
rows.output: The government official said the problem had been building for years, as old ships were no longer available for use but there were no new ships to replace them.
rows.reference: The official said the issue has snowballed over time, because old ships were decommissioned but no replacement vessels were provided.

rows.source: Ó ké ìbòsí pe kò sí ọ̀kankan àwọn fírígéètì Baden-Wuerttemberg-class tí ó le darapọ̀ mọ́ Ilé iṣẹ́ Ogún ojú omi.
rows.output: It is said that none of the Baden-Wuerttemberg-class submarines can be integrated into the Navy's operational fleet.
rows.reference: He lamented that none of the of the Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates were able to join the Navy.

rows.source: National Trust ń ṣe amí lórí i àṣírí ìgbé ayé àwọn àdán
rows.output: The National Trust is working on a project to protect the privacy of our ancestors' lives.
rows.reference: National Trust eavesdrops on secret life of bats

rows.source: Ìwádìí tuntun ń lọ lọ́wọ́ ní àdúgbọ̀ kan ní Orí òkè Scottish tí àfojúsùn rẹ̀ jẹ́ láti ṣàfihàn bí àwọn àdán ṣe ń lo àgbègbè náà láti ṣàwárí fún oúnjẹ́.
rows.output: New research is underway in a community in the Scottish Highlands with the aim of showing how humans have used the area to find food for thousands of years.
rows.reference: New research being carried out at an estate in the Scottish Highlands aims to reveal how bats use the landscape in their hunt for food.

rows.source: Ìgbàgbọ́ wà pé àbọ̀ ìwádìí náà máa tan ìmọ́lẹ̀ tuntun sí ìhùwàsí àkàndá ẹranko tó ń fò náà tí yóò sì ṣèrànwọ́ ìtasọ́nà fún àwọn iṣẹ́ pípa ẹ̀rankọ̀ mọ́.
rows.output: The belief is that the study will shed new light on the behavior of the migratory bird species and will help in the conservation of endangered species.
rows.reference: It is hoped the findings will shed new light on the behaviour of the unique flying mammals and help guide future conservation activities.

rows.source: Ìwádìí nípaṣẹ̀ àwọn oníṣáyẹ́ǹsì ní Onígbẹkẹ̀lé Orílẹ̀-èdè fún Scotland máa tẹ̀lé soprano pipistrelles àti ẹ̀yà tó wapọ̀ àti bíi ẹ̀yà elétí-gígùn aláwọ̀ búránù àti àwọn àdán Daubenton ní Ọgbà Inverewe ní Wester Ross.
rows.output: Research by scientists at the National Trust for Scotland will follow soprano pipistrelles and the species of Daubenton's bat and Noctule bats in the Inverewe Garden in Wester Ross.

rows.source: Ótún sọ síwájú pé “nípa” pé Toyota UK ti sọ fún BBC pé tí Bírítéénì bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láì ní àdéhùn ìsòwò tó só pọ̀, ó máa ṣe ìdádúró ìgbéjáde-iṣẹ̀ ní ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Burnaston, ní ẹ̀bá Derby.
rows.output: The company also said that "in the event" of a British exit from the EU without a trade agreement, it would halt production at its Burnaston plant, near Derby.
rows.reference: He added it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: "A nílò àdéhùn ìṣòwò,” Ọ̀gbẹ́ni Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement," Mr. Clark said.
rows.reference: "We need a deal," Mr Clark said.

rows.source: Aṣemọ́tò Jàpáàanù sọ pé ipa ààlà máa ṣe ìdádúró tí ó bá lọ jẹ́ pé kò sí àd’hpùn ìṣòwò Brexit lẹ́ mú kí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́ wà.
rows.output: The Japanese government says the impact of the border will be a brake on the economic effects of Brexit, which will lead to a loss of jobs.
rows.reference: The Japanese carmaker said the impact of border delays in the event of a no-deal Brexit could cost jobs.

rows.source: Ẹ̀rọ̀ iṣẹ́ Burnaston - tí ó ń ṣe Toyota Auris àti Avensis - pèsè mọ́tò tó súnmọ́ 150,000 ní ọdún tó kọjá tí ó sì jẹ́ pé 90% ní wọ́n ṣàgbéjáde sí Ìṣọ̀kan Yúròpù tó kù.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant, which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis, produces around 150,000 vehicles a year and exports 90% to the rest of Europe.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: "Ìwòyé mi ni pé tí Bírítéènì ba fi le jáde kúrò ní EU láìròtẹ́lẹ̀ ní òpin oṣù kẹta, ìgbéjáde máa dúró ní ilé iṣẹ́ wa,” Marvi Cooke ni ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, Alákòóso adarí ní Burnaston.
rows.output: "My view is that if Britain leaves the EU unexpectedly in March, production will stop at our plant," said Marvi Cooke, managing director at Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Àwọn aṣemọ́tò UK tí fi ìjayà wọn hàn nípa fífi EU sílẹ̀ láìní àdéhùn lórí bí kíkọjá láàlà òkòwò ṣe máa ṣiṣẹ́, gẹ́gẹ́bí i Honda, BMW àti Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: UK carmakers threaten to halt production if Britain leaves EU without a deal on car trade, as Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, fún àpẹẹrẹ, sọ pé ò máa ti Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ kékeré rẹ̀ ní Oxford fún oṣù kan tí ó tẹ̀lé Brexit.
rows.output: For example, BMW said it would close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month after Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Ohun ìkọminú jùlọ jẹ́mọ́ ohun tí àwọn aṣemọ́tò sọ pé ọ jẹ àwọń èwu ètò ìpèsè tí ó bá ṣẹlẹ̀ pé kò sí àdéhun ìṣòwò Brexit.
rows.output: The most significant thing is what the experts say, that it is a customs union that is the worst scenario of the Brexit deal.
rows.reference: The main concerns relate to what carmakers say are supply chain risks in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: Ìgbéjáde àtòpọ̀ Toyota dá lórí i “tó bá àkókò mu”, pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀yà ara rẹ̀ tí ó ń wọlé ní gbogbo ìṣẹ́jú 37 láti ọ̀dọ̀ olùgbéjáde wọn ní UK àti EU fún àwọn mọ́tò láti tà jáde.
rows.output: The launch of Toyota's new model is based on the principle of "just in time", with its components arriving every 37 seconds from its production plants in the UK and EU for sale.
rows.reference: Toyota's production line is run on a "just-in-time" basis, with parts arriving every 37 minutes from suppliers in both the UK and the EU for cars made to order.

rows.source: Tí UK bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láìsí àdéhùn ìṣòwò ní 29 oṣù kẹta, ìdíwọ́ le wà ní ààlà ibode tí àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ sọ pé o le já sí ìdádúro àti àìnító àwọn ẹ̀yà ara.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a trade deal on 29 March, there could be delays at the border, companies say, which could lead to shortages of parts and products.
rows.reference: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be disruption at the border which the industry says could lead to delays and shortages of parts.

rows.source: Kò ní ṣeéṣe fún Tòyótà láti ní ọjà nílẹ̀ tó ju ìwọ̀n ọjọ́ kan lọ ní ibi Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Derbyshire, ilé iṣẹ́ náà ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, àtipé ìgbéṣẹ́jáde máa dáwọ́ dúró.
rows.output: It is not possible for Toyota to have a factory on the site for more than a day in Derbyshire, the company said, adding that production would be suspended.
rows.reference: It would be impossible for Toyota to hold more than a day's worth of inventory at its Derbyshire plant, the company said, and so production would be stopped.

rows.source: Mr Clark sọ pé ète Theresa May fún ìbáṣepọ̀ ọjọ́ iwájú pẹ̀lú EU jẹ́ “àmọ̀ǹmọ̀ṣe láti yàgò fún àwọn àyẹ́wò ní ààlà ìbodè náà.”
rows.output: Mr. Clark said that Theresa May's intention for future relations with the EU is "a desperate attempt to avoid scrutiny at the border."
rows.reference: Mr Clark said Theresa May's Chequers plan for future relations with the EU is "precisely calibrated to avoid those checks at the border."

rows.source: "A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò. A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò tó dára jùlọ tí ó máa gbà wá láàyè bí mo ṣe sọ, tí kò kì í ṣe àṣeyọrí nìkán ní àkókò yì tí a lé gbàdún, ṣùgbọ́n fún wa láti má le sọ àǹfààní yìí nù,” ó sọ fún ètò rédíò 4 BBC Lónìí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement. We need the best trade agreement possible that will allow us to live as I say, not just a success in the time that we are given, but to ensure that we do not lose this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: "Ẹ̀rí àrídájú tí kìíṣe láti ọ̀dọ̀ Toyotà nìkan ṣùgbọ́n tí ó jẹ́ ti àwọn àṣemọ́tò jáde míràn ní pé a nílò láti rí dájú pé a tẹ̀síwájú nínú ohun tí a ti ńṣe láṣeyọrílórí àwọn ààtò ìpèsè.”
rows.output: "Unsubstantiated claims from Toyota alone are not enough, but from other manufacturers as well, to ensure that we continue on the path of providing timely and appropriate support."
rows.reference: "The evidence from not just Toyota but other manufacturers is that we need to absolutely be able to continue what has been a highly successful set of supply chains."

rows.source: Toyota kò le sọ pàtò bí ó ṣe máa pẹ́ tó kí ìgbéṣẹ́jáde tó le dáwọ́ dúró, ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí ó bá ṣe díẹ̀, ó kìlọ̀ pé àwọn ìṣùnà mìràn tó le jẹyọ máa ṣàdínkù ìledíje ẹ̀rọ ìṣẹ́ tí ó sì máa jásí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́.
rows.output: Toyota cannot predict how long the production stoppage will last, but when it does, it warns that other factors may reduce the competitiveness of the vehicle's technology and lead to a loss of jobs.
rows.reference: Toyota was unable to say how long production would be stopped, but in the longer term, warned that added costs would reduce the plant's competitiveness and eventually cost jobs.

rows.source: Peter Tsouvallaris, tí ó ti ṣiṣẹ́ ní Burnaston fún ọdún 24 tí ó sì jẹ́ adárí ìpàdé ìgbìmọ̀ òkòwò níibi ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ náà, sọ pé ó kàn àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òun gan an: "Ní ìrírí mi, ní kété tí àwọn iṣẹ́ yìí bá lọ, wọ̀n kó ní padà wá mọ́ láeláee.
rows.output: Peter Tsouvallaris, who has worked at Burnaston for 24 years and is the leader of the economic and social committee there, said that he was only able to recruit a few members: "In my experience, as soon as these operations are closed, they will not come back."
rows.reference: Peter Tsouvallaris, who has worked at Burnaston for 24 years and is the Unite union convenor at the plant, said his members are increasingly concerned: "In my experience once these jobs go they never come back.

rows.source: Agbẹnusọ fún ìjọba kan sọ wípé: "A ti taari èròǹgbà tí ó ṣe gẹ́gẹ́ tí ó ṣì mú ọgbọ́n wa fún ọjọ́ iwájú ìbáṣepọ̀ wa pẹ̀lú EU.”
rows.output: The government spokesman said: "We have taken note of the concerns that have been expressed and we are maintaining our wisdom for future relations with the EU."
rows.reference: A government spokesperson said: "We have put forward a precise and credible plan for our future relationship with the EU."

rows.source: Ìpàdé Trump pẹ̀lú Rosenstein lé ní ìdádúró lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, Ilé Funfun Báláu ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: The Trump meeting with Rosenstein was delayed again, White House says.
rows.reference: Trump meeting with Rosenstein may be delayed again, says White House

rows.source: Ìpàdé onípinnu-ńlá Donald Trump pẹ̀lú ìgbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò Rod Rosenstein le “sún síwájú fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ kan mìíràn” bí ìjà lórí ẹnítí wọn dábàá fún ilé ẹjọ́ gíga Brett kavanaugh ṣe tẹ́ ṣíwájú, Ilé Funfun Báláú ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ ní Ọjọ́ ìsinmi.
rows.output: A meeting between President Donald Trump and Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein could be delayed for another week or so, White House press secretary Sarah Sanders said on Sunday.
rows.reference: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein could be "pushed back another week" as the fight over supreme court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.

rows.source: Rosensteinní ó ń ṣàbójútó iṣẹ́ àgbẹjọ́rò pàtàkì Robert Mueller, tí ó ń ṣe ìwádìí lórí i ìkọlù Rọ́ṣíà lórí ìdìbò, ìbáṣepọ̀ láàrin àwọn òṣiṣẹ́ Trump àti Rọ́ṣíà àti bí ó ṣe ṣẹéṣe sí fún ààrẹ láti dènà ètò ìdájọ tó péye.
rows.output: Rosenstein oversees a crucial investigation by special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian interference in the election, the relationship between Trump's staff and Russia, and the possibility of the president obstructing justice.
rows.reference: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian election interference, links between Trump aides and Russia and potential obstruction of justice by the president.

rows.source: Bóyá Trump máa dá igbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò dúró tàbí kò ní ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, tí ó máa wá mú kí òmínira Mueller níra, ti jẹ́ kí Washington ṣòfófo fú ọ̀pọ̀ oṣù ṣẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Perhaps Trump will appoint a special prosecutor or not, which will only add to the uncertainty of the Mueller investigation, and keep Washington in a state of turmoil for several more months.
rows.reference: Whether or not Trump will fire the deputy attorney general, and thereby endanger Mueller's independence, has fuelled Washington gossip for months.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ oṣù yìí, ìwé ìròyìn New York Times jábọ̀ pé Rosenstein jíròrò lórí i pé oùn fẹ́ fí wáyà sára láti ṣe àkásílẹ̀ ìtàkurọ̀sọ pẹ̀lú Trump àti ìṣeéṣesí láti yọ ààrẹ nínú àtúnṣe 25.
rows.output: In the beginning of this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed the possibility of secretly recording Trump and using it to justify removing him from office.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed wearing a wire to record conversations with Trump and the possibility of removing the president via the 25th amendment.

rows.source: Rosenstein ní ìròyìn yí kò rí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: Rosenstein said the report did not show that.
rows.reference: Rosenstein denied the report.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n ní ọjọ́ ajé tó kọjá ó lọ sí Ilé Funfun Bbáláú, láàrin àwọn ìròyìn pé ó tí fẹ́ kswé fi ipò rẹ̀ sílẹ̀
rows.output: But on the previous day he went to White House, amidst reports that he had resigned from his position
rows.reference: But last Monday he went to the White House, amid reports he was about to resign.

rows.source: Dípò, ìpàdé pẹ̀lú Trump, ẹni tí ó wà ní ìpàdé Àjọ ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé ní New York ní àkókò náà, di kíkéde láti wáyé ní ọjọ́’rú.
rows.output: Instead, the meeting with Trump, who was at the United Nations General Assembly in New York at the time, was declared to be canceled.
rows.reference: Instead, a meeting with Trump, who was then at the United Nations in New York, was announced for Thursday.

rows.source: Trump sọ pé òun "kò ní fẹ́" láti dá Rosenstein dúró lẹ́nu iṣẹ́ ṣùgbọ́n lẹ́yìn èyí ìpàdé náà di dídá dúró díẹ̀ láti yàgò fún èdè àìyedè pẹ̀lú ìgbìmọ̀ ìdájọ́ Aṣòfin àgbà ní ibi tí Kavanaugh àti ọ̀kan lára àwọn obìnrin tí ó fi ẹ̀sùn ìbálòpọ̀ ní ọ́nà àìtọ́ kan Ọ̀mọ̀wé Christine Blassey Ford, àwọn méjèèjì ló jẹ́ ẹ̀rí
rows.output: Trump said he "doesn't want" to fire Rosenstein but after the meeting, the ouster was delayed to avoid controversy with the Senate Judiciary Committee, where Kavanaugh and one of the women accusing him of sexual misconduct, Christine Blasey Ford, were testifying.
rows.reference: Trump said he would "prefer not" to fire Rosenstein but then the meeting was delayed to avoid a clash with the Senate judiciary committee hearing in which Kavanaugh and one of the women who have accused him of sexual misconduct, Dr Christine Blasey Ford, both testified.

rows.source: Ní ọjọ́ ẹtì, Trump pa àṣẹ fún FBI láti ṣe ìwádìí ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanugh, tí ó tún mú kí ìdádúró wá fún píparí ìbò Ilé Aṣòfin àgbà.
rows.output: On Thursday, Trump ordered the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh, which also delayed the final vote in the Senate.
rows.reference: On Friday, Trump ordered a one-week FBI investigation of claims against Kavanaugh, further delaying a full Senate vote.

rows.source: Àkọ̀wé ìròyǹ Trump, Sarah Sanders, wà farahàn lórí ìòyìn Fox l’ọ́jọ́ Ìsinmi.
rows.output: Trump's former press secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News on Easter Sunday.
rows.reference: Trump's press secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News Sunday.

rows.source: Nígbà tí wọ́n bèèrè ìpàdé pẹ̀lú Rosenstein, ó sọ pé: "A kò tíì ní déètì fún ìyẹn báyìí, ó le jẹ́ ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, mó rí bí ìgbà pé ó máa sún ṣẹ́yìn fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ míràn nítorí gbogbo nǹkan tí ó ń lọ lọ́wọ́ ní ilé ẹjọ́ tó ga jùlọ.
rows.output: When they asked for a meeting with Rosenstein, he said: "We haven't been able to schedule that yet, it might be this week, I'm not sure, but it will probably have to be pushed back for another week because of all the things going on in the highest court.
rows.reference: Asked about the Rosenstein meeting, she said: "A date for that hasn't been set, it could be this week, I could see that pushing back another week given all of the other things that are going on with the supreme court.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n kí á máa wò bọ̀ àtipé mo máa ń fẹ́ fi ohun tí ó ńlọ tó àwọn oníròyìn létí.
rows.output: But I always want to remind the media of what is going on.
rows.reference: But we'll see and I always like to keep the press updated."

rows.source: Àwọn oníròyìn kan máa ṣàríyàjiyàn lórí èléyìí: Sanders kò tíì ṣe ìpàdé pẹ̀lú àwọn oníròyìn Ilé Funfun Báláú láti ọjọ 10 oṣù kẹsàn án.
rows.output: Some journalists argue that Sanders has not met with the White House press corps since January 10.
rows.reference: Some reporters would contest that assertion: Sanders has not held a White House press briefing since 10 September.

rows.source: Agbàlejò, Chris Wallace bèèrè ìdí rẹ̀
rows.output: Candidate, Chris Wallace, asked his reason.
rows.reference: Host Chris Wallace asked why.

rows.source: Sanders sọ pé àìse ìpàdé pẹ̀lú àwọn oníròyìn kí ṣe nípà àìnífẹ́sí “ṣekárími” àwon oníròyìn TV, bíótilẹ̀jẹ́pé ó ní̀: "Emí kò ní ṣe àìfaramọ́ pé wọ́n máa ń ṣe ṣekárími.”
rows.output: Sanders said that not meeting with reporters is not due to a lack of desire to "chat" with TV reporters, although he has: "I don't want to be a chatty Cathy."
rows.reference: Sanders said the scarcity of briefings was not due to a distaste for TV reporters "grandstanding," although she said: "I won't disagree with the fact that they grandstand."

rows.source: Ó wá dá lábàá pé kí ìbáṣepọ̀ tààrà máa túnbọ gbòòrò síi láàrin Trump àti àwọn oníròyìn.
rows.output: He came to the conclusion that the relationship between Trump and the media would continue to grow more complex.
rows.reference: She then suggested direct contact between Trump and the press will increase.

rows.source: "Ààrẹ ṣe ọ̀pọ̀ sáà ìbéèrè àti ìdáhùn ju èyíkéyìí ààrẹ tí ó ṣiwájú rẹ̀,” ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ láìfi ẹ̀rí kankan múlẹ̀: “A ti wo àwọn nọ́ńbà wọ̀nyẹn."
rows.output: The president has asked more questions and given more answers than any previous president, he said, without providing any evidence: "We've looked at those numbers."
rows.reference: "The president does more Q&A sessions than any president has prior to him," she said, adding without citing evidence: "We've looked at those numbers."

rows.source: Ìsọnísókí sì máa wáyé, Sanders sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n “tí oníròyìn bá rí àǹfààní láti bi ààrẹ ilẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà ní ìbéèrè tààràtà, ìyẹn dára púpọ̀ jú bíbá èmi sọ̀rọ̀ lọ.
rows.output: The interview will take place, Sanders said, but "if the media finds an opportunity to interview the president of the United States directly, that's much better than talking to me."
rows.reference: Briefings will still happen, Sanders said, but "if the press has the chance to ask the president of the United States questions directly, that's infinitely better than talking to me.

rows.source: À ń gbìyànjú láti ṣe ìyẹn gan ni àtipé ẹ ti rí wá tí a ń ṣe ìyẹn ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà ní àwọn ọ̀ṣẹ́ tó ti kọjá ṣẹ́hìn. Ìyẹn ló máa dípò ìpàdé ìfitóníròyìnlétí nígbàtí o bá ti le bá ààrẹ ilẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà sọ̀rọ̀.”
rows.output: We are trying to do that exactly as you have seen us do that many times in the past few weeks. That would replace the press conference when you are able to speak to the President of the United States.
rows.reference: We try to do that a lot and you've seen us do that a lot over the last few weeks and that's going to take the place of a press briefing when you can talk to the president of the United States."

rows.source: Trump máa ń dáhùn àwọn ìbéèrè nígbàtí ó bá ń fi Ilé Funfun Báláú sílẹ̀ tàbí tí ó ń kópa nínú ṣàá ìta gbangba tàbí àwọn ìpàdé àjọrò oníròyìn pẹ̀lú àwọn àlejò pàtàkì.
rows.output: Trump often answers questions when he is leaving the White House or participating in a press conference with important guests.
rows.reference: Trump regularly takes questions when leaving the White House or participating in open sessions or press conferences with visiting dignitaries.

rows.source: Ìpàdé àjọrò aládàáṣe kò wọ́pọ̀.
rows.output: A meeting of the minds is not a common occurrence.
rows.reference: Solo press conferences are rare.

rows.source: Ní New York ní ọ́ṣẹ̀ yìí, ààrẹ́ dá bí ẹnípé ó fi ìdí rẹ̀ hàn, bí ó ṣe jẹ́ pé kìí tẹ̀lé ìlànà to ti wa nílẹ̀ àti bí ó ṣe máa ń yọ síwájú àwọn oníròyìn lójijì lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀kan.
rows.output: In New York this week, the president was accused of being a bully, of not following the established rules and of constantly pushing reporters aside.
rows.reference: In New York this week the president perhaps demonstrated why, making a freewheeling and at times bizarre appearance before gathered reporters.

rows.source: Àkọ̀wé Ìlera kọ̀wé sí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ EU ní NHS Scotland lórí ìbẹ́rù Brexit
rows.output: The Health Secretary wrote to EU staff in NHS Scotland about Brexit fears
rows.reference: Health secretary writes to EU workers at NHS Scotland over Brexit fears

rows.source: Àkọ̀wé Ìlera ti kọ̀wé sí òṣìṣẹ́ EU tó ń ṣiṣẹ́ ní NHS ti Scotland láti fi ìdúnnú̀ orílẹ̀ èdè rẹ̀ hàn àti láti kí wọ́n fún ìgbà ọ̀tun lẹ́yìn Brexit.
rows.output: The Health Secretary wrote to the EU official working in the NHS in Scotland to express his delight and to wish them a prosperous future after Brexit.

rows.output: To be found guilty, lawyers will have to show that Saipov "knowingly" killed eight people and "knowingly" caused serious physical injury, as consideration for the death penalty, compared to Southern District of New York.

rows.output: "Many believe that the decision to seek the death penalty is a personal choice that should not be criticized. However, the fact that people are being sentenced to death for their lives in a manner that is not conducive to rehabilitation will only increase the sense of injustice that this event has for all those affected," Patton said.
