rows.output: The strength of the collective is a complete game plan that is agreed upon by the players, which means that everyone is on the same page and plays the game in the same way.
rows.reference: The swinging pendulum of momentum is a completely invented sporting concept but one that players truly believe in, and never more so than at competitions like these.

rows.source: Yabụ kedu ebe ha ga-ekwu na ike dị ugbu a?
rows.output: So where is the current power located?
rows.reference: So where would they say the momentum is now?

rows.source: “Ha ji akara isii aga ma ugbu a ọ bụ anọ, yabụ anyị ga-ebu nke ahụ dịka obere agbamume, a na m eche,” Jordan Spieth kwuru ka ọ na-apụ maka ụbọchị ahụ.
rows.output: “We had six loaves of bread, and now we have four, so we’re going to take that as a little encouragement, and I’m hoping,” said Jordan Spieth as he left for the day.
rows.reference: "They had a six-point lead and now it's four, so we are carrying that as a little bit of momentum I guess," said Jordan Spieth as he strolled off for the day.

rows.source: Mba Europe nwere uru, n’ezie, akara anọ n’ihu yana iri na abụọ a ka na-akụ akụ.
rows.output: European countries, of course, have four fingers in front and twelve behind, and they are still counting.
rows.reference: Europe have the advantage, of course, four points ahead with twelve more in play.

rows.source: Ndị America, dịka Spieth kwuru, chere na ha nwere obere ikuku n’ubu ha ma nwee ọtụtụ ihe agbamume, na abụghị opekempe ụdịdị Spieth na Justin Thomas, bụ ndị gwukọrọ egwuregwu ọnụ ụbọchị niile, na onye ọ bụla ga-anya isi akara atọ n’ime anọ.
rows.output: Americans, as Spieth said, felt they had little wind in their sails and had a lot of encouragement, not at least the kind of Spieth and Justin Thomas, who played together all day, and everyone was to make three birdies in four.
rows.reference: The Americans, as Spieth says, feel they have a little wind in their sails though and they have plenty to be encouraged by, not least the form of Spieth and Justin Thomas who played together all day and each boast three points from four.

rows.source: Spieth dị mmerụ ahụ kemgbe akụpụrụ na tee ruo na ama ndu ndu ma na-aga dịka ọmụmatụ.
rows.output: Spieth was injured after being hit by a tee shot on the first hole and was walking like a zombie.
rows.reference: Spieth has been lethal from tee to green and is leading by example.

rows.source: Mkpu ike nke anurị dasibere ike ka agba nke ya na-aga n’ihu, n’ịkụbanye bọọlụ dị mkpa iji mee ka egwuregwu nke anọ nọrọ n’otu akara mgbe ya na Thomas jiri ọkụkụ abụọ ‘na-akpụ akpụ ka ha kụchara ugboro abụọ.
rows.output: The Anurag's strength was waning, but his determination was still strong as he continued to push the ball forward, using his feet to control it and keep the game level after Thomas had scored twice, hitting the ball twice.
rows.reference: Those guttural screams of celebration got louder as his round went on, sinking a crucial putt to take match four all-square when he and Thomas had been two down after two.

rows.source: Ụdị olu mkpu ahụ zutere ya na nkụbanye nke nyere ha mmeri na 15, ụdị nke na-agwa gị na ọ kwenyere na ndị America apụbeghị na nke a.
rows.output: The vocal style met him with a crunch that gave them the win at 15, a style that tells you that he believes the Americans have not left this one.
rows.reference: His putt that won them the match on 15 was met with a similar scream, the sort that tells you he believes that the American team is not out of this.

rows.source: “Ị ga-enyobanye anya n’ime were na-atụ uche maka egwuregwu nke gị,” Spieth kwuru.
rows.output: "You have to be aware of the lies and the traps of the game," Spieth said.
rows.reference: "You've really just got to dig deep and worry about your own match," Spieth said.

rows.source: Ọ bụ naanị ihe ndị niile na-akụ egwuregwu a nwere ugbu a.
rows.output: It's just a matter of all those who play this game having it now.
rows.reference: It is all each of these players has left now.

rows.source: Oghere18 iji nwee akara.
rows.output: The 18th hole to have a birdie.
rows.reference: 18 holes to make a mark.

rows.source: Naanị ndị na-akụ egwuregwu a nwere akara karịa Spieth na Thomas n’ime ụbọchị abụọ gara aga bụ Francesco Molinari na Tommy Fleetwood, akụkọ nke Ryder Cup enweghị mgbagha.
rows.output: Only those with a score lower than Spieth and Thomas in the last two days are Francesco Molinari and Tommy Fleetwood, the story of the Ryder Cup is one of no debate.
rows.reference: The only players with more points than Spieth and Thomas over the past two days are Francesco Molinari and Tommy Fleetwood, the indisputable story of the Ryder Cup.

rows.source: Njikọ mara mma ma na atụghị anya nke Europe bụ anọ n’ime anọ n’enweghị ike ime ihe ọjọọ ọ bụla.
rows.output: A beautiful and unexpected connection to Europe is that four out of four cannot do anything wrong.
rows.reference: Europe's odd but adorable couple are four from four and can do no wrong.

rows.source: “Moliwood” bụ naanị njikọ na-akụfeghị na ehihe Satọde, mana ha zenarịrị nkụfe n’ụtụtụ Satọde, ehihe Fraịde yana ngwucha oghere itoolu n’ụtụtụ Fraịde.
rows.output: “Moliwood” is just a connection that doesn’t cut into Saturday activities, but they do cut into Saturday morning activities, Friday activities and the nine o’clock opening on Friday morning.
rows.reference: "Moliwood" were the only pair not to shoot a bogey on Saturday afternoon, but they also avoided bogeys on Saturday morning, Friday afternoon and the back nine on Friday morning.

rows.source: Ọkụkụ ahụ, na ka ike ha si aga ma na-abịa site na ndị igwe mmadụ a na-eme mkpọtụ gosipụtara na ha bụ ndị egwuregwu a ga-achọ imeri na Sọnde, nke n’agaghị enwe onye egwuregwu ọzọ ama ama nwere ike bute mmeri nke mba Europe ka anwụ na-ada na Le Golf National karịa Fleetwood na Molinari.
rows.output: The buzz, and the way their power came and went from these noisy machines, was that they were the players to beat on Sunday, and that no other player of note would be able to bring the European title to the golf course at Le Golf National before the sun set on Fleetwood and Molinari.
rows.reference: That run, and the way their energy seems to flow both to and from this boisterous crowd cements that they are the players to beat on Sunday, and there would be no more popular player to seal a potential European victory as the sun sets over Le Golf National than Fleetwood or Molinari.

rows.source: Ọ kacha mma ha abụọ n’otu oge n’oghere dị iche iche.
rows.output: It is best to have them both at the same time in different places.
rows.reference: Preferably both simultaneously on different holes.

rows.source: Okwu ebube mba Europe erubeghị, agbanyeghi.
rows.output: The European Union's word of honor has not been broken, however.
rows.reference: Talk of European glory remains premature, though.

rows.source: Bubba Watson na Webb Simpson jiri Sergio Garcia mere ihe egwuregwu na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ n’ụtụtụ, mgbe etinyekọrọ yana Alex Noren.
rows.output: Bubba Watson and Webb Simpson won the two-man team match play event in the morning, after being paired with Alex Noren.
rows.reference: Bubba Watson and Webb Simpson made short work of Sergio Garcia, the morning's fourballs hero, when he was paired with Alex Noren.

rows.source: Ịkụfe otu ugboro na ịkụfe ugboro abụọ n’ọkụkụ ugboro itoolu kụnyere onye mba Spain na Sweden n’olulu nke ha enweghị ike ịrịpụta.
rows.output: Kicking once and then twice in the ribs nine times, the Spaniard and the Swede were trapped in their hole, unable to escape.
rows.reference: A bogey and two doubles on the front nine dug the Spaniard and the Swede into a hole they never got close to climbing out of.

rows.source: Na Sọnde, agbanyeghị n’onweghị onye ga-enyere gị aka ịpụta n’olulu gị.
rows.output: On Sunday, however, no one will be able to help you get out of your pit.
rows.reference: On Sunday, though, there is nobody to help you out of your hole.

rows.source: Bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ na agba mmadụ anọ bụ ihe ịtụ n’anya ịnọ nso lelee n’ihi mkparịta ụka dị na etiti njikọ a, ndụmọdụ ha na-enye, ndụmọdụ ha anaghị enye na otu atụmatụ na-esi agbanwe ozugbo ozugbo.
rows.output: A two-man team and four-man crew is a surprise to watch closely because of the conversation in the middle of this connection, their advice, their lack of advice on one plan that is constantly changing immediately.
rows.reference: The fourballs and foursomes are so fascinating to watch up close because of the interactions between pairings, the advice they give, the advice they don't and the way that a strategy can change in an instant.

rows.source: Mba Europe akụọla nke ọma dịka otu ruo ugbu a ma werekwa isi pụtara ihie ruo n’ụbọchị ikpeazụ mana agba mmadụ anọ a gosiri na otu USA nwere afọ ilụ ọgụ nke na ụfọdụ, ọ kachasị ndị Stateside na-agbagha mgbagha.
rows.output: Europe has been well known as a single entity until now and has been considered to be a very liberal place, but the four colors shown in the flag of the USA indicate a four-year struggle for freedom, which some, especially those in the States, have been opposing.
rows.reference: Europe have played better as a team thus far and take a significant lead into the final day but this foursomes session also showed that Team USA has the stomach for the fight that some, especially Stateside, had been doubting.

rows.source: Mba Europe ji 10-6 aga, were banye Ryder Cup n’ụbọchị ikpeazụ
rows.output: Europe won 10-6 and entered the Ryder Cup on the final day
rows.reference: Europe take 10-6 lead into Ryder Cup final day

rows.source: Mba Europe ga-eji uru mara abụba were banye ụbọchị ikpeazụ nke Ryder Cup ka ha jichara 10-6 aga United State na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ yana agba mmadụ anọ nke Satọde.
rows.output: The European team will use their advantage to win the final day of the Ryder Cup after leading 10-6 against the United States in the two-man foursomes and the four-man singles on Saturday.
rows.reference: Europe will take a healthy advantage into the final day of the Ryder Cup after emerging from Saturday's fourballs and foursomes matches with a 10-6 lead over the United States.

rows.source: Ndị abụọ a akpalitere mmụọ ha, Tommy Fleetwood na Francesco Molinari bu ụzọ site na mmeri abụọ emeriri Tiger Woods n’agbalị mgbalị, n’iji akara anọ aga na Le Golf National.
rows.output: The two leaders, Tommy Fleetwood and Francesco Molinari, were first by two strokes after a pair of two-under rounds, with a four-shot lead at Le Golf National.
rows.reference: Inspired duo Tommy Fleetwood and Francesco Molinari led the charge with two victories over a struggling Tiger Woods to take their tally so far at Le Golf National to four points.

rows.source: Ndị otu mba Europe nke Thomas Bjorn, na-achụ ijigide iko mmeri anapụrụ ha na Hazeline afọ abụọ gara aga, nọgidere ndị mba America na-akụgheri akụgheri ike na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ n’ụtụtụ, were 3-1 merie agba nke ahụ.
rows.output: The European team of Thomas Bjorn, who were defending their title won two years ago at the Hazeline, were beaten by the Americans in a two-ball match in the morning, and lost 3-1 in the match.
rows.reference: Thomas Bjorn's European side, bidding to retain the trophy they lost at Hazeltine two years ago, dominated a misfiring American side in the morning fourballs, taking the series 3-1.

rows.source: Ndị US zọgidere nke ukwuu na agba mmadụ anọ, wee merie na asompi abụọ, mana ha enweghị ike ibelata ọnụọgụ mmeri.
rows.output: The US continued to dominate in the four-man race, won two of the competitions, but were unable to reduce the number of victories.
rows.reference: The U.S. offered more resistance in the foursomes, winning two matches, but they could not eat into the deficit.

rows.source: Otu Jim Furyk chọrọ akara asatọ site na asompi 12 agba nke otu onye mere na Sọnde iji jigide iko mmeri ha.
rows.output: Jim Furyk needs eight strokes from a 12-hole final round by one man to retain their title.
rows.reference: Jim Furyk's side need eight points from Sunday's 12 singles matches to retain the trophy.

rows.source: Fleetwood bụ onye ọhụrụ mbụ mba Europe meriri akara anọ ugboro ugboro ebe ya na Molinari, agụrụ aha “Molliwood” ka izu ụka pụrụ iche gachara bụ otu abụọ jiri akara anọ merie na asompi izizi anọ ha na hịstrị Ryder Cup.
rows.output: Fleetwood was the first European rookie to win four points in a row, where he and Molinari, who were nicknamed "Molliwood" after a special weekend, won four points in their first four matches in the history of the Ryder Cup.
rows.reference: Fleetwood is the first European rookie to win four points in a row while he and Molinari, dubbed "Molliwood" after a sensational weekend are only the second pair to win four points from their opening four matches in Ryder Cup history.

rows.source: Ebe ha merigoro Woods na Patrick Reed na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ, ha were jikọọ nke ọma were merie Woods dagoro mba na onye ọhụrụ mba America, Bryson Dechambeau site na 5&4 dara ụda.
rows.output: After losing to Woods and Patrick Reed in a two-man match, they teamed up together and won Woods' national title and the new American national champion, Bryson Dechambeau, by a score of 5&4.
rows.reference: Having crushed Woods and Patrick Reed in the fourballs they then gelled superbly to beat a deflated Woods and American rookie Bryson Dechambeau by an even more emphatic 5&4.

rows.source: Woods, bụ onye dọgidere onwe ya na asompi abụọ na Satọde gosiri anya nka ya na adanye adanye mana o tufuola asompi 19 n’ime 29 na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ yana agba mmadụ anọ na nke asaa ugboro ugboro.
rows.output: Woods, who was a strong contender in two-man bobsled races on Saturday, showed his skills in the downhill race but lost 19 out of 29 races in the two-man race and four-man race in the seventh time.
rows.reference: Woods, who dragged himself through two matches on Saturday, showed occasional bursts of brilliance but he has now lost 19 of his 29 matches in fourballs and foursomes and seven in a row.

rows.source: Justin Rose zuru ike bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ nke ụtụtụ, were laghachi isonyere Henrik Stenson na agba mmadụ anọ nke ejiri 2&1 were merie Dustin Johnson na Brooks Koepka-ndị nọ n’ọkwa nke mbu na nke atọ na mba ụwa.
rows.output: Justin Rose won the two-man scramble in the morning, then joined Henrik Stenson to win the four-man foursomes, which were played at 2&1, defeating Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka, who were in first and third place on the world rankings.
rows.reference: Justin Rose, rested for the morning fourballs, returned to partner Henrik Stenson in the foursomes to a 2&1 defeat of Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka - ranked one and three in the world.

rows.source: Mba Europe enwetachaghị ya ka ha siri chọọ, agbanyeghị n’ụbọchị ikuku ọma mgbada ọdịda anyanwu nke Paris.
rows.output: The European countries did not have it as they wished, however, on a windy day in the southern suburbs of Paris.
rows.reference: Europe did not have it al their own way though on a pleasant, breezy day south west of Paris.

rows.source: Jordan Spieth onye mmeri ugboro atọ na Justin Thomas jiri akara abụọ were tọọ ọkọlọtọ maka mba America na Satọde.
rows.output: Three-time champion Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas used two shots to take the lead for the United States on Saturday.
rows.reference: Three-times major winner Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas set the benchmark for the Americans with two points on Saturday.

rows.source: Ha nwetara mmeri siri ike nke 2&1 na Jon Rahm na Ian Poulter nke mba Spain na bọọlụ otu mmadụ abụọ were laghachi ọzọ imeri Poulter na Rory Mcllroy 4&3 na agba mmadụ anọ, ebe emerigoro ha n’oghere mmalite abụọ.
rows.output: They won a strong 2&1 victory over Jon Rahm and Ian Poulter of Spain, who were two-man teams, and then came back to win again over Poulter and Rory McIlroy 4&3 in the four-ball, having won both of their opening matches.
rows.reference: They earned a gritty 2&1 win over Spain's Jon Rahm and Ian Poulter in the fourballs and returned later to beat Poulter and Rory McIlroy 4&3 in the foursomes having lost the opening two holes.

rows.source: Naanị ugboro abụọ na hịstrị Ryder Cup ka otu laghachiri azụ site na akara anọ ejiri emeri ha na mbanye agba nke otu onye, n’agbanyeghị dịka ndị ji iko, otu Furyk chọrọ naanị ịgbata onye laba, onye laba iji jigide iko mmeri ha.
rows.output: Only twice in Ryder Cup history has a team come back from four points down to win the singles session, despite as the holders, Furyk just needed to win one, one to retain the cup.
rows.reference: Only twice in Ryder Cup history has a team come back from a four-point deficit going into the singles, although as holders Furyk's side need only draw to retain the trophy.

rows.source: Mgbe ha gbachara ndị nke abụọ n’ụbọchị abụọ, kosiladị, mbuso agha nke Sọnde dị ka ihe karịrị ha.
rows.output: After they had defeated the second army on the two days, the Sunday attack was like a storm.
rows.reference: After being second-best for two days, however, a Sunday counter-attack looks as though it will be beyond them.

rows.source: North Korea kwuru “ọ gaghị eme” ịgbarapụ ngwa ọgụ na anataghị nkwenye
rows.output: North Korea said "it will not do" to withdraw weapons and unilaterally disband.
rows.reference: North Korea says 'no way' will disarm unilaterally without trust

rows.source: Onye Mịnịsta nke mba ofesi North Korea gwara United Nations na Satọde na ịga n’ihu amachibido ha na-ebute atụkwasịghị obi na United State nke na ọ nweghịkwa ka obodo ha ga-esi gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ nuklịa ha n’ụdị ọnọdụ ahụ.
rows.output: The North Korean Minister of Foreign Affairs told the United Nations on Saturday that continuing to impose sanctions on them would only increase their distrust in the United States and make it impossible for their country to withdraw its nuclear weapons in such a situation.
rows.reference: North Korea's foreign minister told the United Nations on Saturday continued sanctions were deepening its mistrust in the United States and there was no way the country would give up its nuclear weapons unilaterally under such circumstances.

rows.source: Ri Yong Ho gwara otu mba ụwa na Mgbakọ Ezumezu ha kwa afọ na North Korea esorola “ezigbo ụzọ pụtara ihie” n’afọ gara aga, dị ka nkwụsị nlele ngwa nuklịa na ogbunigwe, ntọsa ebe nlele ngwa nuklịa ma kwee nkwa na ọ gaghị arụkasị ngwa ọgụ nuklịa na teknụzụ nuklịa.
rows.output: Ri Yong Ho told the International Assembly of the United Nations that North Korea had followed a "wise and brilliant" path in the previous year, including the suspension of nuclear weapons testing and missile testing, the dismantling of nuclear test sites, and a commitment not to resume nuclear weapons testing and nuclear technology.
rows.reference: Ri Yong Ho told the world body's annual General Assembly that North Korea had taken "significant goodwill measures" in the past year, such as stopping nuclear and missiles tests, dismantling the nuclear test site, and pledging not to proliferate nuclear weapons and nuclear technology.

rows.source: “Kosiladị, anyị ahụghị asịsa na-esote ya sitere na U,S” o kwuru.
rows.output: "Of course, we didn't see any follow-up on that from the U.S.," he said.
rows.reference: "However, we do not see any corresponding response from the U.S.," he said.

rows.source: “N’enweghị ntụkwasị obi na U.S, agaghị enwekwa okwukwe na nchekwa nke obodo anyị, na n’ụdị ọnọdụ a, ọ nweghị ka anyị ga-esi buru ụzọ gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ anyị.”
rows.output: “Without faith in the U.S., we will also have no faith in the safety of our country, and in this situation, we cannot expect to be the first to disarm our weapons.”
rows.reference: "Without any trust in the U.S. there will be no confidence in our national security and under such circumstances there is no way we will unilaterally disarm ourselves first."

rows.source: Ebe Ri gbanwere mkpesa ndị North Korea banyere ọjụjụ nke Washington ime usoro “agba” mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa n’okpuru nke North Korea ga-erite elele dịka ọ na-esonye usoro obere obere, okwu ya bara uru n’ihi na ọ jụghị mgbarapụ ngwa nuklliya ozugbo dịka Pyongyang siri mee n’oge gara aga.
rows.output: In a change of tone, North Korea has made a complaint to Washington that the U.S. is not taking the "bold" step of nuclear disarmament that North Korea would be required to follow as part of the agreement. The U.S. has not agreed to immediate nuclear disarmament as Pyongyang had previously demanded.
rows.reference: While Ri reprised familiar North Korean complaints about Washington's resistance to a "phased" approach to denuclearization under which North Korea would be rewarded as it took gradual steps, his statement appeared significant in that it did not reject unilateral denuclearization out of hand as Pyongyang has done in the past.

rows.source: Ri rụtụrụ aka na nkwuputa Kim Jong Un na Donald Trump kwukọrịtara na ọgbakọ nke izizi n’etiti onye isi ala U.S nọ n’ọchịchị na onye ọchịchị North Korea na Singapore na Juun 12, mgbe Kim kwere nkwa ịhụ banyere “mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa nke okirikiri Korea” ebe Trump kwere nkwa nchekwa nke North Korea.
rows.output: He referred to the statement by Kim Jong Un that Donald Trump agreed to during the first meeting between the U.S. president and the North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim promised to address the "denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" and Trump promised to provide security guarantees for North Korea.
rows.reference: Ri referred to a joint statement issued by Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump at a first ever summit between a serving U.S. president and a North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim pledged to work toward "denuclearization of the Korean peninsula" while Trump promised guarantees of North Korea's security.

rows.source: North Korea na-achọ njedebe agha 1950-53 nke Korea, mana United States ekwuola na Pyongyang ga-ebu ụzọ gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ nuklliya ya.
rows.output: North Korea is seeking an end to the 1950-53 Korean War, but the United States has said that Pyongyang must first dismantle its nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: North Korea has been seeking a formal end to the 1950-53 Korea War, but the United States has said Pyongyang must give up its nuclear weapons first.

rows.source: Washington ajụkwala oku ibelata mmachibido mba ụwa a siri ike nke North Korea.
rows.output: Washington has not called for a reduction in the strict international sanctions against North Korea.
rows.reference: Washington has also resisted calls to relax tough international sanctions on North Korea.

rows.source: “U.S kwụgidere na “mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa-izizi” ma bulikwuo nkwanye ya site na mmachibido iji mezuo ebumnuche ha n’ụzọ nkwanye, ma jụkwuo “nkwuputa nke njedebe agha” Ri kwuru.
rows.output: The U.S. maintained its "first use" policy and bolstered its commitment to using nuclear weapons to achieve their objectives, but rejected the "no first use" declaration. Ri said.
rows.reference: "The U.S. insists on the "denuclearization-first" and increases the level of pressure by sanctions to achieve their purpose in a coercive manner, and even objecting to the "declaration of the end of war,"" Ri said.

rows.source: “Nghọta na mmachibido ga-akputu anyị n’ikpere anyị bụ nrọ efu nke ndị na amaghị anyị.
rows.output: Understanding and restrictions will only make us more humble in our prayers, which is a vain hope of those who do not know us.
rows.reference: "The perception that sanctions can bring us on our knees is a pipe dream of the people who are ignorant about us.

rows.source: Mana nsogbu bụ na ịganihu eme machibido na-emina enweghị ntụkwasị obi anyị.”
rows.output: But the problem is that you are trying to impose a system that lacks trust.
rows.reference: But the problem is that the continued sanctions are deepening our mistrust."

rows.reference: He is of course the daft secret agent who despite his bizarre pretensions to smoothie glamour has got a little bit of Clouseau, a dash of Mr Bean and a dollop of that chap contributing a single note to the Chariots of Fire theme tune at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

rows.source: N’izizi ọ dabere n’onye njem yana nwoke nzuzo mba ụwa Atkinson nke emere na ihe mgbasa ozi Barclaycard TV echefugoro, na-ahapu ọgbaghara n’azụ ya.
rows.output: In the beginning, it was based on the global world traveler Atkinson, who was made famous by the Barclaycard TV advertising campaign, and who left a trail of chaos in his wake.
rows.reference: He's also originally based on the traveller and international man of mystery Atkinson once played in the now forgotten Barclaycard TV ads, leaving chaos in his wake.

rows.source: Enwere otu oge ma ọ bụ abụọ mara mma na JE ọhụrụ a.
rows.output: There are one or two good things in this new JE.
rows.reference: There are one or two nice moments in this latest JE outing.

rows.source: Ọ masịrị m ka Johnny English na-erute nso n’ụgbọ elu ebe oyi uwe agha ndị agba ochie, igwe nkucha were na-akụta n’okpu agha ya.
rows.output: I liked Johnny English getting close to the plane where the old military uniforms, the fan was wrapped around his head.
rows.reference: I loved Johnny English approaching a helicopter while dressed in a medieval suit of armour and the rotor blades briefly clanging against his helmet.

rows.source: Onyinye Atkinson nwere maka ịkpa ọchị a na-ahụ anya pụtara ihie, mana ịkpa ọchị ahụ esighi ike ma mafee oke, tụmadị ihe nkiri ndị ahụ “anaghị akpa ọchị” dịka 007 na Mission Impossible n’onwe ha na-enwekwa ihe ịkpa ọchị n’ime ya ugbu a.
rows.output: Atkinson's gift for slapstick is undeniable, but the slapstick itself is often forced and overdone, and the films "aren't funny" as much as they are "not funny" on their own, and now even the comedy in them is lacking.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.source: Ihe ịkpa ọchị ahụ dịka ọ bụ ụmụaka ka emebere ya karịa ndị okenye, maka mụ onwe m njegheri Johnny English enweghị ihe nchepụta pụrụ iche yana ebumnuche ya dịka ihe nkiri anaghị ekwu okwu nke Atkinson, n’onye nke Bean.
rows.output: The slapstick humor is more childlike than for adults, for my part Johnny English lacks originality and its purpose as a non-verbal comedy film is less than Atkinson's, in whom Bean.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.source: Ebe mgbado ukwu isiokwu ugbu a bụ na Great Britain nọ n’oke nsogbu.
rows.output: The current issue of the high mountains is that Great Britain is in a state of crisis.
rows.reference: The perennially topical premise now is that Great Britain is in serious trouble.

rows.source: Onye nbanye ịntanetị anataghị ikike banyere na netwọk ndị ọrụ nzuzo kachasị dị nzuzo nke Britain, kpughee ndị ọrụ nzuzo niile nọ n’ọrụ, na mgbagwoju anya onye ọrụ nzuzo nọ ọrụ - obere ihe omume maka Kelvin Eldon.
rows.output: The internet user was not authorized to access the most secret network of British secret services, revealing all secret service agents in operation, and confusing the secret agent on duty - a small matter for Kelvin Eldon.
rows.reference: A cyber-hacker has infiltrated Britain's super-secret web network of spies, revealing the identities of all Britain's agents in the field, to the dismay of the agent on duty - a regrettably small role for Kevin Eldon.

rows.source: Ọ bụ nke ikpeazụ maka onye isi ala bụ onye mpako nwere nsogbu, nke enweghịzi nkwado ọchịchị ọ bụla kpamkpam: Emma Thompson nwara ike ya na ime ihe omume a yitebere Teresa-May mana enwekebeghị ihe dị n’akwụkwọ ọ ga-eji rụọ ọrụ.
rows.output: It was the last for a president who was a pompous, arrogant man, who had no political support whatsoever: Emma Thompson tried her best to carry out the task assigned to her by Teresa-May, but she had nothing in her script to work with.
rows.reference: It's the last straw for a prime minister who is a pompous and embattled figure, already suffering a complete meltdown of political unpopularity: Emma Thompson does her very best with this quasi-Teresa-May character but there's nothing much in the script to work with.

rows.source: Ndị na-enye ya ndụmọdụ nchekwa gwara ya na ebe amagoro ndị ọrụ nzuzo ya niile, ọ ga-akpọpụta onye lagoro ezumike nka.
rows.output: The security advisers told her that as long as all of her secret employees were safe, she could call back the retired employee.
rows.reference: Her intelligence advisers inform her that as every single active spy has been compromised, she will have to bring someone out of retirement.

rows.source: Nke ahụ pụtara Johnny English na-emegheri emegheri n’onwe ya, onye nke ewere n’ọrụ dịka onye nkuzi n’ụlọ akwụkwọ ndị ọgaranya, mana na-enye nkuzi nke adịghị n’akwụkwọ ka-esi a bụ onye ọrụ nzuzo: ọmalịcha odide ebe a, dịka English nyere ụdị ụlọ akwụkwọ nzuzo School of Rock.
rows.output: That means Johnny English is redefining himself, a man who took on the role of a teacher at a prestigious school, but who gives lessons that are not in the syllabus as he is a secret agent: a smooth operator here, as English gave the type of secret school the School of Rock.
rows.reference: And that means bumbling Johnny English himself, now employed as a schoolmaster in some posh establishment, but giving off-the-record lessons in how to be an undercover operative: some nice gags here, as English offers a School of Rock-type academy of spying.

rows.source: Ebughachiri English na Whitehall maka inye ntuziaka ntụmadị were zukọta yana onye nke abụọ ya tagbugoro onwe ya n’ahụhụ Bough, bụ Ben Miller mere ya ọzọ.
rows.output: The English returned to Whitehall to give instructions for the collection of the second levy, and the second of its leaders, Ben Miller, was captured by Bough.
rows.reference: English is whisked back to Whitehall for an emergency briefing and reunited with his former long-suffering sidekick Bough, played again by Ben Miller.

rows.output: Bough was married, attached to a naval officer, a role played by the actress Vicki Pepperdine.
rows.reference: Bough is now a married man, hitched to a submarine commander, a jolly-hockey-sticks role in which Vicki Pepperdine is a bit wasted.

rows.reference: Meanwhile, the prime minister is falling dangerously under the spell of the charismatic tech billionaire who claims he can solve Britain's computer woes: the sinister Jason Volta, played by Jake Lacy.

rows.output: The English and Bough embarked on a journey of absurd games: they transformed into waiters, they ignited a fire in a French restaurant; they brought a brawl into a Volta boat; the English caused confusion as he tried to use a Virtual Reality head set to cook in the Volta kitchen.
rows.reference: English and Bough begin their odyssey of farcical high-jinks: disguised as waiters, they set fire to a flash French restaurant; they create mayhem smuggling themselves aboard Volta's luxury yacht; and English triggers pure anarchy as he attempts to use a Virtual Reality headset to familiarise himself with the interior of Volta's house.

rows.source: Eji ihe niile were mee agba nke ikpeazụ ahụ, ma obi uto na egwumegwu niile dị ya, enwere obere TV ụmụaka dị n’ihe niile ahụ.
rows.output: He used everything to make the last box, and there was joy and excitement in all of it, and there was a small children's TV in everything.

rows.output: Like in the other Johnny English movies, I couldn't help but think: can the British actors give Rowan Atkinson a role that would showcase his talent better?
rows.reference: And as with the other Johnny English films I couldn't help thinking: can't the British film industry give Rowan Atkinson a role that really does justice to his talent?

rows.source: Labour na-agọnarị na ha anaghị akpa nkata atụmatụ ka ndị Britain na-arụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu ma nara ụgwọ ọrụ maka ụbọchị ise
rows.output: The Labour Party denies that they are pressuring the British to work four days a week and accept five-day pay

rows.output: The Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, is proposing a change that would see workers in Britain paid for four days of work in five.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn's Labour Party is to consider a radical plan which will see Britons working a four day week - but getting paid for five.

rows.source: Ndị otu a chọrọ ka ndị isi nwe ụlọ ọrụ na-enyefe akụ ha chekwabara n’aka ndị ọrụ siterena mgbanwe artificial intelligence (AI) site na inye ha ụbọchị ụma agaghị arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: This group is demanding that the leaders have companies that transfer the accumulated assets of the company to the workers through artificial intelligence (AI) by giving them a day of paid vacation.
rows.reference: The party reportedly wants company bosses to pass on savings made through the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution to workers by giving them an extra day off.

rows.source: Ọ ga-eme na ndị na-arụ ọrụ ga-erite elele ụbọchị atọ n’izu ụka ma welakwaa otu ụgwọ ọnwa.
rows.output: He will make the workers work for three days in a week and increase their monthly salary.
rows.reference: It would see employees enjoy a three-day weekend - but still take home the same pay.

rows.source: Ndị nzuputa okwu kwuru na echiche a “ga-adaba” na ebumnuche yana atụmatụ akụnụba nke otu a ime ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ.
rows.output: The monitoring group said that this idea "would fit" with the goals and economic plans of the party to make the workers more flexible.
rows.reference: Sources said the idea would 'fit' with the party's economic agenda and plans to tilt the country in favour of workers.

rows.source: Ndị otu Trades Union Congress akwadola ịmalite ụbọchị anọ n’ime izu dịka ụzọ ndị ọrụ ga-esi rite elele na akụnụba na-agbanwe.
rows.output: The Trade Union Congress has approved starting a four-day workweek as a way for workers to cope with the changing economy.
rows.reference: Shifting to a four-day week has been endorsed by the Trades Union Congress as a way for workers to take advantage of the changing economy.

rows.source: Onye senịọ nzuputa okwu nke Labour Party gwara Sunday Times: ‘A na-atu anya ịma ọkwa nyocha amụma tupu ngwucha afọ a.
rows.output: The Labour Party's spokesperson for parliamentary affairs told the Sunday Times: 'We are aiming to make a statement on the policy review before the end of this year.
rows.reference: A senior Labour Party source told The Sunday Times: 'A policy review is expected to be announced before the end of the year.

rows.source: ‘Ọ gaghị eme ozugbo mana ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu bụ ebumnobi ndị otu a dabara n’usoro ihazi akụnụba ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ yana mkpokota ụzọ nrụpụta ihe nke ndị otu ahụ.’
rows.output: 'It won't be immediate, but working four days a week is the goal of this group to align the economy with the workforce and the total production capacity of the group.'
rows.reference: 'It won't happen overnight but a four-day working week is an aspiration that fits in with the party's approach to rebalancing the economy in favour of the worker as well as the party's overall industrial strategy.'

rows.output: The Labour Party will not be the first to endorse this idea, while the Green Party promised to work four days a week during the 2017 election period.

rows.output: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used the Labour Party conference last week to outline his vision for a change in the economy.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.

rows.output: Mr. McDonnell said he decided to return the power to "unknown executives" and "high-value employees" in the consumer goods companies.

rows.output: The shadow chancellor's plan implies that those with a large stake in the water industry may not receive their expected returns, as the Labour government may 'make a mess' of the target for the industry's profits.
rows.reference: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.

rows.source: O kwuputakwara atụmatụ itinye ndị ọrụ na bọdụ ụlọ ọrụ ma mepụta Inclusive Ownership Fund ga-enyefe pesenti 10 n’oke ụlọ ọrụ ndị nkịtị n’aka ndị ọrụ, ndị nwere ike inweta uru isi ego ruru £500.
rows.output: He also announced plans to appoint workers to the board of directors and create an Inclusive Ownership Fund that will distribute 10 percent of the profits of publicly traded companies to workers, who are eligible for a maximum of £500 in share awards.
rows.reference: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.

rows.output: The FBI's investigation into the allegations against Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh has delayed the final vote on his confirmation for at least a week, and raised questions about whether the findings of the agency's inquiry could change the minds of Republican senators who support his nomination.

rows.source: Gịnị bụ Mmemme Global Citizen, na Ọ nwela Ihe Ọ Bụla Ọ Mere Iji Belata Ụbịam?
rows.output: What is the Global Citizen Festival, and Has It Ever Been a Success in Reducing Poverty?
rows.reference: What is the Global Citizen Festival and Has it Done Anything to Decrease Poverty?

rows.source: Satọde nke a New York ga-achịkọba Global Citizen Festival,emume ịgụ egwu a na-eme kwa afọ nke na-enwe ahịrị ndị ama ama na-atụ n’anya nke ukwuu na-eme ihe nkiri, yana ebumnobi dịkwa ịtụnanya; ịkwụsị ụbịam n’ụwa.
rows.output: On Saturday, New York will host the Global Citizen Festival, an annual music festival that features a lineup of world-renowned artists and activists, with a goal to end extreme poverty in the world.
rows.reference: This Saturday New York will host the Global Citizen Festival, an annual music event which has a hugely impressive line-up of stars performing and an equally impressive mission; ending world poverty.

rows.source: Ugbu a n’afọ nke asaa ya, Global Citizen Festival ga-ahụ puku kwụrụ puku mmadụ ga-ezute na Ama Central Park, nke abụghị naanị inweta ọṅụ n’ihe nkiri ndị a dịka Janet Jackson, Cardi B, Shawn Mendes, ma ka ha kwalitekwa mmata ezigbo ebumnuche mmemme ịkwụsị ụbịam na 2030.
rows.output: Now in its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see thousands of people gather at Central Park, not only to enjoy performances by artists like Janet Jackson, Cardi B, Shawn Mendes, but also to raise awareness of the good causes the festival aims to address by 2030.
rows.reference: Now in its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see tens of thousands of people flock to Central Park's Great Lawn to not only enjoy acts such as Janet Jackson, Cardi B and Shawn Mendes, but also to raise awareness for the event's true goal of ending extreme poverty by 2030.

rows.source: Global Citizen Festival nke kwuputara na 2012, bụ alaka nke Global Poverty Project, otu nkwalite amụma mba ụwa nwere olile anya ịkwụsị ụbịam site na ịbawanye ọnụọgụ ndị na-alụso ya ọgụ.
rows.output: The Global Citizen Festival, announced in 2012, is a branch of the Global Poverty Project, a non-profit organization that aims to end extreme poverty by increasing the number of people fighting it.
rows.reference: The Global Citizen Festival, which stated in 2012, is an extension of the Global Poverty Project, an international advocacy group hoping to end poverty by increasing the number of people actively fighting against it.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and the rest of November," said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and chief spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, on Friday, according to the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of the Supreme Court, where Republicans were proceeding with the confirmation of Kavanaugh despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, reported by Mic.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "Excitement and spiritual renewal of the Democratic Party will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: People say that it is high; this is true.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But it can be especially pronounced among women in the absence of a community and among young voters, aged 18 to 29, who are unimpressed by the president and who do not vote regularly.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: The day before Ford's public announcement, the allegations of sexual harassment against the Supreme Court nominee were being investigated by the FBI, and there were concerns that the nominee's confirmation could be jeopardized if Republicans proceeded with the vote.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has become a civil war within the GOP," said Michael Steele, the former chairman of the Republican National Committee, on the first day of the Republican nominating contest, based on NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: "It's not just about the primaries or the general election or even about Kavanaugh's confirmation, but about how the Republicans are handling this and how they are going to make it an issue," Guy Cecil, chairman of Priorities USA, a Democratic group, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: In fact, Americans are as divided as they were on the Ford and Kavanaugh statements, where more than half disagreed with the last one.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A new survey from YouGov shows that 41% of respondents either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Ford, while 35% say they either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: In addition, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh may have said or done something inappropriate during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: Once the flakes fell, the FBI was investigating Ford's allegations, as well as at least one other accusation, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement to the House Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her at a party when she was 17.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez was accused by a nominee to the Supreme Court of showing off his power when they were having a party during their studies at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web Inventor Announces Plan to Launch a New Internet Network to Compete with Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan, Inrupt's groundbreaking technology, is a company that is building on top of Berners-Lee's open-source software, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the freedom to choose where they store their data and information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We're going to do it now," he said of the new building.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to register for the story."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The tool uses Solid technology to give people space to create their own "personal data vaults online" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It can have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music player, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one browser and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about personal data storage on the internet is that it is up to the person who owns the data to choose who will have access to it.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personalization by data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: Inrupt's mission, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together a team, resources, systems, and skills to help make Solid accessible to everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company had only Berners-Lee, Bruce, IBM's storage division, and a group of volunteer coders working on the project.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By the end of this year, global tech manufacturers will be able to create non-invasive devices that they can build and sell on the Inrupt website.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or stop the open web initiative, where the business model is constantly evolving and always in sight.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "the goal of Inrupt is to empower businesses and environments that are conducive to maintaining trust and integrity in the new web that is being built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by inventing the World Wide Web Consortium with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent years, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: During the extraction of Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain as the Inventor and Chairman of the World Wide Web Consortium, Web Foundation, and Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "We are very optimistic about the future of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1
rows.output: Bernard Vann: A memorial service for the WW1 Victoria Cross priest
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.
rows.output: The Church of England has commemorated the only Anglican to win the Victoria Cross during World War One as a soldier in his home country after 100 years.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col Uko Bernard Vann was awarded the Distinguished Service Order on 29 September 1918 for the attack made on Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.
rows.output: However, the unique circumstances of the duel left him with four days to prepare, during which time he was unaware of the soap and water that had been placed in his room, and he was presented with the highest military honors in Britain.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Ụmụ ụmụ ya ndị nwoke abụọ kpughere okwute iji na-eme ncheta ya na ngarube emere na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.
rows.output: His two sons unveiled a stone to commemorate him at a ceremony held in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.
rows.reference: A commemorative stone was unveiled by his two grandsons at a parade in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.source: Otu n’ime nwa nwa ya Michael Vann, kwuru na ọ bụ “ihe nrịbama pụrụ iche nke ukwuu” na a ga-ekpughe okwute ahụ ka afọ gbara 100 kpọmkwem site na mgbe nna ya ochie kpara ike o jiri nweta awọdụ.
rows.output: One of his grandsons, Michael Vann, said it was "a very special symbol" and that the stone would be unveiled exactly 100 years after his great-grandfather's death.
rows.reference: One of his grandsons, Michael Vann, said it was "brilliantly symbolic" the stone would be revealed exactly 100 years on from his grandfather's award-winning feat.

rows.source: Dabere na London Gazette, na 29 Septemba 1918 Lt Col Vann kpọọrọ ndị otu agha ya gafee Canal de Saint-Quentin “n’etiti urukpuru ojii yana n’ime nnukwu ọkụ ọgbụgba sitere na ama yana egbe.”
rows.output: Based on the London Gazette, on 29 September 1918, Lt Col Vann led his troops across the Saint-Quentin Canal "under a black cloud and in the great glare of the burning villages."
rows.reference: According to the London Gazette, on 29 September 1918 Lt Col Vann led his battalion across the Canal de Saint-Quentin "through a very thick fog and under heavy fire from field and machine guns."

rows.source: Ọ mechara gbara ọsọ gbabanye na ndị na-akwa mgbọ ma “kpaa ike ọkpara” duru ahịrị na-aga ihu tupu ọ chụrụ egbe naanị ya were kụpụ mmadụ ndị agha atọ nọpụrụ iche.
rows.output: He finally sprinted into the ranks of the gunners and "charged forward" led the line against the enemy before he alone fired and shot three enemy soldiers.
rows.reference: He later rushed up to the firing line and with the "greatest gallantry" led the line forward before rushing a field-gun single-handed and knocked out three of the detachment.

rows.source: Onye ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe nke Germany gburu Lt Col Vann na 4 Oktoba 1918 - naanị otu ọnwa tupu agha akwụsị.
rows.output: A German sniper killed Lt Col Vann on 4 October 1918 - just one month before the war ended.
rows.reference: Lt Col Vann was killed by a German sniper on 4 October 1918 - just over a month before the war ended.

rows.source: Michael Vann, 72 kwuru na omume nna ya ochie mere “bụ ihe ọ maara na ya agaghị emenwu ma ncha mana ọ bụ ihe na-eme mmadụ obi umeala.”
rows.output: Michael Vann, 72, said his father's old habits were "things he knew he would never do, but they made him feel good."
rows.reference: Michael Vann, 72, said his grandfather's actions were "something that I know that I could never live up to but something which is humbling."

rows.source: Ya na nwanne ya nwoke Dr James Vann tụkwasara ihe ifuru ncheta ka emechara ngarube ahụ, bụ nke Imperial Youth Band Brentwood duru na ya.
rows.output: He and his brother, Dr. James Vann, were entrusted with the care of the memorial garden after the ceremony, which was led by the Imperial Youth Band Brentwood.
rows.reference: He and his brother Dr James Vann also laid a wreath after the parade, which was led by the Brentwood Imperial Youth Band.

rows.source: Michael Vann kwuru na “obi dị ya mma nke ukwuu na nkwanyị ugwu isonye na ngarube ahụ” wee kwukwaa sị na “a na-egosi site na nkwado nke ndị mmadụ kwanyere ike nke dike n’ezie kpara.”
rows.output: Michael Vann said he was "very pleased to be part of the team" and also stated that "it is shown by the support of the people who are worthy of the title of knight."
rows.reference: Michael Vann said he was "feeling very honoured to play a part in the parade" and added "the valour of a genuine hero is being demonstrated by the support that is going to be given by a lot of people."

rows.source: Ndị nkwado MMA mụrụ anya abalị niile iji kiri Bellator 206, kama ha nwetara Peppa Pig
rows.output: My MMA fans stayed up all night to watch Bellator 206, instead they got Peppa Pig.

rows.source: Chegodi nke a, ịmụrụ anya abalị niile ka ikirie Bellator 206 juputara ejuputa, naanị ka agọnarị gị ikiri isi emume.
rows.output: However, you missed the entire event of Bellator 206, just to deny yourself the chance to see the main event.
rows.reference: Imagine this, you have stayed up all night to watch the a packed Bellator 206 only to be denied watching the main event.

rows.source: Akwụkwọ ozi sitere San Jose nwere mgba 13, tinyere isii dị na isi kaadị wee na-egosi ya ka ọ na-eme abalị niile na Uk na Channel 5.
rows.output: A letter from San Jose has 13 charges, including six on the main card and indicating it as making all night on UK and Channel 5.
rows.reference: The bill from San Jose contained 13 fights, including six on the main card and was being shown live through the night in the UK on Channel 5.

rows.source: N’elekere 6 ụtụtụ, ozugbo Gegard Mousasi na Rory MacDonald chọrọ icherịta onwe ha ihu n’ihu, ndị nkiri nọ UK nwere mgbagwoju anya ka nweta ahụ gbanwere bụrụ Peppa Pig.
rows.output: At 6 a.m., just as Gegard Mousasi and Rory MacDonald were about to face off, the audience in the UK were confused as the ring girl became Peppa Pig.
rows.reference: At 6am, just as Gegard Mousasi and Rory MacDonald were preparing to face each other, viewers in the UK were left stunned when the coverage changed to Peppa Pig.

rows.source: Ọ masịghị ụfọdụ ka ha mụchagoro anya abalị ruo isi ụtụtụ tụmadị maka mgba ahụ.
rows.output: Some people prefer to stay up all night and sleep in the morning to avoid the fighting.
rows.reference: Some were unimpressed after they had stayed awake until the early hours especially for the fight.

rows.source: Otu onye nkwado na Twitter kọwara mgbanwe banye n’ihe nkiri ụmụaka ahụ ka “nnukwu njakịrị atọghị ọchị.”
