rows.source: Ala ọmajiji ruru ike 7.5 kpalitere tsunami ma mebie puku kwụrụ puku n’ụlọ.
rows.output: A powerful earthquake with a magnitude of 7.5 triggered a tsunami and caused widespread damage to thousands of homes.
rows.reference: The 7.5-magnitude earthquake triggered a tsunami and has destroyed thousands of homes.

rows.source: Netwọk latrik na nkwukọrịta mebiri emebi, ebe atụrụ anya na ndị nwụrụ anwụ ga-agbago n’ụbọchị ndị na-abịa.
rows.output: The electrical and communication networks have been severely damaged, and we expect that the dead will rise again in the coming days.
rows.reference: Electricity and communication networks are down with death tolls expected to rise in coming days.

rows.source: Ala ọmajiji ahụ dara na obere mpụga etiti Sulawesi nke bụ akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ na ugwu nke isi ala Indonesia, Jakarta.
rows.output: The earthquake struck the small town of Central Sulawesi, which is part of the eastern and northern regions of Indonesia's main island.
rows.reference: The earthquake hit just off central Sulawesi which is northeast of the Indonesian capital, Jakarta.

rows.source: Vidio ndị na agagharị n’ebe mmerịkọta ọhaneze gosiri oge ọ dara.
rows.output: The video of the people who were walking around in a public place showed the moment it fell.
rows.reference: Videos are circulating on social media showing the moment of impact.

rows.source: Ọnụọgụ narị ndị mmadụ kpokọtara maka emume akụkụ osimiri n’obodo nke Palu mgbe tsunami ji iwe daa n’akụkụ mmiri ahu.
rows.output: The number of people gathered for a beach festival in the city of Palu was in the thousands when a tsunami struck the coastline.
rows.reference: Hundreds of people had gathered for a beach festival in the city of Palu when the tsunami smashed on shore.

rows.source: Ndị ọkaikpe etiti obodo na achụ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ maka onye a na enyo enyo maka agha ụjọ mere na NYC
rows.output: A federal jury in New York City has sentenced a man to death for a terror-related murder.
rows.reference: Federal prosecutors seeking rare death penalty for NYC terror attack suspect

rows.source: Ndị ọkaikpe nọ na New York na achọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ maka Sayfullo Saipov, onye a na enyo enyo na agha ụjọ mere na New York nke gburu ndị mmadụ asatọ -- ntaramahụhụ na adịkabeghị nke emebeghị na steeti ahụ maka mpụ etiti obodo ọ bụla kemgbe 1953.
rows.output: The judges in New York are seeking the death penalty for Sayfullo Saipov, who is charged with terrorism in the New York attack that killed eight people - a sentence that has never been carried out in the state for any federal crime since 1953.
rows.reference: Federal prosecutors in New York are seeking the death penalty for Sayfullo Saipov, the suspect in the New York City terror attack that killed eight people -- a rare punishment that hasn't been carried out in the state for a federal crime since 1953.

rows.source: Saipov, 30, eboro ya ebubo ji gwongworo mgbaziri Home Depot wee mee ihe egwu ahụ n’ụzọ anyịnya igwe dị n’ogologo West Highway dị na Lower Manhattan, na ebetu ndị ji ụkwụ aga yana ndị na akwọ anyịnya igwe n’ụzọ ya na Ọkt.
rows.output: Saipov, 30, was charged with driving a Home Depot truck into a crowd in the West Street bike path in Lower Manhattan, injuring pedestrians and cyclists.
rows.reference: Saipov, 30, allegedly used a Home Depot rental truck to carry out an attack on a bike path along the West Side Highway in Lower Manhattan, mowing down pedestrians and cyclist in his path on Oct.

rows.source: Iji gosi ihe kpatara ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ ji dị mma, ndị ọkaikpe ga-egosi na Saipov “kpachara anya” gbuo ndị mmadụ asatọ ma “kpachara anya” merụọ ndị mmadụ nnukwu ahụ, site n’ọkwa nke ebumnuche iji chọọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ, nke Southern District nke New York gbara n’akwụkwọ.
rows.output: To justify the death penalty, judges must show that Saipov was "deliberate" in killing eight people and "deliberate" in injuring many more, from the level of intent to seek the death penalty, which the Southern District of New York imposed in the indictment.
rows.reference: In order to justify a death sentence, prosecutors will have to prove that Saipov "intentionally" killed the eight victims and "intentionally" inflicted serious bodily injury, according to the notice of intent to seek the death penalty, filed in the Southern District of New York.

rows.source: Ebubo abụọ ndị a nwere ike ibu ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ, site n’aka akwụkwọ ụlọ ikpe ahụ.
rows.output: The two charges can carry a death sentence, according to the court.
rows.reference: Both of those counts carry a possibly death sentence, according to the court document.

rows.source: Izu sotechara mbuso agha ahụ, ndị otu ikpe etiti obodo manyere Saipov ebubo ngụ-22 nke gụnyere ebubo asatọ maka igbu mmadụ n’enyemaka nke izu oyi, nke ndị ọkaikpe etiti obodo na ejikarị n’okwu ajọ mpu, yana ebubo nke ihe ike na mmebi nke ụgbọ ala.
rows.output: The next day, the federal court in Brooklyn charged Saipov with 22 counts, including eight counts of terrorism, which are typically reserved for the most serious crimes, as well as charges of destruction of property and use of a destructive device.
rows.reference: Weeks after the attack, a federal grand jury slapped Saipov with a 22-count indictment that included eight charges of murder in aid of racketeering, typically used by federal prosecutors in organized crime cases, and a charge of violence and destruction of motor vehicles.

rows.source: Mbuso agha ahụ chọrọ “nhazi na ntụle echiche dị ọkpụrụkpụ,” ndị ọkaikpe kwuru, na akọwara omume nke Saipov jiri mee ya ka “arụ, jọrọ njọ na mmetọ.”
rows.output: The attack required "careful planning and calculation," the judges said, describing Saipov's actions as "brutal, deliberate and malicious."
rows.reference: The attack required "substantial planning and premeditation," prosecutors said, describing the manner in which Saipov carried it out as "heinous, cruel and depraved."

rows.source: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov butere mmerụ ahụ, mmekpa ahụ, na mbibi maka ezinụlọ na ndị enyi nke Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, na Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," ọkwa nke ebumnuche kwuru.
rows.output: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov caused harm, suffering, and destruction for the families and friends of Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, and Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," the statement said.
rows.reference: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov caused injury, harm, and loss to the families and friends of Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, and Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," the notice of intent states.

rows.source: Mmadụ ise nke ndị ahụ emetụtara bụ ndị njem si Argentina bịara ịlegharị anya.
rows.output: Five of those affected were tourists from Argentina who were sightseeing.
rows.reference: Five of the victims were tourists from Argentina.

rows.source: Ọ bụrụla otu afọ iri kemgbe Southern District nke New York kpere ikpe okwu ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ.
rows.output: It has been over a decade since the Southern District of New York issued a death sentence.
rows.reference: It has been a decade since the Southern District of New York last prosecuted a death penalty case.

rows.source: Onye ahụ eboro ebubo, Khalid Barnes, nwetara amamikpe nke igbu mmadu abụọ na ere ọgwụ ike mana emechara tụọ ya nga ndụ ya niile n’ikpeazụ na Septamba 2009.
rows.output: The man charged, Khalid Barnes, was sentenced to two counts of murder and drug trafficking but was later sentenced to life in prison in September 2009.
rows.reference: The defendant, Khalid Barnes, was convicted of murdering two drug suppliers but was ultimately sentenced to life in prison in September 2009.

rows.source: Oge ikpeazụ emere ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ na okwu etiti obodo nke New York bụ na 1953 maka Julius na Ethel Rosenberg, di na nwunye egburu ka amachara ha ikpe maka ịkpa nkata iji mee ọrụ sabo maka Soviet Union n’oge Cold War afọ abụọ ya gara aga.
rows.output: The last time the death penalty was carried out in the city of New York was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple who were executed after being found guilty of espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War of the previous two decades.
rows.reference: The last time the death penalty was carried out in a New York federal case was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple executed after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years before.

rows.source: Eji oche latrik wee gbuo Rosenberg abụọ ahụ na Juun 19, 1953.
rows.output: The electric chair was used to execute the Rosenbergs on June 19, 1953.
rows.reference: Both Rosenbergs were both put to death by the electric chair on June 19, 1953.

rows.source: Saipov, onye amaala nke Uzbekistan, gosiri enweghị obi mmadụ n’ụbọchị na ọnwa sotere mbuso agha ahụ, nke akwụkwọ ụlọ ikpe gosipụtara.
rows.output: Saipov, a native of Uzbekistan, showed no remorse in the days and weeks following the attack, as court documents indicated.
rows.reference: Saipov, a native of Uzbekistan, demonstrated a lack of remorse in the days and months following the attack, according to court documents.

rows.source: Ọ gwara ndị nyocha na ihe ọ mere dị ya mma, ndị uwe ojii kwuru.
rows.output: He told the investigators that he was doing nothing wrong, the police said.
rows.reference: He stated to investigators that he felt good about what he had done, police said.

rows.source: Saipov gwara ndị ikikere na ihe kpalitere ya ịme mbuso agha ahụ bụ ka ọ lelechara vidio ndị ISIS n’ekwentị ya, nke ebubo ahụ gosiri.
rows.output: Saipov told the judge that the reason for the attack was that he had watched ISIS videos on his phone, as the indictment alleged.
rows.reference: Saipov told authorities he was inspired to carry out the attack after watching ISIS videos on his phone, according to the indictment.

rows.source: Ọ rịọkwara ka o gosipụta ọkọlọtọ ISIS n’ime ụlọ ọgwụ ya, ndị uwe ojii kwuru.
rows.output: He requested to show a video of ISIS in his hospital room, the police said.
rows.reference: He also requested to display the ISIS flag in his hospital room, police said.

rows.source: Ọ rịọla na aka ya dị ọcha n’ebubo ngụ-22 ahụ.
rows.output: He has requested that his hands are clean in the 22nd charge.
rows.reference: He has pleaded not guilty to the 22-count indictment.

rows.source: David Patton, otu n’ime ndị mgbachite etiti obodo maka ọhaneze na anọchite Saipov, kwuru ha nwere “nnukwu mwute” maka mkpebi nke ikpe ahụ.
rows.output: David Patton, one of the mid-level government officials for the open and transparent trial of Saipov, said they were "deeply disappointed" with the court's decision.
rows.reference: David Patton, one of the federal public defenders representing Saipov, said they are "obviously disappointed" with the prosecution's decision.

rows.source: “Anyị chere na mkpebi iji chọọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ kama ịnara arịrịọ ikpe ọmụma maka ndụ niile n’ime nga na enweghị ohere nke nhapụ naanị ga-adọtịkwu ụjọ nke mmemme ndị ahụ maka mmadụ niile emetụtara,” Patton kwuru.
rows.output: “We believed that the decision to seek the death penalty instead of accepting a life sentence without parole for all the crimes would deter more people from committing those crimes against all the individuals affected,” Patton said.
rows.reference: "We think the decision to seek the death penalty rather than accepting a guilty plea to life in prison with no possibility of release will only prolong the trauma of these events for everyone involved," Patton said.

rows.source: Otu mgbachite nke Saipov arịọbuola ndị ọkaikpe ka ha hapụ ịchọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ.
rows.output: Saipov's defense has requested the court to waive the death penalty.
rows.reference: Saipov's defense team had previously asked prosecutors not to seek the death penalty.

rows.source: MP Tory kwuru na ekwesịrị itinye NIGEL FARAGE n’isi nke ụbụbọ Brexit
rows.output: Tory MP said that NIGEL FARAGE should be at the head of the Brexit boat.
rows.reference: Tory MP says NIGEL FARAGE should be put in charge of Brexit negotiations

rows.source: Nigel Farage kwere nkwa “izukọta ndị agha nke igwe mmadụ’ taa n’oge ngagharị iwe n’ọgbakọ Tory.
rows.output: Nigel Farage promised to "assemble an army of the people" today during a protest at the Tory conference.
rows.reference: Nigel Farage vowed to 'mobilise the people's army' today during a protest at the Tory conference.

rows.source: Onye ndu Ukip gara aga kwuru na ndị ndọrọndọrọ kwesịrị ‘ịnweta okpomọkụ’ sitere n’aka ndị Eurosceptics - ebe otu n’ime ndị MP nke Theresa May tụnyere na ọ kwesịrị ị nọ n’isi nke ụbụbọ ahụ dị n’etiti EU.
rows.output: The former leader of Ukip said that politicians should "get a grip" from Eurosceptics - where one of Theresa May's MPs compared himself to the head of the snake in the middle of the EU.
rows.reference: The former Ukip leader said politicians had to 'feel the heat' from Eurosceptics - as one of Theresa May's own MPs suggested he should be in charge of negotiations with the EU.

rows.source: Onye oche azụ Conservative Peter Bone gwara igwe mmadụ nọ na Birmingham na UK “ga-apụgo’ ma ọ bụrụ na Maazị Farage bụ Ọde Akwụkwọ Brexit.
rows.output: Conservative backbench MP Peter Bone told the crowd in Birmingham, UK, that "they would go away" if Mr. Farage was the author of the Brexit book.
rows.reference: Conservative backbencher Peter Bone told the march in Birmingham that the UK 'would have been out' by now if Mr Farage was Brexit Secretary.

rows.source: Mana mgba Nwada May na eche bụ na ijikọtagharị ndị otu ya kewagoro ukwuu bụ ihe pụtara ihie ka ndị na akwado Ịnọrọ Na Tory sonyere ngagharị iwe dị iche na egbochi Brexit n’obodo ahụ.
rows.output: Mrs. May's main concern was that reuniting her divided party was a pipe dream as long as those who support Remain joined the various protests against Brexit in the country.
rows.reference: But the challenge Mrs May faces in reconciling her deeply divided ranks has been underlined by pro-Remain Tories joining a separate protest against Brexit in the city.

rows.source: Onye isi ahụ na enwe nhịahụ idowe atụmatụ nkwekọrịta Chequers ya n’usoro n’etiti mbuso agha sitere n’aka Brexiteers, Remainers na EU.
rows.output: The leader is struggling to keep the Chequers plan in order amid attacks from Brexiteers, Remainers and the EU.
rows.reference: The premier is struggling to keep her Chequers compromise plan on track amid attacks from Brexiteers, Remainers and the EU.

rows.source: Ndị njikọ siri ọnwụ na ọ ga-aga n’ihu ịnwa ịnweta nkwekọrịta yana Brussels na agbanyeghị nkwutọ ahụ - ma manye Eurosceptics na Labour ịhọrọ n’ime ngwungwu ya na ‘ọgbaghara’.
rows.output: The links between the two parties are so strong that they will continue to try to reach an agreement in Brussels, despite the setback - and force Eurosceptics and Labour to choose between its package and 'chaos'.
rows.reference: Allies insisted she will push ahead with trying to strike a deal with Brussels despite the backlash - and force Eurosceptics and Labour to choose between her package and 'chaos'.

rows.source: Maazị Bone gwara otu mgbakọ Leave Means Leave na Solihull na ọ chọrọ ‘itufu Chequers’.
rows.output: Mr Bone told the Leave Means Leave group in Solihull that he wanted 'the destruction of Chequers'.
rows.reference: Mr Bone told the Leave Means Leave rally in Solihull that he wanted to 'chuck Chequers'.

rows.source: Ọ tụnyere na ekwesịrị ịme Maazị Farage onye otu ma nye ya ọrụ maka ụbụbọ dị n’etiti Brussels.
rows.output: In comparison, Mr. Farage should be made a member and given a job in the middle of Brussels.
rows.reference: He suggested Mr Farage should have been made a peer and given responsibility for negotiations with Brussels.

rows.source: ‘Ọ bụrụ na ọ nọ n’isi, anyị kwesịrị ịpụgo ugbu a,’ o kwuru.
rows.output: If he's in the head, we need to get out now,' he said.
rows.reference: 'If he had been in charge, we would have been out by now,' he said.

rows.source: MP Wellingborough ahụ tinyere: ‘M ga-akwụrụ ọtọ maka Brexit mana anyị kwesịrị itufu Chequers.’
rows.output: MP Wellingborough said: 'I will vote for Brexit but we need to ditch Chequers.'
rows.reference: The Wellingborough MP added: 'I will stand up for Brexit but we need to chuck Chequers.'

rows.source: Na ekwupute nkwugide ya maka EU, o kwuru: “Anyị alụghị ọgụ ụwa iji bụrụ ndị nrube isi.
rows.output: In his statement on the EU, he said: "We did not fight the world to become servants.
rows.reference: Setting out his opposition to the EU, he said: 'We didn't fight world wars to be subservient.

rows.source: Anyị chọrọ ịme iwu nke anyị n’obodo anyị.’
rows.output: We want to make our own laws in our own country.
rows.reference: We want to make our own laws in our own country.'

rows.source: Maazị Boone tufuru ntụnye na echiche ọhaneze agbanweela kemgbe ntuli aka 2016: ‘Alo na ndị Britain agbanweela uche ha ma chọọ ịnọrọ abụghị eziokwu ma ncha.’
rows.output: Mr. Boone has lost his deposit and the public mood has shifted since the 2016 election: 'The polls and the British public have changed their minds and want to remain neither true nor clean.'
rows.reference: Mr Bone dismissed suggestions that public opinion had changed since the 2016 vote: 'The idea that the British people have changed their minds and want to remain is completely untrue.'

rows.source: Onye nkwado Brexit nke Tory Andrea Jenkyns nọkwa na mgbakọ ahụ, na agwa ndị nta akụkọ: ‘Naanị ihe m na ekwu: Praịm Minista, gee ndị mmadụ ntị.
rows.output: Conservative Brexit supporter Andrea Jenkyns was also at the meeting, and told reporters: "All I said was: Prime Minister, listen to the people.
rows.reference: Tory Brexiteer Andrea Jenkyns was also at the march, telling reporters: 'I am simply saying: Prime Minister, listen to the people.

rows.source: ‘Ọtụtụ ndị ọhaneze amasịghị Chequers, Ndị Nkwugide agaghị atuli aka maka ya, ndị otu ndọrọndọrọ na ndị mmume anyị amasịghi ya, ndị nke na agagharị n’okporo ụzọ wee hụ na ahọpụtara anyị.
rows.output: Many ordinary people do not like Chequers, the Tory Party and our civil servants do not support it, those who walk the streets and make sure we are chosen.
rows.reference: 'Chequers is unpopular with the general public, the Opposition's not going to vote for it, it's unpopular with our party and our activists who actually pound the streets and get us elected in the first place.

rows.source: Biko hapụ Chequers ma bido ịge ntị.’
rows.output: Please leave Chequers and start listening.’
rows.reference: Please drop Chequers and start listening.'

rows.source: N’ozi atụrụ Nwada May, o kwuru: ‘Ndị praịm minista na edowe ọrụ ha mgbe ha dowere nkwa ha.’
rows.output: In a message to Mrs. May, he said: 'Prime ministers have put their jobs on the line when they have made their promises.'
rows.reference: In a pointed message to Mrs May, she added: 'Prime ministers keep their jobs when they keep their promises.'

rows.source: Maazị Farage gwara ndị mgbakọ ahụ na ndị ndọrọndọrọ kwesịrị “ịnweta okpomọkụ ahụ’ ma ọ bụrụ na ha chọrọ ịgbarapụ mkpebi emere na nhọpụta 2016.
rows.output: Mr. Farage told the lawmakers and politicians that they should "take the heat" if they wanted to reverse the decision made in the 2016 referendum.
rows.reference: Mr Farage told the rally politicians must be made to 'feel the heat' if they were about to betray the decision made in the 2016 referendum.

rows.source: ‘Nke a ugbu a bụ okwu nke ntụkwasị obi n’etiti anyị - ndị mmadụ - yana otu ndị ndọrọndọrọ anyị,’ o kwuru.
rows.output: "This is now a matter of trust between us - the people - and the political parties," he said.
rows.reference: 'This is now about a matter of trust between us - the people - and our political class,' he said.

rows.source: ‘Ha na anwa ịgbarapụ Brexit mana anyị nọ ebe a taa iji gwa ha ‘anyị agaghị ahapụ unu ma unu mee nke ahụ’.’
rows.output: They are trying to reverse Brexit, but we are here today to tell them, 'We will not be left behind if you do that.'
rows.reference: 'They are trying to betray Brexit and we are here today to tell them 'we won't let you get away with doing that'.'

rows.source: N’ozi maka igwe mmadụ mmụọ ha gbalitegoro o tinyere: ‘Achọrọ ka unu mee otu ndị ndọrọndọrọ anyị, ndị nọ n’isi nke ịgbarapụ Brexit, ka ha hụta okpomọkụ ahụ.
rows.output: In a message to the human race, he added: 'We want you to make our politicians, the leaders of the pro-Brexit, to feel the heat.
rows.reference: In a message to the enthusiastic crowd he added: 'I want you to make our political class, who are on the verge of betraying Brexit, feel the heat.

rows.source: ‘Anyị na ezukọta ndị agha igwe mmadụ nke obodo a nyere anyị mmeri na Brexit, anyị agaghị ezu ike ruo mgbe anyị bụrụkwara United Kingdom nke nnwere onwe, na achịkwa onwe ya, nwere ugwu.’
rows.output: 'We are meeting the human army of this nation that gave us the victory in Brexit, we will not rest until we are also a free United Kingdom, independent and self-governing, with our own destiny.'
rows.reference: 'We are mobilising the people's army of this country that gave us victory in Brexit and will never rest until we have become an independent, self-governing, proud United Kingdom.'

rows.source: Otu aka ọzọ, ndị Remainers gara site na Birmingham tupu ha emee mgbakọ nọrọ aka elekere-abụọ n’ama obodo ahụ.
rows.output: Another group of Remainers, who came from Birmingham, held a two-hour sit-in in the city center.
rows.reference: Meanwhile, Remainers marched through Birmingham before holding a two-hour rally in the city centre.

rows.source: Obere mgbakọ nke ndị mmume fere ọkọlọtọ Tory Yana Brexit ka ebidochara otu ahụ n’izu ụka a.
rows.output: A survey of Tory voters found that 70% were in favor of the party's Brexit strategy.
rows.reference: A smattering of activists waved Tories Against Brexit banners after the launch of the group this weekend.

rows.source: Onye otu Labour Lord Adonis kọtọrọ Conservatives maka nsogbu nchedo ha tara ahụhụ ya site na iji ngwa otu ndọrọndọrọ ka ọgbakọ ahụ mepere.
rows.output: The Labour peer Lord Adonis criticized the Conservatives for their security problems, which were caused by using a single-party tool to open the party's website.
rows.reference: Labour peer Lord Adonis mocked the Conservatives for the security issues they suffered with a party app as the conference opened.

rows.source: ‘Enwere ndị mmadụ ndị na agwa anyị na ha nwere sistemụ IT dị njikere yana teknụzụ niile maka Canada gbakwunyere gbakwunyere, maka oke ala na enweghị nsogbu, maka azụmahịa efu na enweghị oke ala na Ireland,’ o tinyere.
rows.output: 'There are people who tell us that they have a ready IT system and all the technology for Canada, including unlimited land, no problems, unlimited business opportunities, and no land shortages in Ireland,' he said.
rows.reference: 'These are the people who tell us they can have the IT systems in place and all of the technology for Canada plus plus, for the frictionless border, for free trade without borders in Ireland,' he added.

rows.source: ‘Ọ bụ nnukwu asị.
rows.output: It's a big lie.
rows.reference: 'It is a complete farce.

rows.source: Ọ nweghị ihe dị ka ezigbo Brexit,’ o tinyere.
rows.output: There is no such thing as a good Brexit, he said.
rows.reference: There isn't such a thing as a good Brexit,' he added.

rows.source: Warren na akwado ‘ịlenyesị anya ike’ maka ịpụta maka onye isi ala
rows.output: Warren advocates for 'blind ambition' for running for president.
rows.reference: Warren plans to take a 'hard look' at running for president

rows.source: U.S. Onye Ọmeiwu Elizabeth Warren kwuru na ọ “ga-elenyesị anya ike maka ịpụta maka onye isi ala” ka ntuli aka Nọvemba gachara.

rows.reference: Medium concentrations in or offshore of Pinellas County have been reported in the past week, low to high concentrations offshore of Hillsborough County, background to high concentrations in Manatee County, background to high concentrations in or offshore of Sarasota County, background to medium concentrations in Charlotte County, background to high concentrations in or offshore of Lee County, and low concentrations in Collier County.

rows.output: We are still experiencing a shortage of healthcare workers in the Pinellas, Manatee, Sarasota, Lee, and Collier counties.
